**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*[Hyphenated line breaks in the block are joined. The Pada has पुरोळाशं (*puroḷāśaṃ*) where the bhāṣya has "ಪುರೋಡಾಶಂ"; kept as supplied.]*

> एष भागः शृंगरहितोऽजोऽश्वेन वाजिना शीघ्रव्यापकेनाश्वेन सह पूष्णः
> पोषकस्याग्नेर्भागो भजनीयो विश्वदेव्यः सर्वदेवार्हः । अग्नेः सर्वदेवात्मकत्वात् तदर्हत्वेन सर्वदेवप्रियत्वं । एवंविधोऽजः पुरः पुरस्तानीयते । प्राप्यते।
> यद्यस्मादेवं क्रियते तस्मात्प्रियं प्रीणयितारं पुरोडाशं पुरस्ताद्घातव्यमेनमजं त्वष्टा सर्वस्कोत्पादको देवः । त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोतीति श्रुतेः । तूर्णव्यापकोऽग्निर्वा । उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुरित्युक्तत्वात् अहोरात्रे इति वारणी इति वेति
> यास्केनारणी बिभ्यतुरित्युक्तत्वात् । नि ८-१५ । अरणिसंबंधोऽग्नेरेवेति गम्यते
> अर्वतारणवताश्वेन सह सौश्रवसाय देवानां शोभनान्ननिमित्तमभि जिन्वति । प्रीतिहेतुकं करोति ॥

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): this hornless goat, Agni's share fit for all gods, is led before the swift horse; Tvaṣṭṛ (or Agni) makes it a pleasing offering.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

विश्वदेव्यः (*viśvadevyaḥ*)—fit to be offered to all the gods; पूष्णः भागः (*pūṣṇaḥ bhāgaḥ*)—assigned to Agni, the nourisher (that which belongs to him); एषः भागः (*eṣaḥ bhāgaḥ*)—this goat; वाजिना (*vājinā*)—swift; अश्वेन (*aśvena*)—with the horse; पुरः (*puraḥ*)—in front; नीयते (*nīyate*)—is led; यत् (*yat*)—therefore; प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—giving pleasure; पुरोळाशं (*puroḷāśaṃ*)—to be offered first; एनं (*enaṃ*)—this goat; त्वष्टा (*tvaṣṭā*)—Tvaṣṭṛ or Agni; अर्वता (*arvatā*)—with the horse; सौश्रवसाय (*sauśravasāya*)—so that it becomes excellent food, and; अभि जिन्वति इत् (*abhi jinvati it*)—makes it be pleasing.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

This goat, fit to be offered to all the gods and belonging to the share of Agni, the nourisher, is led in front together with the swift horse. Therefore Tvaṣṭṛ, together with the horse, makes this goat, which gives pleasure and is to be offered first, be excellent food and pleasing.

**Printed English translation**

This goat, the portion of Pushan, fit for all the gods, is brought first with the fleet courser, so that Twashtri may prepare him along with the horse, as an acceptable preliminary offering for the (sacrifical) [sic] food.

### Printed p. 159

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೭. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 159 (as supplied).* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 3.)

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

In stating the rule by which, in the Aśvamedha, the goat in the form of the puroḍāśa is made dear to the gods, there is an epithet "viśvadevyaḥ" for this food in the form of a goat. In this context an objection arises, and the answer to it is as follows.

यत्पाजापत्योऽश्वोऽथ कथाप्यन्याभ्यो देवताभ्यः प्रोक्षतीति सर्वा वै (*yatpājāpatyo 'śvo 'tha kathāpyanyābhyo devatābhyaḥ prokṣatīti sarvā vai*)
देवता अश्वमेधेऽन्वायत्ता यदाह सर्वेभ्यस्त्वा देवेभ्यः प्रोक्षामीति (*devatā aśvamedhe 'nvāyattā yadāha sarvebhyastvā devebhyaḥ prokṣāmīti*)
सर्वा एनास्मिन्देवता अन्वायातयति तस्मादश्वमेधे सर्वा देवता अन्वायत्ताः ॥ (*sarvā enāsmindevatā anvāyātayati tasmādaśvamedhe sarvā devatā anvāyattāḥ ‖*) (ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ. 13-1-2-9) *[abbreviation as printed; the hyphenated line break "ಅನ್ವಾ-ಯತ್ತಾಃ" is joined]*

Since the sacrificial horse belongs chiefly to Prajāpati alone, this whole share of the sacrifice should belong to that deity alone. In such a case, to the question why the horse is sprinkled with reference also to the other deities, the answer is given that, since all the deities are connected with the Aśvamedha, all are addressed. According to that rule, the food in the form of the goat, described in the present ṛk and being in the form of the puroḍāśa, is also "viśvadevya".

पुरोळा (डा)शं-पुरस्ताद्दातव्यं । (*puroḷā (ḍā)śaṃ-purastāddātavyaṃ |*) *[so printed]* "that which is to be offered first".

स ना एभ्यस्तत्पुरोऽदाशयत् । य एभ्यो यज्ञं प्रारोचयत्तस्मात्पुरोदाशः पुरोदाशो ह वै नामैतद्यत्पुरोडाश इति ॥ (*sa nā ebhyastatpuro 'dāśayat | ya ebhyo yajñaṃ prārocayattasmātpurodāśaḥ purodāśo ha vai nāmaitadyatpuroḍāśa iti ‖*) (ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ. 1-6-2-5) *[the hyphenated line break "ಪುರೋ-ದಾಶಃ" is joined]*

The name "puroḍāśa" *[printed "ಪುರೋಡಾರ"]* is given to the preliminary offering that makes the sacrifice attractive and the sacrificial portion palatable. Here the offering of the goat is the one that precedes the offering of the horse. It is the puroḍāśa.

वाजिना, अर्वता (*vājinā, arvatā*)—the two words "vājī" and "arvā" are also read among the names of the horse (Ni. 2-27). When explaining the description of the horse called Dadhikrāḥ, the Nirukta authors, quoting the ṛk

आ दधिक्राः शवसा पंच कृष्टीः सूर‍्य इव ज्योतिषापस्ततान । (*ā dadhikrāḥ śavasā paṃca kṛṣṭīḥ sūrya iva jyotiṣāpastatāna |*)
सहस्रसाः शतसा वाज्यर्वा पृणक्तु मध्वा समिमा वचांसि ॥ (*sahasrasāḥ śatasā vājyarvā pṛṇaktu madhvā samimā vacāṃsi ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-38-10)

have explained वाजी वेजनवान्, अर्वेरणवान् (*vājī vejanavān, arveraṇavān*) as having both speed and movement. But since the root "vī" (ओविजी भयचलनयोः) (*(ovijī bhayacalanayoḥ)*) has both the meaning of fear and the meaning of movement,

### Printed p. 160

*Running head: 160 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨.] (as supplied; "ಆ." printed for "ಅ.").*

one may even say that the horse frightens (its enemies) by its swift gait.

त्वष्टा अभिजिन्वति (*tvaṣṭā abhijinvati*)—when it is said that Tvaṣṭṛ makes it pleasing, that is, makes it be satisfied, Sāyaṇa has first taken it as the god Tvaṣṭṛ, explaining त्वष्टा सर्वस्य उत्पादको देवः (*tvaṣṭā sarvasya utpādako devaḥ*), and afterwards, by तूर्णव्यापकोऽग्निर्वा (*tūrṇavyāpako 'gnirvā*), he has given the word "tvaṣṭṛ" the meaning "spreading quickly and pervading" and made it an epithet of Agni, so that he has said that "tvaṣṭṛ" may also mean Agni. To support this meaning,

अविष्टो वर्धते चारुरासु जिह्मानामूर्ध्वः स्वयशा उपस्थे। (*aviṣṭo vardhate cārurāsu jihmānāmūrdhvaḥ svayaśā upasthe|*)
उभे त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुर्जायमाना त्प्रतीची सिंहं प्रति जोषयेते ॥ (*ubhe tvaṣṭurbibhyaturjāyamānā tpratīcī siṃhaṃ prati joṣayete ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-5)

Sāyaṇa has explained that, having quoted this ṛk, the word "tvaṣṭṛ" is used as a synonym of Agni in the sentence त्वष्टुर्बिभ्यतुः (*tvaṣṭurbibhyatuḥ*). अरणी इति वा (*araṇī iti vā*) (Ni., the number printed "೮. ೧೫") इति यास्केन (*iti yāskena*) बिभ्यतुरित्युक्तत्वात् अरणिसंबंधः अग्नेरेवेति गम्यते । (*bibhyaturityuktatvāt araṇisaṃbaṃdhaḥ agnereveti gamyate |*) Sāyaṇa explains that, in giving the derivation of the word "tvaṣṭṛ", Yāska has also shown a derivation as a synonym of Agni.

जिन्वति—जिन्वतिः प्रीतिकर्मा । (*jinvati—jinvatiḥ prītikarmā |*) The word is used in the sense "cause satisfaction". *[In the supplied text this paragraph is printed twice; the second is kept in kn.md as an italic note.]*

भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः । (*bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-51)

The word is used in a context that indicates the same kind of satisfaction, as in "Parjanya, providing abundance of food, satisfies the earth, and the fires, providing food in the form of oblations, satisfy the gods".

Sū. 5-1-67 and 6-2-106), सौश्रवसाय (*sauśravasāya*) and जिन्वति (*jinvati*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-58), with the accents; it ends with the mark ॥ ೩ ॥.

### Printed p. 162

*Running head: 162 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

यत् (*yat*)—when; मानुषाः (*mānuṣāḥ*)—the priests; हविष्यं (*haviṣyaṃ*)—fit for the oblation (for the offering); देवयानं (*devayānaṃ*)—and that which belongs to the gods (printed "ಆದ್ವ" for "ಆದ"); अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—the horse; ऋतुशः (*ṛtuśaḥ*)—at the times of the sacrifice; त्रिः (*triḥ*)—three times; परि (*pari*)—round (the fire); नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—lead, (make it go round to the right); अत्र (*atra*)—at this time; पूष्णः (*pūṣṇaḥ*)—of Agni, the nourisher; प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*) भागः (*bhāgaḥ*)—which is the first portion; अजः (*ajaḥ*)—the goat; देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods; यज्ञं (*yajñaṃ*)—the sacrifice; प्रतिवेदयन् (*prativedayan*)—announcing; एति (*eti*)—comes as the one going in front.

*[The label of the Bhāvārtha is garbled in the supplied text ("॥ ಭಾನುವಾರ ॥"); the standard label is inserted and the garbled words kept in kn.md as an italic note.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The priests, at the times of the sacrifice, make the horse, which is fit for the oblation and belongs to the gods, go three times round the fire. At that time the goat, which is the first share of Agni, goes in front announcing the sacrifice to the gods.

**Printed English translation**

When the priests at the season (of the ceremony) lead forth the horse, the offering devoted to the gods, thrice round (the sacrificical [sic] fire); then the goat, the portion of Pushan, goes first, announcing the sacrifice to the gods.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

ऋतुशः (*ṛtuśaḥ*)—the word "ṛtu" is here a word for time. "Mānuṣāḥ" is a synonym for priests. Wherever the word "ṛtuśaḥ" is used, the meaning is "at the regular time". In some places Sāyaṇa has explained against the Nirukta. For example:

आयूया धृष्णो अभिगूर्या त्वं नेष्त्रात्सोमं द्रविणोदः पिब ऋतुभिः । (*āyūyā dhṛṣṇo abhigūryā tvaṃ neṣtrātsomaṃ draviṇodaḥ piba ṛtubhiḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-37-3)

in this ṛk, while the Nirukta authors have explained ऋतुभिः (*ṛtubhiḥ*) as "at the right time" (Ni. 8-3), Sāyaṇa has explained this word as "with the priests" *[printed "ಸಂಜ್ಞ ಕೈಃ ಸಹ"]*.

यत्वाकत्रा मनसा दीनदक्षा न यज्ञस्य मन्वते मर्त्यासः । (*yatvākatrā manasā dīnadakṣā na yajñasya manvate martyāsaḥ |*)
अग्निष्टद्भोता क्रतुविद्विजानन्यजिष्ठो देना ऋतुशो यजाति । (*agniṣṭadbhotā kratuvidvijānanyajiṣṭho denā ṛtuśo yajāti |*) (ಋ. ಸಂ. 18-2-5) *[reference as printed, "೧೮-೨-೫"]*

### Printed p. 163

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೭. ) ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 163] (as supplied, with a closing round bracket and tabs).* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 4: the Special Topics continue.)

In the ṛk quoted at the end of the previous window, the two words "martyāsaḥ" and "ṛtuśaḥ" are used together. Here "martyāsaḥ" means men, that is, the priests, and "ṛtuśaḥ" means "at the time fit for each one's sacrifice". It should be understood in the same way everywhere. In the present ṛk it means "at the specific times of the Aśvamedha sacrifice", that is, the rite called "paryagnikaraṇa", in which the animal that is the offering is made to go three times around the fire before the oblation is offered to the gods. It must be understood here as "at the time of doing this". The same description is in

कृष्णग्रीवमाग्नेयग्ं रराटे पुरस्तात् । पूर्वाग्निमेव तं कुरुते ॥ (*kṛṣṇagrīvamāgneyagṃ rarāṭe purastāt | pūrvāgnimeva taṃ kurute ‖*) (ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ. 13-2-2-3) *[abbreviation as printed]*

and it indicates that the goat with a black neck, ready for the offering to the fire, goes around the fire in front of the horse, and that the goat too, in front of the horse, making the circumambulation of the fire, announces to the gods that the sacrifice is being accomplished.

पूष्णः पूषन् (*pūṣṇaḥ pūṣan*) is here a synonym of Agni. It is also the well-known name of one of the twelve Ādityas. In both meanings there is one and the same derivation. By this derivation one can take it to mean either Agni or Āditya. Here Agni

प्रूषा यद्रश्मिपोषं पुष्यति तत् प्रूषा भवति । (*prūṣā yadraśmipoṣaṃ puṣyati tat prūṣā bhavati |*) (ನಿ. 12-16) *[so printed, "ಪ್ರೂಷಾ" and "ರತ್ನಿಗಳಿಂದ" in the Kannada for "ಪೂಷಾ" and "ರಶ್ಮಿಗಳಿಂದ"]*

is the derivation of the Nirukta authors: he is called "Pūṣan" because he nourishes with rays. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too,

इयं वै पूषा पूषेयं हीदं सर्वं पुष्यति यदिदं किंच ॥ (*iyaṃ vai pūṣā pūṣeyaṃ hīdaṃ sarvaṃ puṣyati yadidaṃ kiṃca ‖*) (ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ. 14-4-2-25)

it is said that this deity is called "Pūṣan" because he nourishes everything. This kind of meaning can apply to Āditya, or, since Agni, as the carrier of the oblations, is the cause of the nourishment of all, gods, men and the rest, it can apply to Agni; or, if one takes it that Āditya himself is one of the transformations of Agni, there is no difficulty at all. The same meaning is indicated by

पुष्यन् क्षितिं पोषयति प्रणुदन् रश्मिभिस्तमः । (*puṣyan kṣitiṃ poṣayati praṇudan raśmibhistamaḥ |*)
तेनैनमस्तौत्पोषेति भरद्वाजस्तु पंचभिः ॥ (*tenainamastautpoṣeti bharadvājastu paṃcabhiḥ ‖*) (ಬೃ. ವೇ. 2-6-3) *[abbreviation "ಬೃ. ವೇ." as printed]*

the sentence of the Bṛhaddevatā that the name "Pūṣan" is given because, destroying darkness, he nourishes the earth so that it grows. Moreover,

### Printed p. 164

*Running head: 164 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

त्वं वात्यैररुण्यर्यासि शंगयस्त्वं पूषा विधतः पासि नु त्मना । (*tvaṃ vātyairaruṇyaryāsi śaṃgayastvaṃ pūṣā vidhataḥ pāsi nu tmanā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-6)

त्वमग्ने द्रविणोदा आरंकृते त्वं देवः सविता रत्नधा असि ॥ (*tvamagne draviṇodā āraṃkṛte tvaṃ devaḥ savitā ratnadhā asi ‖*)
त्वं भगो नृपते वस्व ईशिषे त्वं पायुर्दमे यस्तेऽविधत् ॥ (*tvaṃ bhago nṛpate vasva īśiṣe tvaṃ pāyurdame yaste 'vidhat ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-7)

In ṛks of this kind the identity of Agni with Pūṣan, Bhaga, Savitṛ and others is stated; so the twelve Ādityas are transformations of Agni. Therefore here too, in accordance with the Nirukta derivation, the meaning is Agni. Or,

अजा अन्यस्य वह्नयो हरी अन्यस्य संस्कृता । ताभ्यां वृत्राणि जिघ्नते ॥ (*ajā anyasya vahnayo harī anyasya saṃskṛtā | tābhyāṃ vṛtrāṇi jighnate ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-57-3)

since the goat is a dear oblation of Pūṣan, there is also an opinion that the goat to be offered here may be meant for the well-known god Pūṣan himself.

**Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)**

*Note (the Sanskrit grammar is only transcribed, not explained):* the Kannada analyses हविष्यम् (*haviṣyam*) (the number of the sūtra is split over two lines), ऋतुशः (*ṛtuśaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-43), देवयानम् (*devayānam*), त्रि: (*tri:*) (Pā. Sū. 5-4-18), नयंति (*nayaṃti*), अत्रा (*atrā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133) and प्रतिवेदयन् (*prativedayan*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-86), with the accents; it ends with the mark ॥ ೪ ॥. *[A stray line ":-0:-" follows in the supplied text; kept in kn.md as an italic note.]*

#### Ṛk 5

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> होता॑ध्व॒युर्राव॑या अग्निमिं॒धो ग्रा॑वग्रा॒भ उ॒त शंस्ता॒॑
> सुवि॑प्रः ।
> तेन॑ य॒ज्ञेन॒ स्व॑रंकृतेन॒ स्वि॑ष्टेन व॒क्षणा॒ आ पृ॑णध्वं ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> होता । अध्वर्युः । आवयाः । अग्निं इंधः । ग्रावग्राभः । उत । शंस्ता ।
> सुविप्रः ।
> तेन । यज्ञेन । सुअरंकृतेन । सुइष्टेन । वक्षणाः । आ । पृणध्वं ॥ ५ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*[Hyphenated line breaks in the block are joined.]*

> होता देवानामाह्वातैतन्नामक ऋत्विक् अध्वर्युरध्वरयुरध्वरस्य नेता
> सोऽप्यावया अभिमुख्येन हविषां गमयिता । अध्वर्योर्विशेषणमेतत् ॥ आज्पूर्वाद्वैतेरसुन् । पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं च ॥ यद्वा । अभिमुख्येनावयष्टा
> प्रतिप्रस्थातोच्यते ॥ अवे यजः । पा ३-२-७२ । इति ण्णिन्। अनाप्योरुपसर्गयोरित्यल्लोपः ॥ अग्निमिंधोऽग्नीत् ॥ भ्राषाग्नोरिंधे । पा. ६-३-७०-६ । इति मुम् ॥
> ग्रावग्राभः । ग्राव्वः स्तुत्या गृह्णातीति ग्रावस्तुत् ॥ कर्मण्यण् ॥ उतापि च शंस्ता
> प्रशास्ता । सुविप्र इति मेधाविनाम । शोभनमेधोपेतो ब्रह्मोच्यते । ब्रह्मा
> तो वदति जातविद्यामित्यत्र ब्रह्मैको जाते जाते विद्यां वदति ब्रह्मा सर्वविद्यः
> सर्वं वेदितुमर्हति । नि. १-८ । इत्युक्तत्वादब्रह्मैव सुविप्रशब्देनाभिधेयः । स
> चानुक्तर्त्विगुपलक्षकः ! एते सर्वे तेन प्रसिद्धेन स्वरंकृतेन सुष्करणीयं कृतेन
> स्वलंकृतेन पोच्चारसौष्ठवादिना सुष्टु संपादितेन स्विष्टेन सुष्टिष्टेन यज्ञेन
> वक्षणा अभितो धृतकुल्यादीन् प्रवहणस्वभावाः प्रसिद्दा नदीर्वा पृणध्वं । सर्वतः
> पूरयत । यज्ञं सम्यग्निर्वर्त फलं साधयतेत्यर्थः ॥

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): the hotṛ, adhvaryu, agnīdh, grāvastut, śaṃstṛ and Brahman, with this well-done sacrifice, fully accomplish its fruit (or fill the streams).]*

### Printed p. 166

*Running head: 166 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied; "ಆ." printed for "ಅ."). (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 5.)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

होता (*hotā*)—the hotṛ who invokes the gods; ग्रावग्राभः (*grāvagrābhaḥ*)—the priest who praises the stones called grāvan that crush *[printed "ಜಜ್ವಿಸುವ"]* the Soma plant; आवयाः (*āvayāḥ*)—the one who offers oblations to the fire, facing it; अग्निमिंधः (*agnimiṃdhaḥ*)—the priest called Āgnīdhra, who makes the fire blaze; अध्वर्युः (*adhvaryuḥ*)—the priest called adhvaryu; उत (*uta*)—and; शंस्ता (*śaṃstā*)—the praśāstṛ *[printed "ಪ್ರಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ"]*; सुविप्रः (*suvipraḥ*)—the intelligent Brahman; तेन (*tena*)—by that well-known; स्वरंकृतेन (*svaraṃkṛtena*)—excellently adorned; स्विष्टेन (*sviṣṭena*)—well offered *[printed "ತ್ಯರ್ಪಣೆ"]*; यज्ञेन (*yajñena*)—by the sacrifice; वक्षणा (*vakṣaṇā*)—the flowing streams of ghee and the like; आ पृणध्वं (*ā pṛṇadhvaṃ*)—may they make them full and overflowing all round *[printed "ತುಂಬಿದರಿಯುವಂತೆ"]*.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the hotṛ who invokes the gods, the priest who praises the stones that crush the Soma plant and who offers the oblations to the fire facing it, the priest called adhvaryu, who makes the fire blaze, and also the praśāstṛ and the intelligent Brahman, with the well-known, excellently adorned and well-offered sacrifice, make the streams of ghee and the like that flow from it full and overflowing all round.

**Printed English translation**

The innoker [sic] of the gods, the minister of the rite, the offerer of the oblation, the kindler of the fire, the bruiser of the Soma plant, the director of the ceremony, the sage (superintendent of the whole); do you replenish the rivers by this well-ordered, well conducted, sacrifice.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

This describes the nature of the fruit of the sacrifice. But it also tells of the knowledge of duty that is the means to the fruit described here. It is said that, if the hotṛ and the others perform their duties without omission, the fruit is assured.

होता (*hotā*)—among the four chief priests he is the one who recites the ṛg-mantras and gives the invitation to the gods. His duty is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in this way:

तदाहुर्यदन्यो जुहोत्यथ योऽनु चाह यजति च कस्मात्तं होतेत्याचक्षत इति । यद्वाव स तत्र यथाभाजनं देवता अमुमावहामुमावहेत्यावाहयति तदेव होतुर्होतृत्वं होता भवति ॥ होतेत्येन (*tadāhuryadanyo juhotyatha yo 'nu cāha yajati ca kasmāttaṃ hotetyācakṣata iti | yadvāva sa tatra yathābhājanaṃ devatā amumāvahāmumāvahetyāvāhayati tadeva hoturhotṛtvaṃ hotā bhavati ‖ hotetyena*)
माचक्षते य एवं वेद । (*mācakṣate ya evaṃ veda |*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 1-2) *[the hyphenated line breaks "ಹೋತೇತ್ಯಾ-ಚಕ್ಷತ" and "ಅಮುಮಾವಹೇ-ತ್ಯಾವಾಹಯತಿ" are joined; "ಹೋತೇತ್ಯೇನ|ಮಾಚಕ್ಷತೇ" is split over two lines without a hyphen and is quoted in two parts]*

### Printed p. 167

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೭ ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 167 (as supplied).*

If it is asked why the one who recites the anuvākya and yājyā mantras is called "hotṛ": he gives the gods an invitation in the form of a mantra and directs them to come and sit in their places. From "āvaha" (that is, bring near) the name "hotṛ" has arisen. One who knows the nature of the gods and has the knowledge of the mantras that give the proper invitation to each god is called "hotṛ".

ग्रावग्राभः—ग्राव्णः स्तुत्या गृह्णातीति ग्रावस्तुत् । (*grāvagrābhaḥ—grāvṇaḥ stutyā gṛhṇātīti grāvastut |*) Maitrāvaruṇa, Acchāvāka and Grāvastut: he is one of these three priests who are the helpers of the hotṛ.

प्रैते वदंतु प्र वयं वदाम ग्रावभ्यो वाचं वदता वदद्भ्यः । (*praite vadaṃtu pra vayaṃ vadāma grāvabhyo vācaṃ vadatā vadadbhyaḥ |*)
यदद्रयः पर्वताः साकमाशवः श्लोकं घोषं भरथेंद्राय सोमिनः ॥ (*yadadrayaḥ parvatāḥ sākamāśavaḥ ślokaṃ ghoṣaṃ bharatheṃdrāya sominaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-94-1)

the sūkta that begins with this ṛk *[printed "ಹಕ್ಕಿನಿಂದ"]*, and

आ व ऋंजस ऊर्जां व्युष्टिष्टिंद्रं मरुतो रोदसी अनक्तन ॥ (*ā va ṛṃjasa ūrjāṃ vyuṣṭiṣṭiṃdraṃ maruto rodasī anaktana ‖*)
उभे यथा नो अहनी सचाभुवा सदः सदो वरिवस्यात उद्भिदा ॥ (*ubhe yathā no ahanī sacābhuvā sadaḥ sado varivasyāta udbhidā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-76-1)

the sūkta that begins with this verse *[printed "ಮುಕ್ಕಿನಿಂದ"]*, and

प्र वो ग्रावाणः सविता देवः सुवतु धर्मणा । धूर्षु युज्यध्वं सुनुत ॥ (*pra vo grāvāṇaḥ savitā devaḥ suvatu dharmaṇā | dhūrṣu yujyadhvaṃ sunuta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-175-1)

the sūkta that begins with this ṛk, are recited at the time of the midday pressing; thus they show his duty as the priest who helps in pressing out the Soma juice.

A situation that explains the necessity of this grāvastut and his duty is told in the form of a story in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

देवा ह वै सर्वचरौ सत्रं निषेदस्ते ह पाप्मानं नापजघ्निरे तान्होवाचार्बुदः काद्रवेयः सर्प ऋषिर्मंत्रकृदेका वै वो होत्राकृता तां (*devā ha vai sarvacarau satraṃ niṣedaste ha pāpmānaṃ nāpajaghnire tānhovācārbudaḥ kādraveyaḥ sarpa ṛṣirmaṃtrakṛdekā vai vo hotrākṛtā tāṃ*)
वोऽहं करवाण्यथ पाप्मानमपहनिष्यध्व इति ते ह तथेत्यूचुस्तेषां ह (*vo 'haṃ karavāṇyatha pāpmānamapahaniṣyadhva iti te ha tathetyūcusteṣāṃ ha*)
स्म स मध्यंदिने मध्यंदिन एवोपोदासर्पद्ग्राव्णोऽभिष्टौति । तस्मान्मध्यंदिने मध्यंदिन एव ग्राव्नोऽभिष्णुवंति तदनुकृति सह स्म येनोपोदासर्पत्तद्दाप्येतर्ह्यर्बुदोदासर्पणी नाम प्रपदस्ति । (*sma sa madhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina evopodāsarpadgrāvṇo 'bhiṣṭauti | tasmānmadhyaṃdine madhyaṃdina eva grāvno 'bhiṣṇuvaṃti tadanukṛti saha sma yenopodāsarpattaddāpyetarhyarbudodāsarpaṇī nāma prapadasti |*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 6-1) *[the hyphenated line breaks "ತಾನ್ಹೋವಾ-ಚಾರ್ಬುದಃ", "ಮಧ್ಯಂ-ದಿನೇ" and "ಯೇನೋಪೋದಾ-ಸರ್ಪತ್ತ" are joined]*

### Printed p. 168

*Running head: 168 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

The gods once began a sattra called Sarvacaru. Then they could not destroy their fault. Then Arbuda, the son of Kadrū, a mantra-seer and a serpent-seer, came and said: "You have forgotten one chief rite that is to be performed by the hotṛ; I shall perform it for you; then you will be able to destroy your fault." The gods agreed. Arbuda, every time, came exactly at the time of the midday pressing and recited the mantra of pressing at the time of grinding the Soma. (The path by which the serpent king came was named "Arbuda-sarpaṇī".)

तान्ह राजा मदयांचकार ते होचुराशीविषो वै नो राजानमवेक्षते (*tānha rājā madayāṃcakāra te hocurāśīviṣo vai no rājānamavekṣate*)
हंतास्योष्टीषेणाक्ष्यावपिनह्यामेति तथेति तस्य होष्टीषेणाक्ष्यावपिनह्युस्तस्मादुष्टीषमेव पर्यस्य ग्राप्पोऽभिष्णुवंति तदनुकृति।तान्हराजा मद (*haṃtāsyoṣṭīṣeṇākṣyāvapinahyāmeti tatheti tasya hoṣṭīṣeṇākṣyāvapinahyustasmāduṣṭīṣameva paryasya grāppo 'bhiṣṇuvaṃti tadanukṛti|tānharājā mada*)
यामेव चकार ते होचुः स्वेन वै नो मंत्रेण ग्राप्पोऽभिष्णौति हंता (*yāmeva cakāra te hocuḥ svena vai no maṃtreṇa grāppo 'bhiṣṇauti haṃtā*)
स्यान्याभिर्यग्निर्यंत्रमापृणचामेति तथेति तस्य हान्याभिर्यग्निर्मंत्र (*syānyābhiryagniryaṃtramāpṛṇacāmeti tatheti tasya hānyābhiryagnirmaṃtra*)
मापृचुस्ततो दैनान्न मदयांचकार तद्यदस्याभिर्यग्निर्मंत्रमापृं (*māpṛcustato dainānna madayāṃcakāra tadyadasyābhiryagnirmaṃtramāpṛṃ*)
चंति शांत्या एव । ते ह पाप्मानमपजघ्निरे तेषामन्वपहतिं सर्पाः पाप्मानमपजघ्निरे त एतेऽपहतपाप्मानो हित्वा पूर्वां जीर्णां त्वचं नव (*caṃti śāṃtyā eva | te ha pāpmānamapajaghnire teṣāmanvapahatiṃ sarpāḥ pāpmānamapajaghnire ta ete 'pahatapāpmāno hitvā pūrvāṃ jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ nava*)
य्यैव प्रयंति ॥ (*yyaiva prayaṃti ‖*) (इ. बॊ. ६ १ (*i. bò. 6 1*)) *[reference printed so, probably for the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 6-1; several lines begin or end in the middle of a word, "ಮದ|ಯಾಮೇವ", "ಆಪೃಂ|ಚಂತಿ", "ನವ|ಯ್ಯೈವ", the line breaks being printed without hyphens, so the quotation is given line by line; the hyphenated line breaks "ಅಕ್ಷ್ಯಾವಪಿನ-ಹ್ಯುಸ್ತಸ್ಮಾದ್" and "ಪಾಪ್ಮಾ-ನಮಪಜಘ್ನಿರೇ" are joined]*

Then King Soma made the gods drink. Then they said, "A venomous serpent is looking at our king; let us bind its eyes", and they did so. [Therefore, at all times when this praise is generally recited, people bind their eyes, to imitate what the gods did to the serpent.] Then King Soma made them drink. Then they arranged that other mantras too be recited together with the mantras recited by the serpent. When both mantras were mixed and recited together, their sin was removed. This is the origin of the grāvastuti. One who recites it at the times of the midday pressing is named "grāvastut". He is the helper of the hotṛ.

अध्वर्युः— अध्वर्युरध्वरयुरध्वरं युनक्त्यध्वरस्य नेताध्वरं कामयत इति वा । (*adhvaryuḥ— adhvaryuradhvarayuradhvaraṃ yunaktyadhvarasya netādhvaraṃ kāmayata iti vā |*) Because he carries out the sacrifice, or is the leader of the sacrifice, or serves the sacrifice with devotion, the name "adhvaryu" is well known (Ni., the number printed "೧. ೮"). Measuring the sacrificial ground, constructing the altar, preparing the sacrificial vessels, making the fire blaze and the other works favourable to these are what the adhvaryu does *[printed "ಅಧ್ಯಯ್ಯ"]*. While doing these works he must recite the respective mantras.

### Printed p. 169

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩ ನ ೭.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 169 (as supplied; "ನ" printed for "ವ").* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 5: the Special Topics continue.)

आवयाः - अभिमुख्येन हविषां गमयिता अध्वर्योर्विशेषणमेतत् । (*āvayāḥ - abhimukhyena haviṣāṃ gamayitā adhvaryorviśeṣaṇametat |*) He who offers the oblations facing the fire: in one way it is explained as an epithet of the adhvaryu (printed "ಅಧ್ವರುವಿಗೆ"); or, अथवा अभिमुख्येन अवयष्टा । प्रतिप्रस्थाता उच्यते । (*athavā abhimukhyena avayaṣṭā | pratiprasthātā ucyate |*) it is explained in another way that, among the helpers of the adhvaryu, प्रतिप्रस्थातृ, नेष्टृ, उन्नतृ (*pratiprasthātṛ, neṣṭṛ, unnatṛ*), the first, the pratiprasthātṛ, can also be meant. This mantra is also in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (the number is printed "೪. ೬. ೮"). Explaining it, Keith says about this word as follows:

"The origin of आवयाः (*āvayāḥ*) is uncertain. The tradition here of the पद (*pada*) derives it from अवयाः (*avayāḥ*) *[the hyphenated line break "ಅ-ವಯಾಃ" is joined]* but यज् (*yaj*) or या (*yā*) have also been in the last part, what priest of the later ritual is meant is uncertain." *[Taittiriya Sampita [sic] I Vol. H [sic], O. S. P. 378: the source line is printed so, without the closing bracket; the English sentence is kept as supplied, with the Sanskrit words in Kannada letters as printed.]*

As explained by Sāyaṇa in his second alternative, it must be the pratiprasthātṛ.

अग्निमिंधः (*agnimiṃdhaḥ*)—since the one who makes the fire blaze is the adhvaryu, this too must be an epithet of the adhvaryu.

शंस्ता (*śaṃstā*)—"śaṃstā" means the priest called praśāstṛ *[printed "ಪ್ರಶಾಸ್ತ"]*.

सुविप्रः— विप्र इति मेधाविनाम । शोभनमेधोपेतो ब्रह्मोच्यते । (*suvipraḥ— vipra iti medhāvināma | śobhanamedhopeto brahmocyate |*) Sāyaṇa explains that it is a synonym of the priest called Brahman, who has an excellent intellect, and, quoting the ṛk

ऋचां त्वः पोषमास्ते पुपुष्वान् गायत्रं त्वो गायति शक्वरीषु । (*ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣamāste pupuṣvān gāyatraṃ tvo gāyati śakvarīṣu |*)
ब्रह्मा त्वो वदति जातविद्यां यज्ञस्य मात्रां वि मिमीत उ त्वः ॥ (*brahmā tvo vadati jātavidyāṃ yajñasya mātrāṃ vi mimīta u tvaḥ ‖*) (ಋ. ಸಂ. 10. 71-11) *[reference as printed, "೧೦. ೭೧-೧೧"]*

he has explained, with ब्रह्मैको जाते जाते विद्यां वदति ब्रह्मा सर्वविद्यः सर्वं (*brahmaiko jāte jāte vidyāṃ vadati brahmā sarvavidyaḥ sarvaṃ*) वेदितुमर्हति । (*veditumarhati |*): Brahman expounds all the śāstras; he is omniscient, supreme in knowledge, and so on; on the basis of this Nirukta sentence (the number is printed "೧. ೮"), Sāyaṇa has explained "suvipraḥ" as Brahman.

वक्षणा (*vakṣaṇā*)—this word is read among the names of rivers (the number is printed "೨. ೨೪"); here it means the flow of ghee and the like, flowing like a river; that is, the meaning is: carry the sacrifice out completely and obtain its full fruit.

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**

> यू॒प॒व्र॒स्का उ॒त ये यू॑पवा॒हाश्च॒षालं॒ ये अ॑श्वयू॒पाय॒ तक्ष॑ति ।
> ये चार्व॑ते॒ पच॑नं सं॒भरं॑त्यु॒तो तेषा॑म॒भिगू॑र्तिर्न
> इन्वतु ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यूपव्रस्काः । उत । ये । यूपवाहाः । चषालं । ये । अश्वयूपाय ।
> तक्षति ।
> ये । च । अर्वते । पचनं । संभरंति । उतो इति । तेषां । अभिगूर्तिः ।
> नः । इन्वतु ॥ ६ ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> यूपप्रस्का यूपार्हवृक्षस्य व्रश्चनकर्तारश्वेत्तारः । उत ये च यूपवाहाश्चिन्नस्य वोढारः । ये च चषालं । यूपस्योपरिस्थाप्यं यूपाग्रभागं चषालमाहुः । तद्येऽश्व यूपाय बंधनयूपाय तक्षति ॥ तक्षतीति वचनव्यत्ययः ॥ साधु
> संपादयंति । ये चार्वतेऽरणवतेऽश्वाय पचनं पाकसाधनं काष्ठभांडादिकं
> संभरंति । उतो अपि च नोऽस्मत्संबंधिनां तेषामृत्तिजामभिगूर्तिः संकल्पः
> सर्वथा करणीयमिति बुद्धिरिन्वतु । व्याप्पोतु ॥ इन्वतिव्याप्तिवचनः इन्वति ननक्षेति
> तद्वचनेषु पाठात् ॥ यद्वा । तेषामभिगूर्तिर्नोऽस्मानिन्वतु । यागं साधुपारं
> प्रापय्य फलेन योजयत्वित्यर्थः ॥

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): woodcutters, carriers, makers of the post's ring and gatherers of the horse's cooking-vessels: may their resolve reach and bless us.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ये (*ye*)—who; यूपव्रस्काः (*yūpavraskāḥ*)—cut the tree suitable for the sacrificial post; उत (*uta*)—and; (ये (*ye*)—who) यूपवाहाः (*yūpavāhāḥ*)—carry the (cut) tree for the post; ये (*ye*)—who; अश्वयूपाय (*aśvayūpāya*)—for the post to which the horse is tied; चषालं (*caṣālaṃ*)—the ring *[printed "ಕೊಂಡಿ", a hook or ring]* to be attached to the upper part of the post; तक्षति (*takṣati*)—make (procure); ये (*ye*)—who; आर्वते (*ārvate*)—for the sacrificial horse... *[the supplied text ends here, after "ಯಜ್ಞಾಶ್ವ"; the rest of the Pratipadārtha is in the next window]*

### Printed p. 172

*Running head: 172 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬.] (as supplied: "ಸೂ. ೧೬." for "೧೬೨").* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 6: the Pratipadārtha continues from the previous window.)

**Pratipadārtha (continued)**

...क्कागि । (*kkāgi |*) *[completes "ಯಜ್ಞಾಶ್ವ|ಕ್ಕಾಗಿ", "for the sacrificial horse", cut at the end of the previous window]* पचनं (*pacanaṃ*)—the vessels and the like that are the means of cooking; संभरंति (*saṃbharaṃti*)—procure, (of those who); their अभि (*abhi*)गूर्तिः (*gūrtiḥ*) *[the word is split over two lines]*—faith-filled intelligence (resolve); नः (*naḥ*)—our (and); तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—belonging to them, the priests' (desired aims); इन्वतु (*invatu*)—may it bring to fulfilment.

*[The label of the Bhāvārtha is garbled in the supplied text ("ಭಾಷಾರ್ಥ", printed without a blank line before it); the standard label is inserted and the garbled word kept in kn.md as an italic note.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the faith-filled intelligence of all those who cut the tree suitable for the post, those who then carry that tree, those who prepare the ring or hook to be fixed on the top of that post for tying the horse, and those who make ready the vessels and the like as the means of cooking for the sacrificial horse, bring to fulfilment the desired aims of us and of the priests connected with us.

**Printed English translation**

Whether they be those who cut the (sacrificial) post, or those who bear the post, or those who fasten the rings on the top of the post, to which horse (is bound), or those who prepare the vessels in which the food of the horse is dressed, let the exertions of them all fulfil our expectations.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

तक्षति-तक्षतिः करोटिकर्मा । (*takṣati-takṣatiḥ karoṭikarmā |*) (Ni. 4-19) *[so printed, "ಕರೋಟಿ"]* "Chaṣāla" means: those who make ready and finish the ring on the top for tying the horse to the post.

अभिगूर्ति: (*abhigūrti:*)—this word is explained as "resolve". The good intent to perform the enjoined rites without fail and the devotion to the rite are indicated.

इन्वति— इन्वतिः व्याप्तिकर्मा (*invati— invatiḥ vyāptikarmā*) (Ni. 2-18) यागं साधुपारं प्रापय्य फलेन (*yāgaṃ sādhupāraṃ prāpayya phalena*) योजयत्वित्यर्थः । (*yojayatvityarthaḥ |*) The purport is that the excellent resolve of all of them may bring our desired aims to fulfilment.

ये यूपव्रस्काः उत ये यूपवाहाः (उत) ये अश्वयूपाय चषालं (*ye yūpavraskāḥ uta ye yūpavāhāḥ (uta) ye aśvayūpāya caṣālaṃ*)
तक्षति (*takṣati*)—in this ṛk some acts to be performed before planting the sacrificial post (yūpa-stambha) are described. "Yūpa" means the wooden post planted in the sacrifice for tying the animal. Although the use of the word "yūpa" in the Ṛgveda is not frequent (it occurs only in the ṛks 1-51-14, 1-162-6, 4-33-3 and 5-2-7), the word "vanaspati", which indicates the same meaning, is much used. Therefore this post is always connected with a tree or wood; one can say that it is not connected with metal

### Printed p. 173

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೮. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 173 (as supplied).*

*[so the sentence is split over the page break: "ಲೋಹಸಂಬಂಧ|ವಾದದ್ದಲ್ಲ"]*. When a sacrifice is performed, people on the sacrificer's side go to the forest and cut a tree suitable for the post to the proper shape. Others bring them, carrying them, to the sacrificial ground. Others carve them well and attach at the top a ring or hook for tying the horse. This is what is said in the first half of this ṛk. यूपव्रस्काः (*yūpavraskāḥ*) means those who go to the forest for the post and cut the tree, यूपवाहाः (*yūpavāhāḥ*) those who carry the cut tree from the forest to the sacrificial ground, and ये आश्वयूपाय चषालं तक्षति (*ye āśvayūpāya caṣālaṃ takṣati*) *[so printed, "ಆಶ್ವ"]* those who attach the ring (चषाल (*caṣāla*)) (or hook) at the top of the post to which the horse is tied. They must generally be people who know woodwork: to carve the tree smooth, cut it to the proper measure and fit the ring at the top, they must be skilled in those works. The tree thus prepared is planted upright in the sacrificial ground. In this matter,

ऊर्ध्व ऊ षु ण ऊतये तिष्ठा देवो न सविता । (*ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaye tiṣṭhā devo na savitā |*)
ऊर्ध्वो वाजस्य सनिता यदंजिभिर्वाघद्भिर्विह्वयामहे ॥ (*ūrdhvo vājasya sanitā yadaṃjibhirvāghadbhirvihvayāmahe ‖*)
ऊर्ध्वो नः पाह्यंहसो नि केतुना विश्वं समत्रिणं दह । (*ūrdhvo naḥ pāhyaṃhaso ni ketunā viśvaṃ samatriṇaṃ daha |*)
कृधी न ऊर्ध्वाञ्चरथाय जीवसे विदा देवेषु नो दुवः ॥ (*kṛdhī na ūrdhvāñcarathāya jīvase vidā deveṣu no duvaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-36-14)

in these ṛks the matter of the prayer to the post when it is planted is stated. After the post is planted, they anoint it with ghee and the like (smear it with ghee), adorn it, perform many sanskāras with mantras, and pray to it. This is told in detail in the sūkta आंजंति त्वामध्वरे देव (*āṃjaṃti tvāmadhvare deva*)यंतः (*yaṃtaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-8) *[the word is split over two lines]*. This whole sūkta is the praise of the post.

In the Aśvamedha there is only one post, but in some sacrifices it seems that the custom was to plant many posts in accordance with the number of animals. On this matter the opinion of some Western scholars is:

"Twenty-one posts, of different kinds of wood, each twenty-one cubits long, are to be set up to which the different animals are to be fastened, amounting to three-hundred and forty-nine, besides two hundred and sixty wild animals, making altogether six hundred and nine according to Katyayana ; a similar enumeration occurs in the Ramayana b. i. ch. 12, 13 ; but the text is no warrant for such a multiplication and it would seem as if a single post

### Printed p. 174

*Running head: 174 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

was intended ; when the word occurs uncompounded it is in the singular चषालं ये अश्वयूपाय तक्षति (*caṣālaṃ ye aśvayūpāya takṣati*). चषाल (*caṣāla*) is given in the आमरकोश (*āmarakośa*) and is explained by most of the commentators a wooden ring. or bracalet [sic] on the top of the sacrificial post; some notice also authority for its being an iron ring at the foot of the post." *[English as supplied, with the Sanskrit words in Kannada letters as printed; the hyphenated line break "ಅಶ್ವಯೂ-ಪಾಯ" is joined.]*

Thus it is said. The matter of the post will be explained in detail when the sūkta अजंतित्वा (*ajaṃtitvā*) *[so printed, probably for "ಆಂಜಂತಿ ತ್ವಾ"]* is expounded.

ये च अर्वते पचनं संभरंति (*ye ca arvate pacanaṃ saṃbharaṃti*)—the commentator and others have explained this sentence as people who prepare the equipment needed for cooking food for the horse, that is, vessels and the like. Although this meaning appears from the words of the sentence, it is possible to conjecture that there may be another meaning besides this. The reason for making vessels for cooking the horse's food in a sacrifice is not so strong. It is the opinion of some that probably the vessels needed for cooking the limbs and flesh of the horse when they are offered to the gods may be what is indicated here. Since cooking food in a wooden vessel is not possible, it may be that the making of wooden vessels in which cooked food, or the flesh and other parts of the horse before the offering, are to be placed is what is specified. For to the words of this sūkta, or पचनं संभरंति (*pacanaṃ saṃbharaṃti*),

ये वाजिनं परिपश्यंति पक्वं य ईमाहुः सुरभिर्नर्हरेति । (*ye vājinaṃ paripaśyaṃti pakvaṃ ya īmāhuḥ surabhirnarhareti |*)
ये चार्वतो मांसभीक्षामुपासत उतो तेषामभिगूर्तिन् इन्वतु ॥ (*ye cārvato māṃsabhīkṣāmupāsata uto teṣāmabhigūrtin invatu ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-12)

in this ṛk, since the cooking of the flesh of the horse (the sacrificial animal) is stated, support for this kind of meaning is found. It may also mean collecting and bringing wood and the like (firewood) that are the means of cooking.

तेषां अभिगूर्तिःनः इन्वतु (*teṣāṃ abhigūrtiḥnaḥ invatu*)—for this sentence Sāyaṇa has explained, नोऽस्मत्संबंधिना तेषामृत्विजामभिगूर्तिः संकल्पः सर्वथा करणीयमिति बुद्धिरिन्वतु व्याप्नोतु । यागं साधुपारं प्रापय्य फलेन योजयत्वित्यर्थः (*no 'smatsaṃbaṃdhinā teṣāmṛtvijāmabhigūrtiḥ saṃkalpaḥ sarvathā karaṇīyamiti buddhirinvatu vyāpnotu | yāgaṃ sādhupāraṃ prāpayya phalena yojayatvityarthaḥ*) *[the hyphenated line breaks "ತೇಷಾಮೃ-ತ್ವಿಜಾ" and "ಸಾಧು-ಪಾರಂ" are joined]*—that is, in the matters mentioned above, namely felling the tree for the post, carrying it, carving and fixing it and attaching the ring at the top, and making the vessels for preparing the horse's food, and in the other rites, the explanation is given in such a way that our priests may be favoured as they wish, so that their purpose is accomplished and the fruit of the sacrifice performed reaches us. That is, as Wilson says, "Let the exertions of them all fulfil our expectations": the meaning is that the labour they have taken in these matters may be fruitful and bring us satisfaction.

मन्म (*manma*)—the horse that is worthy of reflection, that is, venerable and the fruit of the sacrifice; सुमत् (*sumat*)—of itself; उप प्रागात् (*upa prāgāt*)—may it approach; अधायि (*adhāyi*)—let it afterwards be held (by me); वीतपृष्ठः (*vītapṛṣṭhaḥ*)—(therefore) this horse with a well-grown back; देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods;

### Printed p. 177

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೮.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 177 (as supplied).*

आशाः (*āśāḥ*)—the desired aims; उप (*upa*)—(to fulfil) may it approach; एनं (*enaṃ*)—that has come for the sacrifice, and; सुबंधुं (*subaṃdhuṃ*)—having an excellent binding, the horse; देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—(of the gods who desired this); पुष्टे (*puṣṭe*)—for the nourishment; चक्रम (*cakrama*) *[so printed in the Pratipadārtha]*—we shall prepare; विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the intelligent priests; ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—the seers with supersensory knowledge; अनुमदंति (*anumadaṃti*)—let them approve (that our rite is excellent) and show satisfaction.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

This horse, the fruit of the sacrifice, has come of itself and has been held by me. Therefore may it approach to fulfil the desired aims of the gods. The horse that has come for the sacrifice, with a well-grown back and an excellent binding, we shall prepare for the nourishment of the gods who desired it. May the intelligent priests and the seers with supersensory knowledge also approve that our rite is excellent, and show satisfaction.

**Printed English translation**

May my desire be of itself accomplished, such as it has been entertained, that the smooth-backed steed should come to (gratify) the expectations of the gods: we have made him well-secured for the nutriment of the gods; let the wise saints now rejoice. *[the line-end hyphenation "entertain-ed" is joined]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

सुमत्—सुमत्स्वयमित्यर्थः (*sumat—sumatsvayamityarthaḥ*) (ನಿ- 6- 22) *[reference as printed, with hyphens for stops]* quoting this sentence of the Nirukta authors, Sāyaṇa has explained this word as "of itself". The purport is that the fruit may come of itself. The word "sumat" has not only the meaning "svayam", that is, "of its own accord", but also the meanings "auspicious", "beautiful" or "good". This was explained earlier with examples.

मन्म (*manma*)—"mananīya" means "worthy of meditation". Although the literal sense of the word "manma" is "wish of the mind", in the sentences of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā the use of this word is to denote a thing that shows an excellent longing. The Nirukta authors, quoting this same ṛk, have explained the meaning of this word as above (Ni., the number printed "೬. ೨೨"). In this context Durgācārya, explaining the word, explained मन्म-मननी (*manma-mananī*)यमर्थजातं । (*yamarthajātaṃ |*) *[the word is split over two lines]* as an "ādṛta" thing *[so printed, "ಆದೃತ", with the next sentence "ಅದೃತ"]*. The "adṛta" thing may be the fruit of the sacrifice, praise, or an oblation. In the present ṛk it means a fruit that is venerable and worthy of meditation. In sentences such as अग्निः प्रश्नेन मन्मना (*agniḥ praśnena manmanā*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 1. 4, reference as printed with a stop) the superior sense of this word may also be noted. *[A stray signature "(12)" and "Vol. 12]" at the foot of the page is kept in kn.md as italic notes.]*

### Printed p. 180

*Running head: 180 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

**Printed English translation**

May the halter and the heel-ropes of the fleet courser, and the head-ropes, the girths, and any other (part of the harness); and the grass that has been put into the mouth; may all these be with you, (horse), amongst the gods. *[the line-end hyphenation "head-ropes" is printed over two lines]*

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The sacrificer who, by offering the horse as an oblation and performing the sacrifice, wishes to obtain wealth, valour and a good state, wishes that a good state and happiness may be obtained also by the horse, the means of his happiness. By the epithets वाजिनः अर्वतः (*vājinaḥ arvataḥ*) the independent movement of the horse and the speed of its movement are indicated, but दाम ; शीर्षणी, रशना (*dāma ; śīrṣaṇī, raśanā*) *[so printed, "ಶೀರ್ಷಣೀ"]* and the like indicate a bound condition. But the purport is that, although the horse made ready for the Aśvamedha and offered to the gods has these worldly bonds, they remain merely as ornaments and lead the horse among the gods. Here it is also prayed that the same happiness that arises from grazing on grass may continue uninterruptedly *[printed "ಅನುಸ್ಯೂತ"]*.

> यत् । अश्वस्य । क्रविषः । मक्षिका । आश । यत् । वा । स्वरौ । स्वधितौ । रिप्तं । अस्ति ।
> यत् । हस्तयोः । शमितुः । यत् । नखेषु । सर्वा । ता । ते । अपि । देवेषु।अस्तु

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*[The label is garbled in the supplied text ("ಬಾಯಣಧ್ವನಿಃ", inside the Pada block); the standard label is inserted and the garbled words kept in kn.md as an italic note. Hyphenated line breaks in the block are joined.]*

> अश्वस्य तदवयवभूतस्य क्रविष आममांसस्य यत् यदंगं मक्षिकाश अभक्षयत् ॥ अश भोजने ॥ यद्वा ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ अश्वस्य यन्मांसं भक्षयति ।
> वाथवा स्वरौ पश्वंजनकाले यद्रिप्तं लिप्तमस्ति । स्वरुणा पशुमनक्तीति श्रुतेः । अथवा
> स्वधितौ छेदनकाले चावदानकाले यद्रिप्तमस्ति शमितुर्हस्तयोर्लिप्तमस्ति । विशसनकाले यच्च नखेषु लिप्तं । ता सर्वा तानि सर्वाणि हे अश्व ते तव संबंधीनि देवेष्टस्तु । देवेषु संतोषार्थाय भवंतु ॥

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): whatever flesh a fly ate, or stuck to the post, knife, slaughterer's hands and nails: may all be with you among the gods.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

अश्वस्य (*aśvasya*)—of this sacrificial horse; क्रविषः (*kraviṣaḥ*)—full of flesh; यत् (*yat*)—which limb; मक्षिका (*makṣikā*)—the fly; आश (*āśa*)—was eating; वा (*vā*)—or; स्वरौ (*svarau*)—on the stake of slaughter; स्वधितौ (*svadhitau*)—on the knife, the means of cutting; (यत्) रिप्तं अस्ति (*(yat) riptaṃ asti*)—whatever part is stuck on; शमितुः (*śamituḥ*)—of the slaughterer *[printed "ಭೇದಕಾರನ"]*; हस्तयोः (*hastayoḥ*)—on the hands; नखेषु (*nakheṣu*)—and on the nails; यत् (*yat*)—whatever smearing there is; (O horse); ते (*te*)—belonging to you; ता सर्वा (*tā sarvā*)—all that; देवेषु अस्तु (*deveṣu astu*)—may it go to the gods.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O horse, whichever limb of you, the sacrificial horse, full of flesh, a fly ate here, whatever part stuck to the stake of slaughter or to the knife, the means of slaughter *[the supplied text ends here, in the middle of the sentence, after "ಅಂಟಿಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಿತೋ"; the rest of the Bhāvārtha is in the next window]*

### Printed p. 182

*Running head: 182 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨.] (as supplied; "ಆ." printed for "ಅ.").* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 9: the Bhāvārtha continues from the previous window.)

...and whatever part is attached to the hands and nails of the slaughterer: may all of it be offered to the gods.

**Printed English translation**

Whatever the flies may eat of the raw flesh of the horse; whatever (grease) is smeared upon the brush or upon the axe; (what is smeared) upon the hands or the nails of the immolator, may all this be with thee, (horse), among the gods.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

It is the custom to smear anointing paste on the sacrificial post to which the sacrificial horse is tied and on the knife that cuts. It is prayed that the smear of such anointing paste too may go to the gods, for the adornment of the horse.

स्वरौ (*svarau*)—generally "svaru" means the sacrificial post. Just as collyrium is applied to the eye, applying anointing paste to the sacrificial post is an enjoined rite. There is also a usage of calling the "svaru" a chip of the post (yūpa-śakala). For example,

अथ ये तेभ्योऽवर आसंस्त एतं स्वरुमपश्यन्यूपशकलं । (*atha ye tebhyo 'vara āsaṃsta etaṃ svarumapaśyanyūpaśakalaṃ |*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 2-3)

in this, and also in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā in अग्रेगा नेतृणां वनस्पतिः (*agregā netṛṇāṃ vanaspatiḥ*) (1-3-6, reference as printed) it is explained as यूपस्य प्रथमशकलः (*yūpasya prathamaśakalaḥ*). But Sāyaṇa, explaining the sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, has explained प्रथमशकलः; स्वरुः; चषालं (*prathamaśakalaḥ; svaruḥ; caṣālaṃ*) as three different parts of the post. The Bhaṭṭabhāskara commentary also has the same divisions. But Sāyaṇa, in the sentence

अपश्यंध्वरुं यूहस्य संस्थिते सोमे । (*apaśyaṃdhvaruṃ yūhasya saṃsthite some |*) (ತೈ. ಸಂ. 6-3-4) *[abbreviation as printed]*

of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā only, has explained "svaru" as the first chip. There is a contradiction between his earlier explanation and the explanation of this sentence. In the present ṛk Sāyaṇa has explained the word "svar" as पश्वंजनकाले (*paśvaṃjanakāle*).

स्वधितौ—स्वधिति शब्दवु वज्र नामगळल्लि (*svadhitau—svadhiti śabdavu vajra nāmagaḷalli*) *[the Kannada continues: "the word is read among the names of vajra"]* (Ni. 3-11); it means the knife *[printed "ಮಚ್ಚು"]* for slaughtering the animal.

ब्रह्मा देवानां पदवीः कवीनामृषिर्विप्राणां महिषो मृगाणां । (*brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnāmṛṣirviprāṇāṃ mahiṣo mṛgāṇāṃ |*)
शैनो गृध्राणां स्वधितिर्वनानां सोमः पवित्रमत्येति रेभन् ॥ (*śaino gṛdhrāṇāṃ svadhitirvanānāṃ somaḥ pavitramatyeti rebhan ‖*) (ಋ. ಸಂ. 9-96 6) *[reference as printed, without a hyphen between 96 and 6]*

in this, for the word "vanānām" it has been explained हिंसकानां छेदकानां मध्ये स्वधितिः एतन्नामकश्वेद (*hiṃsakānāṃ chedakānāṃ madhye svadhitiḥ etannāmakaśveda*)कोऽसि (*ko 'si*) *[the word is split over two lines]* and, as the meaning "instrument of cutting" is given to this word, the same meaning applies here too. शमितु: (*śamitu:*)—Sāyaṇa has not given a meaning for this word. The one who kills the sacrificial animal is called "śamitṛ". This matter will be discussed in the explanation of the next ṛk.

### Printed p. 184

*Running head: 184 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).* (The Saṃhitā continues.)

> सुकृता तच्छमितारः कृण्वंतूत मेधं शृतपाकं पचंतु॥१०॥

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**

> यत् । ऊवध्यं । उदरस्य । अपवाति । यः । आमस्य । क्रविषः । गंधः । अस्ति ।
> सुकृता । तत् । शमितारः । कृण्वंतु । उत । मेधं । शृतपाकं । पचंतु ॥ १० ॥

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

*[Hyphenated line breaks in the block are joined.]*

> उदरस्य संबंधि यदूवध्यमीषज्जीर्णं तृणं पुरीषमपवाति अपगच्छति ।
> यश्चामस्यापक्वस्य क्रविषो मांसस्य गंधोऽस्ति लेशोऽस्ति । पाकस्य समये यत्किंचिदूवध्यमपक्वस्य च लेशोऽस्ति आमगंधोऽस्ति । तत्सर्वं शमितारो विशसनकर्तारः
> सुकृता कृण्वंतु । सुकृतमुक्तदोषरहितं कुर्वंतु । उतापि च मेधं मेध्यं
> यज्ञार्हं पश्ववयवं शृतपाकं देवयोग्यपाकोपेतं यथा भवति तथा पचंतु ।
> पितृमनुष्यादियोग्यमतिपक्षमीषत्पक्वं च मा कुर्वंतित्यर्थः ॥

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): may the slaughterers make pure the undigested stomach contents and the raw-flesh odour, and cook the sacrificial parts to suit the gods.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

उदरस्य (*udarasya*)—(of this horse) in the belly; यत् (*yat*)—which; ऊवध्यं (*ūvadhyaṃ*)—food not completely digested; अपवाति (*apavāti*)—comes out (at the time of killing); यः (*yaḥ*)—whatever; आमस्य (*āmasya*)—raw; क्रविषः (*kraviṣaḥ*)—of the flesh; गंधः (*gaṃdhaḥ*)—smell; अस्ति (*asti*)—there is; तत् (*tat*)—all that; शमितारः (*śamitāraḥ*)—the slaughterers; सुकृताः (*sukṛtāḥ*)—as free from fault and pure; कृण्वंतु (*kṛṇvaṃtu*)—let them make; उत (*uta*)—and; मेधं (*medhaṃ*)—the part of it fit for the sacrifice; कृतपाकं (*kṛtapākaṃ*) *[so printed]*—so that it has a cooking suitable for the gods; पचंतु (*pacaṃtu*)—let them cook.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

Whatever food, not completely digested, comes out of the belly of this sacrificial horse at the time of killing, and whatever bad smell of raw flesh there is, all that may the slaughterers make free from fault and pure. And the part of it fit for the sacrifice may they cook so that it suits the gods.

### Printed p. 185

*Running head: [ಅ ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೮. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 185 (as supplied).* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 10.)

**Printed English translation**

Whatever undigested grass fall from his belly; whatever particle of raw flesh may remain; let the immolators make the whole free from defect, and so cook the pure (offering) that it may be perfectly dressed.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

ऊवध्यं (*ūvadhyaṃ*)—food that is not completely digested is called "ūvadhya".

ऊवध्यगोहं पार्थिवं खनत । (*ūvadhyagohaṃ pārthivaṃ khanata |*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 2-6)

here it is explained as excrement (puriṣa). It means food that is the remnant of digestion. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, at the time of describing this same sacrificial horse,

ऊवध्यं सिकताः सिंधवो गुदा । (*ūvadhyaṃ sikatāḥ siṃdhavo gudā |*) (ಬೃ. ಉ. 1-1-1)

"sand is the ūvadhya of this sacrificial horse" *[printed "ಮೇಧಾಶ್ವ"]*: Śaṅkarācārya has explained "ūvadhya" as उदरस्थमर्धजीर्णमशनं (*udarasthamardhajīrṇamaśanaṃ*), food in the belly that is half digested.

शमितारः (*śamitāraḥ*)—the "śamitṛ" is the one who kills the sacrificial animal. There are some disagreements about whether he is one of the priests or someone else. Although it appears to be the duty of the adhvaryu, the adhvaryu used to appoint others to assist him in it. Some hold that he is not one of the priests and need not even be a Brahmin.

अध्रिगो शमीध्वं सुशमि शमीध्वं शमीध्वमध्रिगा ३ उ इति तिब्रूयादपापेति (*adhrigo śamīdhvaṃ suśami śamīdhvaṃ śamīdhvamadhrigā 3 u iti tibrūyādapāpeti*)
चाद्रिगुर्वै देवानां शमितापापो निग्रभीता शमितृभ्यश्चैवैनं तन्निग्रभीतृभ्यश्च संप्रयच्छति ॥ (*cādrigurvai devānāṃ śamitāpāpo nigrabhītā śamitṛbhyaścaivainaṃ tannigrabhītṛbhyaśca saṃprayacchati ‖*) (ಐ. ಬ್ರಾ. 2-7) *[the hyphenated line break "ನಿಗ್ರಭೀ-ತೃಭ್ಯಶ್ಚ" is joined]*

"O Adhrigu, kill this animal; kill it completely. Since Adhrigu is the śamitṛ of all the gods, those who utter his name become sinless": thus the hotṛ says and gives the animal into the hand of the śamitṛ.

नैष यजमानेनान्वारभ्यो मृत्यवे ह्येतं नयंति .... .... .... वपाश्रपणीभ्यां (*naiṣa yajamānenānvārabhyo mṛtyave hyetaṃ nayaṃti .... .... .... vapāśrapaṇībhyāṃ*)
प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रतिप्रस्थातारमध्वर्युरध्वर्युं यजमान एतदु परोक्षमन्वारब्धं (*pratiprasthātā pratiprasthātāramadhvaryuradhvaryuṃ yajamāna etadu parokṣamanvārabdhaṃ*)
भवति । (*bhavati |*) (ಶ. ಬ್ರಾ 3-8-1-10) *[abbreviation as printed; the first line has printed dots]*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**

> हे अश्व ते तवाग्नि ना पच्यमानाद्दात्राद्यदूष्मरूपं रसो वा यत्किंचिदवधावति । तथा निहतस्य निःशेषेण हतस्य तव यदंगं रसरूपं शूलमभिलक्ष्यावधावति

*[Gist of the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (my own short summary): may whatever drips from your body while cooking, or slips from the spit, not cling to ground or grass but go to the gods.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

हे अश्व (*he aśva*)—O horse; अग्निना (*agninā*)—by fire; पच्यमानात् (*pacyamānāt*)—being cooked; ते (*te*)—your; गात्रात् (*gātrāt*)—from the body; यत् (*yat*)—whatever part, or juice in liquid form; अवधावति (*avadhāvati*)—spills and flows down, (and); निहतस्य (*nihatasya*)—whatever part of your dead body; शूलमभि (*śūlamabhi*)—slips and falls down from the spit (on which the flesh is pierced and cooked); भूम्यां तत् (*bhūmyāṃ tat*)—that part fallen on the ground; मा आश्रित् (*mā āśrit*) *[so printed]*—let it not cling to the earth (also the part fallen on the spread darbha grass); मा (श्रिषत्) (*mā (śriṣat)*)—let it not cling; (but) तत् (*tat*)—the part thus spilled; उशद्भ्यः (*uśadbhyaḥ*)—who desire the whole oblation; देवेभ्यः (*devebhyaḥ*)—to the gods; रातं अस्तु (*rātaṃ astu*)—let it be as if offered.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

O horse, the juice and other parts that fall down and spill out of the vessel while your dead body is being cooked in the fire, and the part (piece or fragment) that slips and falls from the spit while the flesh is pierced and roasted, whether they fall on the ground or on the spread darbha grass, may they not be wasted but be offered to the gods who love the oblation.

### Printed p. 188

*Running head: 188 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧ ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 11.)

**Printed English translation**

Whatever (portion) of your slaughtered (body) fall from your carcase when it is being roasted by the fire, (escaping) from the spit : let it not be left on the ground, nor on the (sacred) grass, but let it (all) be given to the longing gods.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

The main idea: when the flesh of the sacrificial horse is put, for the offering, into the large vessel like a big cauldron called "ukhā" and is being cooked, a little may boil over and spill out of the vessel. Or, when it is stirred with implements such as a ladle, some portion may fall on the ground. Besides the method of cooking flesh, there is also the roasting of it by piercing a piece of flesh with a long rod (śūla, "spit") and holding it over the fire. When roasting in this way, one or two small pieces may slip from the rod and fall. The seer prays that such pieces of flesh fallen down may not cling to the earth and be wasted but be offered to the gods.

यत्ते गात्रात् (*yatte gātrāt*)—in the ṛk the use of the words "te", "your", addressing the horse, refers to the dead horse; is not this usage contradictory? It is not so. It need not be said that the seer recited this mantra while the horse was being killed and its flesh cooked; it should be understood that, before the killing of the horse, indicating the rite that may take place later, he is addressing the horse.

शूलं (*śūlaṃ*)—a long rod (spit). It is common even now to roast flesh by piercing it with a rod and holding it over the fire. Or, when cooking flesh in a large vessel, a long rod (or ladle) is used to stir it from time to time. In both these situations it is possible that some portion of the flesh may fall on the ground. The seer's intention is that the portion so fallen may not be wasted but be offered to the gods. The word "śūla" occurs in the Ṛgveda only in this ṛk and nowhere else.

तृणेषु—विशसनसमये दर्भेषु मापगच्छतु । (*tṛṇeṣu—viśasanasamaye darbheṣu māpagacchatu |*) May the part that falls on darbha grass when the horse's body is being cut not be wasted. In performing sacrifices and the like it is the custom to invite the gods and to prepare a seat for them to come and sit, by spreading on the ground the darbha grass called "barhis". In the same way it is the practice to place the sacrificial materials too, such as the sacrificial vessels (ghee vessels and the like), the oblation, the food and the puroḍāśa,

### Printed p. 189

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩ ವ. ೯.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 189 (as supplied).*

on darbha spread on the ground. Therefore, when the dead body of the horse is cut, since the body is then on darbha, the blood, flesh and the like that fall fall on the darbha. Or, since here, without a word indicating darbha such as "barhis", तृणेषु (*tṛṇeṣu*) is said, "on grass", and since grass generally grows on the ground, it may also mean the blood and flesh that may fall on grass.

रातं (*rātaṃ*)—the word "rātam", derived from the root "rā dāne", which means "give", means giving, donating or offering.

**Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)**

*Note (the Sanskrit grammar is only transcribed, not explained):* the Kannada analyses गात्रात् (*gātrāt*) (ಉ. ಸೂ. 4-608, abbreviation as printed), पच्यमानात् (*pacyamānāt*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-67, 7-2-82 and 6-1-186), निहतस्य (*nihatasya*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-37 and 6-2-49), अवधावति (*avadhāvati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71), श्रिषत् (*śriṣat*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-175, 3-1-55 and 6-4-74), उशद्भ्यः (*uśadbhyaḥ*) (the number of the Pā. Sū. 6-1-16 is split over two lines) and, on p. 190, रातम् (*rātam*), with the accents; it ends with the mark ॥ ೧೧ ॥.

### Printed p. 191

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. .೯ ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 191 (as supplied, with a stray stop before "೯").* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 12.)

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

ये (*ye*)—who; पक्वं (*pakvaṃ*)—cooking; वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—the parts of the horse (the flesh); परिपश्यंति (*paripaśyaṃti*)—look at with eagerness; ये (*ye*)—who; ईं (*īṃ*)—this horse-flesh that is cooking; सुरभिः (*surabhiḥ*)—fragrant with a good smell, (therefore); निः हर इति (*niḥ hara iti*)—(give) to us also, or, because it is well cooked and fragrant, it must be offered to the gods; आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—say; ये च (*ye ca*)—and who; अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—of the horse that is cooking; मांस (*māṃsa*)भिक्षां (*bhikṣāṃ*) *[the word is split over two lines]*—a small part of the flesh (left over from the oblation); उपासते (*upāsate*)—desire; उतो (*uto*)—and; तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—of these people (or priests); अभिगूर्तिः (*abhigūrtiḥ*)—faith-filled intelligence or request; नः (*naḥ*)—our (desired aims); इन्वतु (*invatu*)—may it bring to fulfilment.

*[The label of the Bhāvārtha is garbled in the supplied text ("ಭಾನಾರ್ಥಿ", printed without a blank line before it); the standard label is inserted and the garbled word kept in kn.md as an italic note.]*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

May the requests of those be fulfilled who look with great eagerness at the limbs and flesh of the horse while they are cooking, and who desire that, because the flesh is well cooked and gives out a good smell, it be taken down from the fire, offered to the gods, and also given to them.

**Printed English translation**

Let their exertions be for our good who watch the cooking of the horse : who say, It is fragrant : therefore give us some : who solicit the flesh of the horse as alms.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

ये वाजिनं परिपश्यंति पक्वं—अश्वावयवं परिपश्यंति परितः पावनबुद्ध्येक्षंते । (*ye vājinaṃ paripaśyaṃti pakvaṃ—aśvāvayavaṃ paripaśyaṃti paritaḥ pāvanabuddhyekṣaṃte |*) *[the hyphenated line break "ಪಾವನಬುದ್ಧ್ಯೇ-ಕ್ಷಂತೇ" is joined]* Those who look at the horse-flesh cooking in the vessel with the good intent that it be offered to the gods. Here "vājinam" means the parts of the horse, or the flesh of the horse, cooking in the vessel. For the horse is not cooked whole; it is cut up, put into the vessel and cooked. The description of this is given in the following ṛks. "Paripaśyanti" means that they stand around the fire and watch with great curiosity how long it will take to cook.

सुरभि (*surabhi*)—after the horse-flesh is well cooked, a good smell indicating that it is cooked comes out; therefore enough cooking, and it must be taken down from the fire: that is the meaning.

निः हर इति (*niḥ hara iti*)—for these words the commentator gives two kinds of meaning, निर्हर किंचिदस्मभ्यं देहीत्याहुः । यद्वा (*nirhara kiṃcidasmabhyaṃ dehītyāhuḥ | yadvā*) यतः सुरभिः अतो देवयोग्यमिति निश्शेषेण देवेभ्यो हरेत्याहुः । (*yataḥ surabhiḥ ato devayogyamiti niśśeṣeṇa devebhyo haretyāhuḥ |*)

### Printed p. 192

*Running head: 192 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied).*

one that some say "give us a little of the cooked flesh", and another that, because it is well cooked and fragrant, it must be offered entirely to the gods. Of these two meanings, the meaning "they say, give us a little" does not seem very appropriate, because in the second half of this very ṛk, which indicates this same idea, ये चार्वतो मांस (*ye cārvato māṃsa*) भिक्षामुपासते (*bhikṣāmupāsate*) *[the word is split over two lines]*, "others desire the cooked horse-flesh for themselves too", is said; so the second meaning, "offer to the gods", fits properly; or, since "surabhiḥ nirhara" is said, another meaning may also be given: "enough, there is no need to cook more; therefore take the vessel down from the fire". This last opinion has been stated by the Yajurveda commentator Mahīdhara, explaining this mantra (the mantras of this sūkta are also found in the Yajurveda-saṃhitā, printed "ತ್ರೈ. ಸಂ. ಕಾಂ. ೪").

मांसभीक्षां उपासते (*māṃsabhīkṣāṃ upāsate*) *[so printed here, "ಮಾಂಸಭೀಕ್ಷಾಂ"]*—after the cooked flesh has been offered to the gods in the fire as an oblation, they desire that a small part of the remaining flesh be given to them also. Those who desire thus may be priests taking part in the sacrifice or others.

तेषामभिगूर्तिन् इन्वतु (*teṣāmabhigūrtin invatu*)—this sentence has been explained in the sixth ṛk of this sūkta.

### Printed p. 194

*Running head: 194 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ ೧೬೨] (as supplied).* (Sūkta 162, Ṛk 13.)

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**

मांस्पचॆन्या (*māṃspacènyā*) *[so printed, "ಚೆ"]*—of the pot in which flesh is put and cooked; उखाया (*ukhāyā*)—of the vessel; यत् (*yat*) नीक्षणं (*nīkṣaṇaṃ*) *[split over two lines]*—the wooden ladle or stick, the means of testing the cooking; (and) यूष्णः आसेचनानि (*yūṣṇaḥ āsecanāni*)—for pouring in the cooked flesh-broth; या पात्राणि (*yā pātrāṇi*)—whatever vessels there are, those also; (तथा (*tathā*)—likewise) ऊष्मण्या (*ūṣmaṇyā*)—plates that cover so that the heat (of the cooked flesh) does not cool; (तथा (*tathā*)—likewise) चरूणां अपिधाना (*carūṇāṃ apidhānā*)—also vessels for putting the cooked flesh; (तथा (*tathā*)—likewise) अंकाः (*aṃkāḥ*)—the twigs of the vetasa tree pierced, before cooking, into the limbs such as the heart *[printed "ದೃದಯಾದಿ"]* to identify them; सूना (*sūnā*)—implements such as knives and cleavers for cutting flesh; अश्वं परि (*aśvaṃ pari*)—spread around the horse; भूषंति (*bhūṣaṃti*)—appear as if adorning.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**

The wooden stick used to see whether the horse-flesh, put in a large vessel and cooking, is well cooked; the vessels for putting the cooked flesh-broth; the plates that cover the vessels so that the cooked flesh does not cool; the vessels for putting the flesh; the twigs of the vetasa tree pierced into the pieces of flesh, to identify, after cooking, the various limbs of the horse such as the heart; the knives, cleavers and the like for cutting the flesh: all these, placed around the horse in the sacrificial ground, look as if they adorn the horse.

**Printed English translation**

The stick that is dipped into the caldron in which the flesh is boiled ; the vessels that distribute the broth; the covers of the dishes, the skewers, the knives, all do honour (to the horse).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

यन्निक्षणं—पाकपरीक्षणसाधनं काष्ठं । (*yannikṣaṇaṃ—pākaparīkṣaṇasādhanaṃ kāṣṭhaṃ |*) A long wooden stick used to test whether the flesh cooking in the vessel is well cooked or not. It may be in the shape of a ladle or like a stick. With it they lift the hot flesh cooking in the vessel and look from time to time to see whether it is cooked enough or still needs cooking. The commentator has explained it as a piece of wood used for this.

मांस्पचन्या उखायाः (*māṃspacanyā ukhāyāḥ*)—the large vessel for cooking flesh. This vessel is called "ukhā". This vessel is a large earthen pot (printed "Coldron", in Latin letters, as supplied). It is also customary to call it "sthālī".

### Printed p. 195

*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ಪ. ೯] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 195 (as supplied; "ಪ." printed for "ವ.").*

The use of this word is in the places Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-13, 1-162-15, 3-53-22, Atharvaveda 7-3-23 (printed "ಅ. ವೇ."), Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-1-6-3, Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 11-59 (printed "ವಾ. ಸಂ."), Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4-1-5-4 and others. The method of making this vessel "ukhā" is told in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-1-7, and its sanskāras, the filling and so on, in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-1-7 *[so printed twice]*, and the Ukhā-homa in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā 5-5-3.

आसेचनानि पात्राणि यूष्णः (*āsecanāni pātrāṇi yūṣṇaḥ*)—"sechana" means sprinkling water; here the name means vessels for putting or distributing (serving) to all the essence of the flesh in the form of juice.

ऊष्मण्या अपिधाना (*ūṣmaṇyā apidhānā*)—plates that cover so that the hot flesh in the vessels does not cool.

अंका:—हृदयावयवांकनसाधना वेतसशाखाः । (*aṃkā:—hṛdayāvayavāṃkanasādhanā vetasaśākhāḥ |*) To mark the limbs and parts of the horse-flesh such as the heart, twigs of the vetasa tree are used. Since these twigs are pierced into the respective pieces of flesh, it is easy to know to which limb the horse-flesh belongs. In course of time it seems that needles made of gold, silver and lead came into use instead of the vetasa wood. The work of piercing these needles to identify the flesh of the limbs of the horse is generally done by women, especially the sacrificer's wife and others. This matter is stated in the mantras recited while doing this work:

गायत्री त्रिष्टुब्बगत्यनुष्टुप्पंक्ता सह । (*gāyatrī triṣṭubbagatyanuṣṭuppaṃktā saha |*)
बृहत्युष्टिहा ककुत्सूचीभिः शिम्यंतु त्वा ॥ (*bṛhatyuṣṭihā kakutsūcībhiḥ śimyaṃtu tvā ‖*)
द्विपदा या चतुष्पदा त्रिपदा या च षट्टदा । (*dvipadā yā catuṣpadā tripadā yā ca ṣaṭṭadā |*)
सछंदा या च विच्छंदास्सूचीभिः शिम्यंतु त्वा ॥ (*sachaṃdā yā ca vicchaṃdāssūcībhiḥ śimyaṃtu tvā ‖*)
महानामिन्ना रेवतयो विश्वा आशाः प्रसूवरीः । (*mahānāminnā revatayo viśvā āśāḥ prasūvarīḥ |*)
मेघ्या विद्युतो वाचः सूचीभिः शिम्यंतु त्वा ॥ (*meghyā vidyuto vācaḥ sūcībhiḥ śimyaṃtu tvā ‖*)
रजता हरिणीस्सा युजो युज्यंते कर्मभिः । (*rajatā hariṇīssā yujo yujyaṃte karmabhiḥ |*)
अश्वस्य वाजिनस्त्वचि सूचीभिः शिम्यंतु त्वा ॥ (*aśvasya vājinastvaci sūcībhiḥ śimyaṃtu tvā ‖*)
नारीस्ते पत्नियो लोम विचिन्वंतु मनीषया । (*nārīste patniyo loma vicinvaṃtu manīṣayā |*)
देवानां पत्निर्दिशःसूचीभिः शिम्यंतु त्वा ॥ (*devānāṃ patnirdiśaḥsūcībhiḥ śimyaṃtu tvā ‖*)
कुविदंग यवमंतो यवं चिद्यथा दांत्यनुपूर्वं वियूयॆ । (*kuvidaṃga yavamaṃto yavaṃ cidyathā dāṃtyanupūrvaṃ viyūyè |*)
इहेहैषां कृणुत भोजनानि ये बर्हिषो नमोव्यक्तिं न जग्मुः ॥ (*ihehaiṣāṃ kṛṇuta bhojanāni ye barhiṣo namovyaktiṃ na jagmuḥ ‖*) (ಕೃ. ಸಂ. 5-2-11) *[reference as printed, "ಕೃ. ಸಂ."]*

कुविदंग (*kuvidaṃga*)—this last mantra is read in Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-131-2, Atharvaveda 20-125-2, Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 10-32, 19-16 and 23-38, Taittirīya Saṃhitā 1-8-21-1 and 5-2-11-2, and

### Printed p. 196

*Running head: 196 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied; "ಆ." printed for "ಅ.").*

Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2-6-1-3. The horse-flesh is put in large earthen pots called "ukhā" and cooked, and afterwards the various limbs of the horse are offered in the fire as oblations, each with its respective mantra. Since after the flesh is cooked it is difficult to say which flesh belongs to which limb, before cooking, that is, when the flesh (the body of the horse) is being cut, needles made of metals such as gold, or sharp twigs of the vetasa tree, are pierced into the pieces of flesh, so as to make it convenient to identify the respective limbs well, and by cooking them thus it is easy to identify to which limb the cooked flesh belongs. For this reason women such as the sacrificer's wife do this work.

सूनाः—अवदानसाधनाः स्वधित्यादयः । (*sūnāḥ—avadānasādhanāḥ svadhityādayaḥ |*) A cleaver or other weapons for cutting flesh. The commentator has explained the word "sūnayā" in the ṛk 1-161-10 (printed "೧-೧೬೧-೧೦") as छेदनसाधनेन (*chedanasādhanena*), that is, with a weapon like a cleaver, the means of cutting flesh. "Implements of dissection, the Swadhiti and others." Some Western scholars (Macdonell and Keith) are of the opinion that this word means "Woven wickerwork basket for holding flesh", a woven basket for putting flesh *[the English phrases are in Latin letters in the supplied text, kept as supplied]*. But there is no proper basis for this. This word is read in the mantras Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-161-10, 1-162-13, 10-86-18, and "ಆ. ನೇ. ೫-೧೭-೧೪" *[so printed]*.

परि भूषंति अश्वं (*pari bhūṣaṃti aśvaṃ*)—vessels and the like used in sacrificial rites, and the oblation, food, animal and so on that are to be offered to the gods, are placed on the sacrificial altar or near the fire, while the sacrificial rite is going on, in order to be consecrated with mantras; they are purified with various sanskāras together with mantras, and afterwards used in the respective rites. In domestic rites too, the performing of such arranging of vessels and the like in the rite of establishing the fire called "agnimukha" with mantras is still the custom. This order has come down following the order of sacrifices and the like. Therefore the seer describes that, in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the weapons to be used after the horse is killed, the vessel "ukhā" for cooking flesh, the spit, the basket for filling the flesh and the various things that may be used at that time, which are placed around the horse in the sacrificial altar in order to be consecrated with mantras, look like an ornament, and that it is as if the horse were adorned.

**Grammar (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)**

*Note (the Sanskrit grammar is only transcribed, not explained):* the Kannada analysis of नीक्षणं (*nīkṣaṇaṃ*) (the rules Pā. Sū. 7-1-1 and 7-1-163 as printed) begins here; the analysis of Ṛk 13 is cut off in the supplied text at the end of this window and continues in the next window.

### Printed p. 197
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೯.] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 197] (as supplied; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 3, Varga 9, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with a stray closing bracket).*

*(Grammar, continued from the previous page; transcribed, not explained.)*

मांस्पचन्याः (*māṃspacanyāḥ*)—the root *ḍupachiṣ* (to cook); the affix *lyuṭ* in the sense of locus, by the rule Pā. Sū. 3-3-117; the substitution as before; the elision in the word *māṃsa* by the rule cited as Kā. 6-1-144 (as printed); in the compound the accent of the final member's base applies.

आसेचनानि (*āsecanāni*)—the root *ṣicir* (to flow); the affix *lyuṭ* in the sense of instrument; in the compound with a prefix the accent of the final member's base applies.

ऊष्मण्या (*ūṣmaṇyā*)—the affix *yat* in the sense of "fit for"; the svarita accent by the rule Pā. Sū. 6-1-185; in the neuter the elision of *śi* by the rule Pā. Sū. 6-1-70. The same elision of *śi* occurs in अपिधाना (*apidhānā*).

भूषंति (*bhūṣaṃti*)—the root *bhūṣa* (to adorn), first class, present tense, third person plural; being after a finite verb it takes the *nighāta* accent.

#### Ṛk 14
**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**
> नि॒क्रम॑णं नि॒षद॑नं वि॒वर्त॑नं॒ यच्च॒ षड्बे॑श॒मर्व॑तः ।
> यच्च॑ प॒पौ यच्च॑ घा॒सिं ज॒घास॒ सर्वा॒ ता ते॒ अपि॑ दे॒वे॑
> श्वस्तु ॥ १४ ॥
**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> निक्रमणं । निसदनं । विवर्तनं । यत् । च । पद्भीशं । अर्वतः ।
> यत् । च । पपौ । यत् । च । घासिं । जघूस । सर्वा । ता । ते । अपि । देवेषु । अस्तु ॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> यन्नि क्रमणं नितरां क्रमते यत्र तन्नि क्रमणं स्थानं । नितरां सीदत्यत्रेति ।
> निषदनं । विवर्तनं विविधवर्तनमितस्ततो लुंठनं यत्र तत् ॥ यच्चार्वतोऽश्वस्य

> *yanni kramaṇaṃ nitarāṃ kramate yatra tanni kramaṇaṃ sthānaṃ | nitarāṃ sīdatyatreti |*
> *niṣadanaṃ | vivartanaṃ vividhavartanamitastato luṃṭhanaṃ yatra tat ‖ yaccārvato 'śvasya*
### Printed p. 198
*Running head: 198 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೨] (as supplied; Maṇḍala 1, Anuvāka 22, Sūkta 162).*

> पद्वीशं पादबंधनं । यद्वा । बंधनं पट् तद्वान्प्रदेशः । अत्र सर्वत्र देवार्थस्याश्वस्य रोमादीनामपि निरर्थकत्वाभावाय तत्स्थानमपि स्वीक्रियते । यद्वा ।
> क्रियापरावगंतव्या । आलंभसमये निग्रहेण या निक्रमणादयश्वेष्टाः संति ता
> इत्यर्थः । यच्च पपौ यदुदकमपिबत् । यच्च घासिमदनीयं तृणादिकं जघास
> अभक्षयत् । हे अश्व ते तव ता तानि सर्वाणि निक्रमणादीनि देवेष्वस्तु । संतु ।
> देवेषु व्याप्नोतु । तान्यपि निरर्थकानि मा भूवन्नित्यर्थः ॥
*Gist:* Sāyaṇa explains the places of going forth, sitting and rolling, and the foot-fastening (rope or place); the water drunk and the grass eaten by the horse are likewise to go to the gods, so that nothing is wasted.

*[as supplied: the label "ಪ್ರಗಿದಾರ್ಥ" stands after the bhāṣya; it is garbled and was replaced by the standard label Pratipadārtha.]*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
(हे अश्व (*he aśva*)—O sacrificial horse); अर्वतः (*arvataḥ*)—of you, this sacrificial horse; निक्रमणं (*nikramaṇaṃ*)—the place of going about; निषदनं (*niṣadanaṃ*)—the place of standing; विवर्तनं (*vivartanaṃ*)—the place of rolling on the ground; यच्च पद्वीशं (*yacca padvīśaṃ*)—and the rope that binds the horse's feet; यच्च पपौ (*yacca papau*)—and the water the horse drank; यच्च घासिं जघास (*yacca ghāsiṃ jaghāsa*)—and also the food, grass and the like, that the horse ate; ते (*te*)—your; ता अपि (*tā api*)—all such acts as well; देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods (to the gods); अस्तु (*astu*)—may they be offered (may they reach).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
O sacrificial horse, the places where you walked while grazing, where you stood here and there, and where you rolled on the ground to rest, the rope used to bind your feet, the water you drank and the grass you ate: may all these not be wasted but be offered to the gods themselves.

**Printed English**
May the place of going forth, of tarrying, of rolling on the ground ; tha [sic] foot-fastening of the horse, (the water) that he has drunk, the grass that he has eaten ; may all these be yours among the gods.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
In this Ṛk the seer, praying to the horse, indicates his wish that its hair and the like, and the grass it ate and the water it drank, should not be wasted but should reach the gods. Since the limbs and flesh of the horse, prepared by cooking and so on, are offered in the fire for the gods' pleasure, all of that reaches the gods and becomes fruitful; and what cannot be offered in the fire, the water in the horse's belly, the undigested grass and the like, is also prayed for, that it may not be wasted but may reach the gods. This prayer is described in this Ṛk.

### Printed p. 199
*Running head: [ಅ ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೯.] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 199] (as supplied; Aṣṭaka 2, Adhyāya 3, Varga 9, Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, with a stray closing bracket).*

निक्रमणं (*nikramaṇaṃ*), निषदनं (*niṣadanaṃ*), विवर्तनं (*vivartanaṃ*)—the places where the horse, in its lifetime, walked about, lay down and rested, and the like: the description is that these too should reach the gods and cause them pleasure; thus the daily course of the horse's life is described, and the prayer is that it may be a cause of the gods' delight.

पद्वीशं (*padvīśaṃ*)—the commentator has explained this word in two ways: पद्वीशं पादबंधनं (*padvīśaṃ pādabaṃdhanaṃ*) and यद्वा तद्वान् प्रदेशः (*yadvā tadvān pradeśaḥ*), that is, either the rope that binds the horse's feet or the place where the horse is tied. Some parts of the meaning stated in this Ṛk are stated in another manner in the Ṛk of this same sūkta beginning यद्वाजिनो दाम (*yadvājino dāma*).

यच्च पपौ यच्च घासिं जघास (*yacca papau yacca ghāsiṃ jaghāsa*)—the seer prays that the water the horse drank and the grass it ate should reach the gods. For, as stated in यदूवध्यमुदरस्यापवाति (*yadūvadhyamudarasyāpavāti*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-162-10) of this sūkta, the undigested food in the form of grass in the horse's belly is to be removed and only the clean flesh cooked. Therefore the grass the horse ate and the water it drank, which cannot be offered to the gods in the oblation, are, according to my prayer, to reach the gods themselves: such is the seer's intention described.

The rite of offering the horse's limbs, that is, the rite of offering the various limbs of the horse in the fire with mantras, is described in detail in the 14 anuvākas, 11-23, of the fifth kāṇḍa of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, beginning स्तेगान्नंष्ट्राभ्यां (*stegānnaṃṣṭrābhyāṃ*). For fear of prolixity they are not explained here.

As there are Āprī-sūktas for the animal offering in other animal sacrifices, the Āprī-sūkta relating to the horse, used in the Aśvamedha sacrifice, is found in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā. It has eleven mantras. Since this sūkta is not in the Ṛgveda, it is given here:

1. (1)
समिद्धो अंजन्करं मतीनां धृतमग्ने मधुमत्पिन्वमानः । (*samiddho aṃjankaraṃ matīnāṃ dhṛtamagne madhumatpinvamānaḥ |*)
वाजी वहन्वाजिनं जातवेदो देवानां वक्षि प्रियमा सधस्थं ॥ (*vājī vahanvājinaṃ jātavedo devānāṃ vakṣi priyamā sadhasthaṃ ‖*)
(2)
धृतेनांजन्तं पथो देवयानान्स्र जानन्वाज्यप्येतु देवान् । (*dhṛtenāṃjantaṃ patho devayānānsra jānanvājyapyetu devān |*)
अनु त्वा सप्ते प्रदिशस्सचंताग् स्वधामस्मै यजमानाय धेहि ॥ (*anu tvā sapte pradiśassacaṃtāg svadhāmasmai yajamānāya dhehi ‖*)
(3)
ईड्यश्चासि वंद्यश्च वाजिन्नाशुश्चासि मेध्यश्व सप्ते । (*īḍyaścāsi vaṃdyaśca vājinnāśuścāsi medhyaśva sapte |*)
अग्निष्ट्वा देवैर्वसुभिस्सजोषाः प्रीतं वह्निं वहतु जातवेदाः ॥ (*agniṣṭvā devairvasubhissajoṣāḥ prītaṃ vahniṃ vahatu jātavedāḥ ‖*)
(4)
स्तीर्णं बर्हिस्सुष्टरीमा जुषाणोरु पृथु प्रथमानं पृथिव्यां । (*stīrṇaṃ barhissuṣṭarīmā juṣāṇoru pṛthu prathamānaṃ pṛthivyāṃ |*)
देवेभिर्युक्तमदितिस्सजोषाः सोनं कृष्णाना सुविते दधातु ॥ (*devebhiryuktamaditissajoṣāḥ sonaṃ kṛṣṇānā suvite dadhātu ‖*)
