#### Ṛk 7
**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**
> इ॒ह ब्र॑वीतु॒ य ई॑मं॒ग वेदा॒स्य वा॒मस्य॒ निहि॑तं प॒दं वेः ।
> शी॒र्ष्णर् क्षी॒रं दु॑प्रते॒ गावो॑ अस्य व॒व्रिं वसा॑ना उद॒कं॒॑
> पदापुः ॥ ७ ॥

> *iha bravītu ya īmaṃga vedāsya vāmasya nihitaṃ padaṃ veḥ |*
> *śīrṣṇar kṣīraṃ duprate gāvo asya vavriṃ vasānā udakaṃ*
> *padāpuḥ ‖ 7 ‖*

### Printed p. 331
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 331 (as supplied).*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> इह । ब्रवीतु । यः । ईं । अंग । वेद । अस्य । वामस्य । निहितं । पदं । वेरिति
> वेः ।
> शीर्ष्णः । क्षीरं । दुह्रते । गावः । अस्य । वव्रिं । वसानाः । उदकं । पदा । अपुः ॥७॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> इहेदानीमीमेतद्वक्ष्यमाणं तत्त्वमंग क्षिप्रमविचारेण ब्रवीतु । कः ।
> यो वेद सः । कीदृशं तत् । अस्य पुरतो दृश्यमानस्य वामस्य वननीयस्य वेर्गंतुरादित्यस्य सदं सर्वैर्गंतव्यं स्वरूपं निहितं गूढं वर्तते । किंचास्यादित्यस्य शीर्षः
> शिरोवदुन्नतस्य सर्वेषामुत्कृष्टस्य वा गावः केचन वर्षकालीना रश्मयः क्षीरमुदकं दुह्रते । क्षरंति । वन्रिं । रूपनामैतत् । रूपं वसाना आच्छादयंतोऽतिविस्तरेण तेजसा तपंतः केचनास्य गावो रश्मय उदकं स्वसृष्टं पदा सृष्टेनैव
> मार्गेणापुः । पिबंति । भूमिं निरुदकां कुर्वंतीत्यर्थः । तस्य स्वरूपं ब्रवीत्वित्यन्वयः ॥
*Gist:* Let the one who knows quickly declare the hidden, true station of the lovely, moving sun, whose rays shed water and drink it back by the same paths.
**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
इह (*iha*)—in the present context; ईं (*īṃ*)—this chief principle; यः (*yaḥ*)—which wise man; वेद (*veda*)—has known (he); अंग (*aṃga*)—quickly; ब्रवीतु (*bravītu*)—let him say; वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—of one who has a charming form; वेः (*veḥ*)—and who is given to moving about; अस्य (*asya*)—of this Āditya; पदं (*padaṃ*)—the station that is of the nature of truth; निहितं (*nihitaṃ*)—is hidden *[as supplied: the dash is lost and the words are run together in print]*; शीर्ष्णः (*śīrṣṇaḥ*)—from his most excellent station; गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—rays; वव्रिं (*vavriṃ*)—his form; वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*)—covering with radiance; क्षीरं (*kṣīraṃ*)—water; दुह्रते (*duhrate*)—shed; अस्य (*asya*)—of this same Āditya (those same rays); उदकं (*udakaṃ*)—the water shed by themselves; पदा (*padā*)—by the very path by which they shed it; आपुः (*āpuḥ*)—they drink up.
**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Let the wise man who knows this chief principle here explain it quickly. The station, of the nature of truth, of this Āditya, who has a charming form and is given to moving about, remains hidden. From his most excellent station the rays pour out water, covering his form with radiance. The rays of this same Āditya drink up, by the very paths by which they poured it out, the water shed by themselves.

### Printed p. 332
*Running head: 332 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧ ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

**Printed English**
Let him who knows this (truth) quickly declare it; the mysterious condition of the beautiful ever-moving (sun): the rays shed (their) milk from his (exalted) head, investing his form with radiance: they have drunk up the water by the paths (by which they were poured forth).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
In the fifth Ṛk of this same hymn, वत्से बष्कयोऽधि सप्त तंतून्वितत्निरे कवय ओतवा उ (*vatse baṣkayo 'dhi sapta taṃtūnvitatnire kavaya otavā u*), the very close connection between sacrificial rites and so on and Āditya is shown. Since the protection of Āditya is absolutely necessary both for the maintenance of the warp and woof of the world-form and for the furtherance of the rites that are the means to it, there is praise of Āditya in the words that the poets worship such an Āditya with the seven threads. In the Ṛk after that, the fact that Āditya is upholding and regulating the six worlds is stated, and in the Ṛk now under consideration, गावः क्षीरं दुह्रते (*gāvaḥ kṣīraṃ duhrate*) and उदकं पदापुः (*udakaṃ padāpuḥ*) *[as supplied: printed "ಶೀರ್ಷ ೯" before ಗಾವಃ, and a semicolon between the two]*: the rays of Āditya, issuing from the excellent station of Āditya, spread water over the whole world from various sides, and the manner in which they again drink that water by the same paths is also described. Thus, in all the mantras one after the other, after it has been stated that Āditya and the rays of Āditya are the means for the maintenance of the world of practical affairs, the principle of the universe, which is beyond such a world, beyond the senses such as the eye, and which shines eternally in the disc of Āditya, is described by sentences such as देवानामेना निहिता पदानि (*devānāmenā nihitā padāni*) (5), अजस्य रूपे किमपि स्विदेकं (*ajasya rūpe kimapi svidekaṃ*), अस्य वामस्य निहितं पदं वेः (*asya vāmasya nihitaṃ padaṃ veḥ*) (7) and so on. In each Ṛk the glory of Āditya, who is within reach of ordinary perception, is described on one side, and on the other the glory of the principle that is beyond this, both together. In the Ṛk now under consideration, first the hidden principle is hinted at by निहितं पदं (*nihitaṃ padaṃ*), and then,

शीर्षः क्षीरं दुह्रते गावो अस्य वप्रा वसाना उदकं पदापुः (*śīrṣaḥ kṣīraṃ duhrate gāvo asya vaprā vasānā udakaṃ padāpuḥ*) *[as supplied: ವಪ್ರಾ where the Saṃhitā has ವವ್ರಿಂ]*

the rays of Āditya, issuing from the excellent station of Āditya, spread water for the whole world in various places and again take it in from the same directions: thus it is shown that Āditya is both the support and the means for the maintenance of the world of practical affairs. Thus, pervading all heaven and earth with his rays, he is the cause of the sacrifice, which is the cause of the maintenance of things, and of the ancillary rites that go with it, both in the form of effect, which changes, and in the form of cause, which is eternal; combining the purport of these three Ṛks, this is described in the Chāndogya and other texts as follows.

### Printed p. 333
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೪ ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 333 (as supplied).*

असा वादित्यो देवमधु तस्य द्यौरेव तिरश्चीनवंशोऽंतरिक्षमपूपो मरीचयः पुत्राः । तस्य ये प्रांचो रश्मयस्ता एवास्य प्राच्यो मधुनाड्यः । ऋच एव मधुकृत ऋग्वेद एव पुष्पं ता अमृता आपस्तावा एता ऋचः । एतमृग्वेदमभ्यतपग्गस्तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस्सेज इंद्रिय वीर्यमन्नाद्यं रसोऽजायत ॥ तद्व्यक्षरत्तदादित्यमभितोऽश्रयत्तद्वा एतद्यदेतदादित्यस्य रोहितं रूपं (*asā vādityo devamadhu tasya dyaureva tiraścīnavaṃśo 'ṃtarikṣamapūpo marīcayaḥ putrāḥ | tasya ye prāṃco raśmayastā evāsya prācyo madhunāḍyaḥ | ṛca eva madhukṛta ṛgveda eva puṣpaṃ tā amṛtā āpastāvā etā ṛcaḥ | etamṛgvedamabhyatapaggastasyābhitaptasya yaśasseja iṃdriya vīryamannādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ‖ tadvyakṣarattadādityamabhito 'śrayattadvā etadyadetadādityasya rohitaṃ rūpaṃ*)
(छा. उ. (*chā. u.*) 3-1)

This Āditya is the divine honey; the heaven-world is the line of support that bears it, the atmosphere is the nest, and the rays are the sons. The rays that spread towards the eastern quarter are the honey-channels of the eastern quarter. The Ṛks are the bees. The Ṛgveda is the flower; the oblations of ghee and milk offered in the sacrifice are the drops of nectar. After the Ṛk mantras had ripened, fame, lustre, the senses, virility, strength and sap arose from rites such as sacrifice. Afterwards all these, sap and the rest, which are of the nature of fruit, spread facing Āditya and joined him. These are the causes of the beautiful form of the red disc of the rising Āditya.

अथ येऽस्य दक्षिणा रश्मयस्ता एवास्य दक्षिणा मधुनाड्यो यजूग्ंष्येव मधुकृतो यजुर्वेद एव पुष्पं ता अमृता आपः । तानि वा एतानि यजूग्ं ष्येतं यजुर्वेदमभ्यतपग्गस्तस्याभितप्तस्य यशस्सेज इंद्रियं वीर्यमन्नाद्यं रसोऽजायत ॥ तद्व्यक्षरत्तदादित्यमभितोऽश्रयत्तद्वा एतद्यदेतदादित्यस्य शुक्लं रूपं (*atha ye 'sya dakṣiṇā raśmayastā evāsya dakṣiṇā madhunāḍyo yajūgṃṣyeva madhukṛto yajurveda eva puṣpaṃ tā amṛtā āpaḥ | tāni vā etāni yajūgṃ ṣyetaṃ yajurvedamabhyatapaggastasyābhitaptasya yaśasseja iṃdriyaṃ vīryamannādyaṃ raso 'jāyata ‖ tadvyakṣarattadādityamabhito 'śrayattadvā etadyadetadādityasya śuklaṃ rūpaṃ*)
(भा. उ. (*bhā. u.*) 3-2-) *[as supplied: ಭಾ. ಉ. ೩-೨- with a trailing hyphen]*

The rays that spread towards the southern quarter are the honey-channels of the south. The Yajus mantras are the bees. The Yajurveda is the flower, the ghee and milk offered as sacrificial oblations are the drops of nectar. From this, sap and the rest arose, and again spreading facing Āditya, join Āditya himself. These are the causes of the white form of Āditya.

अथ येऽस्य प्रत्यंचो रश्मयः .... .... .... सामान्येव मधुकृतस्सामवेद एव पुष्पं .... .... .... एतदादित्यस्य कृष्णं रूपं (*atha ye 'sya pratyaṃco raśmayaḥ .... .... .... sāmānyeva madhukṛtassāmaveda eva puṣpaṃ .... .... .... etadādityasya kṛṣṇaṃ rūpaṃ*)

### Printed p. 334
*Running head: 334 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

In the flower in the form of the Sāmaveda, the bees in the form of the Sāmans created the drops of nectar in the form of oblations and joined the sun. That is the cause of the black form of that Āditya. Afterwards, from the flower in the form of Itihāsa and Purāṇa, the bee in the form of Atharva created the drop of nectar in the form of sap and the rest. These joined Āditya. These are the causes of the dark black form of this same Āditya.

ते ना एते रसानां रसा वेदा हि रसास्तेषामेते रसास्तानि वा एतान्यमृतानाममृतानि वेदा ह्यमृतास्तेषामेतान्यमृतानि (*te nā ete rasānāṃ rasā vedā hi rasāsteṣāmete rasāstāni vā etānyamṛtānāmamṛtāni vedā hyamṛtāsteṣāmetānyamṛtāni*)
(छा. उ. (*chā. u.*) 3-5)

These various colours of Āditya are the essences of the saps. Of which saps are they the essences? The essence of the finest things on the earth is the Vedas; after these have undergone transformation into the form of sacrifice, the colours of the sun that arose as the fruit of its sap are the essence of sacrifices and the rest. This radiance of Āditya, of many colours, kindled by the immortal Vedas and the rest, is like nectar even to all nectar.

यद्यत्पथमममृतं तद्वसव उपजीवंत्यग्निना मुखेन वै देवा अश्नंति न पिबंत्येतदेवामृतं दृष्ट्वा तृप्यंति (*yadyatpathamamamṛtaṃ tadvasava upajīvaṃtyagninā mukhena vai devā aśnaṃti na pibaṃtyetadevāmṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā tṛpyaṃti*)
*[Before and after each of the following passages the print has four-dot ellipses, as supplied.]*
अथ यद्द्वितीयममृतं तद्रुद्रा उपजीवंति .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... अथ यत्तृतीयममृतं तदादित्या उपजीवंति .... .... ........ .... .... .... .... अथ यच्चतुर्थममृतं तन्मरुत उपजीवंति .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... अथ यत्पंचमममृतं तत्साध्या उपजीवंति (*atha yaddvitīyamamṛtaṃ tadrudrā upajīvaṃti .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... atha yattṛtīyamamṛtaṃ tadādityā upajīvaṃti .... .... ........ .... .... .... .... atha yaccaturthamamṛtaṃ tanmaruta upajīvaṃti .... .... .... .... .... .... .... .... atha yatpaṃcamamamṛtaṃ tatsādhyā upajīvaṃti*)
(भा. उ. (*bhā. u.*) 12-6 to 10) *[as supplied: ಭಾ. ಉ. 12-೬ ರಿಂದ ೧೦, with mixed numerals]*

In these five kinds of forms of Āditya, which are nectarous and sap-natured, dwell the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Maruts and the Sādhyas; they themselves enter these colours, the red and the rest. He who knows the essences of these nectars obtains a place among the Vasus, Rudras and the rest. He too mingles in those colours of Āditya and is born again from those very colours. (त एतदेव रूपमभिसंविशंत्येतस्माद्रूपादुद्यंति (*ta etadeva rūpamabhisaṃviśaṃtyetasmādrūpādudyaṃti*)) Āditya too moves about in these worlds of the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas and the rest, beholding as he moves the glory of their self-rule.

अथ तत ऊर्ध्वं उदेत्य नैवोदेता नास्तमेतैकल एव मध्ये स्थाता तदेष श्लोकः ॥ न वै तत्र न निम्मोच नोदियाय कदाचन । देवास्तेनाहं सत्येन मा विराधिषि ब्रह्मणेति (*atha tata ūrdhvaṃ udetya naivodetā nāstametaikala eva madhye sthātā tadeṣa ślokaḥ ‖ na vai tatra na nimmoca nodiyāya kadācana | devāstenāhaṃ satyena mā virādhiṣi brahmaṇeti*)

### Printed p. 335
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 335 (as supplied).*

न ह वा अस्मा उदेति न निम्मोचति सकृद्दिवा हैवास्मै भवति य एतामेवं ब्रह्मोपनिषदं वेद (*na ha vā asmā udeti na nimmocati sakṛddivā haivāsmai bhavati ya etāmevaṃ brahmopaniṣadaṃ veda*)
(छा. उ. (*chā. u.*) 3-11 ; 1-3) *[as supplied: with a semicolon]*

Here, for the word अथ (*atha*), Śaṅkarācārya has given the meaning कृत्त्वमुदयास्तमनेन प्राणिनां स्वकर्मफलभोगनिमित्तमनुग्रहं (*kṛttvamudayāstamanena prāṇināṃ svakarmaphalabhoganimittamanugrahaṃ*), that is, having made the movements in the form of rising and setting in the worlds of the Vasus, Rudras and so on, in order to give to all living beings the fruits in accordance with their deeds; and also the meaning "afterwards". Since in the hymn now under consideration also it is described that Āditya carries on the maintenance of the world by his movements of rising and setting, and that in the eternal state he is in the form of the Supreme Self, the Upaniṣadic sentences up to here have described only the world-regulating activity of Āditya. From here onward they describe the Supreme-Self nature of Āditya.

Āditya, having shone in all the worlds of the Vasus, Rudras, Ādityas and the rest, then reaches the world that lies above them, and remains there in an eternal state. In that world Āditya has neither rising nor setting. He is resplendent in the middle and is without a second. In the verse beginning न वै तत्र न निम्लोच (*na vai tatra na nimloca*) *[as supplied: the quotation on p. 334 has ನಿಮ್ಮೋಚ]* the state of this supreme abode of Āditya is described. He who has known this principle described in the Upaniṣadic sentence reaches that world, and for him too there are no risings and settings of the sun. For him it is always eternal day. This very thing:

तस्माद्वा एतं सेतुं तीर्थापि नक्तमहरेवाभिनिष्पद्यते सकृद्विभातो ह्यैवैष ब्रह्मलोकः (*tasmādvā etaṃ setuṃ tīrthāpi naktamaharevābhiniṣpadyate sakṛdvibhāto hyaivaiṣa brahmalokaḥ*)
(भा. उ. (*bhā. u.*) 8-4-2)

It is described that, after crossing the bridge by which one goes from the impermanent worlds and joins the world of Brahman, one reaches the world of Brahman and, seeing no darkness of any kind, experiences eternal light.

In the same way, the nature of Āditya described in the 5th, 6th and 7th Ṛks of the hymn now under consideration shows both these kinds of nature of Āditya. In the 7th Ṛk the latter half describes the work of world-maintenance of Āditya, and the former half describes his eternal, hidden nature, which is beyond ordinary perception.

ईं (*īṃ*)—ordinarily this word has no meaning. अथ ये प्रवृत्तेऽर्थेऽमिताक्षरेषु ग्रंथेषु वाक्यपूरणा आगच्छंति पदपूरणास्ते मिताक्षरेष्वनर्थकाः कमीमिद्विति (*atha ye pravṛtte 'rthe 'mitākṣareṣu graṃtheṣu vākyapūraṇā āgacchaṃti padapūraṇāste mitākṣareṣvanarthakāḥ kamīmidviti*)
(Ni. 1-9), that is, the word ईं (*īṃ*) does not have a separate meaning of its own. This word, in many places *(the sentence breaks off at the end of the page and continues in the next window)*

### Printed p. 336
*Running head: 336 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

[Continuing from the previous page:] ...is used merely to complete the sentence. Although this is the explanation given in the Nirukta, in the present Ṛk it is used to point to a definite indication, namely एतद्वक्ष्यमाणं तत्त्वं (*etadvakṣyamāṇaṃ tattvaṃ*) ("the truth that is about to be told").

वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—by the word वननीयस्य (*vananīyasya*) the attractive form of Āditya is described. This is the outer form of Āditya. Within such an outer disc lies the supreme abode of the Supreme Self, which is visible to no one

*Grammatical process (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)*

ब्रवीतु (*bravītu*)—the root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*). A form ending in the third person singular of loṭ. Because it stands after a finite verb, the nighāta accent comes.

वेद (*veda*)—the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*). When tip comes in the third person singular of laṭ, by विदो लटोवा (*vido laṭovā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-83) it takes the substitute ṇal. By पुगंतलघूपधस्य च (*pugaṃtalaghūpadhasya ca*) the root's light penultimate takes guṇa. Because of the connection with yad, the nighāta accent does not come. Because the suffix is lit, by लिति (*liti*) the udātta accent falls on the syllable before the suffix.

वेः (*veḥ*)—the root वी गत्यादिषु (*vī gatyādiṣu*). To it the Aunādika suffix i. The ṭi (ī) of the root is dropped; it becomes udātta by the suffix accent. A form ending in the genitive singular.

शीर्षः (*śīrṣaḥ*)—by शीर्षन् छंदसि (*śīrṣan chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-60) the word शिरः (*śiraḥ*) has, as an alternative, the word śīrṣan, which is fixed as final-udātta. When the genitive singular follows, by अल्लोपोऽनः (*allopo 'naḥ*) the vowel a of अनिन (*anina*) [sic; as supplied] is dropped. By the udātta-nivṛtti accent the case ending becomes udātta.

दुह्रते (*duhrate*)—the root दुह प्रपूरणे (*duha prapūraṇe*). In the third person plural of laṭ, the suffix jha. luk for śap. By आत्मनेपदेष्टनतः (*ātmanepadeṣṭanataḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-5) [as supplied] the suffix takes the substitute ata, and ṭi takes e. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) it takes the augment ruṭ; because it is ṭit, it comes as the initial part. Because it stands after a finite verb, the nighāta accent comes.

वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*)—the root वस आच्छादने (*vasa ācchādane*). The substitute śānac for laṭ. Because the root is anudāttet, by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the suffix becomes anudātta, and therefore the accent of the root remains.

पदा (*padā*)—by ऊडिदंपदादि- (*ūḍidaṃpadādi-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the case ending takes the udātta accent.

अपुः (*apuḥ*)—the root पा पाने (*pā pāne*). In the third person plural of luṅ, the suffix jhi. When the substitute sic has come for च्चिगॆ (*ccigè*) [as supplied], by गातिस्थासिच— (*gātisthāsica—*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-77) [as supplied] luk for it, and by आतः (*ātaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-110) *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> माता । पितरं । ऋते । आ । बभाज । धीती । अग्रे । मनसा । सं । हि । जग्मे ।
> सा । बीभत्सुः । गर्भरसा । निविद्धा । नमस्वंतः । इत् । उपवाकं । ईयुः ॥ ८ ॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> माता सर्वस्य निर्मात्री पृथिवी पितरं पालकं द्युलोकं तत्स्थं । द्युलोकस्थमादित्यमित्यर्थः । तमा बभाज । आभजते । किमर्थं । ऋत उदके यज्ञे वा
> निमित्तभूते सति । केन द्वारेण । धीती धीत्या कर्मणा यागादिरूपेण । स्वकीयेनाज्यसोमादिहविषा तर्पयतीत्यर्थः । अग्रे ततः पूर्वं पिता च मनसास्यामभिप्रायवता चेतसा सं जग्मे हि । संश्लिष्टो वर्तते खलु । वृष्टिमकरोदित्यर्थः ।
> अनंतरं सा माता बीभत्सुर्गर्भबंधनेच्छावती गर्भरसा गर्भरसेन गर्भोत्पत्ति निमित्तेन रसेन निविद्दा नितरां विद्यासीत् । यद्वा । गर्भे रस ओषध्याद्युत्पादनसमर्थमुदकं यस्याः सा तादृश्युदकेनात्यंतं क्लिन्ना निविद्दा कृषीवलैर्हलमुखेन नितरां
> विदारिता भवति बीजावासार्थं । अत्रायं समाधिः । या काचन योषिदपत्यार्थं
> स्वपतिं युवानं यौति स च तस्यामनुरागयुक्तः संगतो भवति सा चांतर्वती
> सती पुत्राञ्जनयतीति तद्वदत्रापि । अनंतरं नमस्वंत इद्भाविव्रीहिप्रियंग्वाद्यन्नवंत
> एवोपवाकमुपेत्य वचनं परस्परं सम्यगभिवृद्धानि सस्यानीति वचनमीयुः । प्राप्पुवंति । यद्वा । हनिर्लक्षणान्नवंत उपेत्य वचनं प्रैषादिरूपमीयुः । वृष्टौ
> सत्यां सस्यादिद्वारा यागमनुतिष्ठेयुरित्यर्थः ॥

> *mātā sarvasya nirmātrī pṛthivī pitaraṃ pālakaṃ dyulokaṃ tatsthaṃ | dyulokasthamādityamityarthaḥ | tamā babhāja | ābhajate | kimarthaṃ | ṛta udake yajñe vā*
> *nimittabhūte sati | kena dvāreṇa | dhītī dhītyā karmaṇā yāgādirūpeṇa | svakīyenājyasomādihaviṣā tarpayatītyarthaḥ | agre tataḥ pūrvaṃ pitā ca manasāsyāmabhiprāyavatā cetasā saṃ jagme hi | saṃśliṣṭo vartate khalu | vṛṣṭimakarodityarthaḥ |*
> *anaṃtaraṃ sā mātā bībhatsurgarbhabaṃdhanecchāvatī garbharasā garbharasena garbhotpatti nimittena rasena nividdā nitarāṃ vidyāsīt | yadvā | garbhe rasa oṣadhyādyutpādanasamarthamudakaṃ yasyāḥ sā tādṛśyudakenātyaṃtaṃ klinnā nividdā kṛṣīvalairhalamukhena nitarāṃ*
> *vidāritā bhavati bījāvāsārthaṃ | atrāyaṃ samādhiḥ | yā kācana yoṣidapatyārthaṃ*
> *svapatiṃ yuvānaṃ yauti sa ca tasyāmanurāgayuktaḥ saṃgato bhavati sā cāṃtarvatī*
> *satī putrāñjanayatīti tadvadatrāpi | anaṃtaraṃ namasvaṃta idbhāvivrīhipriyaṃgvādyannavaṃta*
> *evopavākamupetya vacanaṃ parasparaṃ samyagabhivṛddhāni sasyānīti vacanamīyuḥ | prāppuvaṃti | yadvā | hanirlakṣaṇānnavaṃta upetya vacanaṃ praiṣādirūpamīyuḥ | vṛṣṭau*
> *satyāṃ sasyādidvārā yāgamanutiṣṭheyurityarthaḥ ‖*

*Gist:* Earth serves the heavenly sun through sacrifice for rain; he rains; the soaked earth is ploughed, and sacrificers voice praise for the coming crops.

### Printed p. 338
*Running head: 338 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied; "ಆ" stands for "ಅ." here).*

*[as supplied: a garbled label प्रतिकदार्थ (*pratikadārtha*) stands here, before the label Pratipadārtha.]*
**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
माता (*mātā*)—the earth, the maker (of all); ऋते (*ṛte*)—for water; धीत्या (*dhītyā*)—by the rite in the form of sacrifice etc.; पितरं (*pitaraṃ*)—the protector, the Āditya who is in the heaven-world; आ बभाज (*ā babhāja*)—she served. (पिता (*pitā*)—Āditya.) अग्रे (*agre*)—even prior to this; मनसा (*manasā*)—with a mind (that knew the earth's wish); सं जग्मे हि (*saṃ jagme hi*)—had indeed formed the resolve to produce rain, or: sent down the rain beforehand. सा (*sā*)—the earth; बीभत्सुः (*bībhatsuḥ*)—with the desire to conceive; गर्भरसा (*garbharasā*)—and with the sap that is the means of the origin of the embryo; निविद्धा (*nividdhā*)—became united. इत् (*it*)—immediately after that; नमस्वंतः (*namasvaṃtaḥ*)—(all the sacrificers) who looked forward to the rice and other grain that will surely grow; उपवाकं (*upavākaṃ*)—words of praise accompanied by congratulation; ईयुः (*īyuḥ*)—they exchange.

*[as supplied: a garbled label धनार्थ (*dhanārtha*) stands here, before the label Bhāvārtha.]*
**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
The earth, the maker of the world, served, for the sake of water, by the rite in the form of sacrifice etc., Āditya who abides in the heaven-world. Even before that, Āditya, with a mind that knew the earth's wish, sent down rain. The earth became united with the desire to conceive and with the sap that is the means of the origin of the embryo. Immediately, all the sacrificers, who looked forward to the rice and other grain that will surely grow hereafter, exchanged words of congratulation with one another.

**Printed English**
The mother, (earth), worships the father, (sun). with [sic] holy rites, for the sake of water; but he has anticipated (her wants) in his mind ; whereupon, desirous of progeny, she is penetrated by the dews of impregnation, and, {all} [sic] expectant of abundance, exchange words (of congratulation).

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
In this Ṛk the conjugal relation between Earth and Āditya is stated, and the manner of love in that conjugal union and the nature of the fruit of that love are made known. This is just what Sāyaṇa explains in the bhāṣya with the words “या काचन योषिदपत्यार्थं स्वपतिं युवानं यौति स च तस्यामनुरागयुक्तः संगतो भवति सा चांतर्वत्नी सती पुत्रान् जनयतीति तद्वदत्रापि (*yā kācana yoṣidapatyārthaṃ svapatiṃ yuvānaṃ yauti sa ca tasyāmanurāgayuktaḥ saṃgato bhavati sā cāṃtarvatnī satī putrān janayatīti tadvadatrāpi*)” [that is: when a woman who desires her husband's love desires, for the sake of a son, union with her husband, and the husband too, being extremely affectionate towards her, fulfils her wish, then she becomes pregnant and obtains a son]; in the same way the woman in the form of Earth showed love towards the husband in the form of Āditya, obtained in return his love as well, and as a result obtained a fruit in the form of food—so it is explained.

### Printed p. 339
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 339 (as supplied).*

माता (*mātā*)—सर्वस्य निर्मात्री पृथिवी (*sarvasya nirmātrī pṛthivī*); that is, the Earth, who creates everything.

तद्यदुपयामेन ग्रहा गृह्यंते अनय्येव तद्गृह्यंतेऽथ यद्योन् सादयतीयं वा अस्य सर्वस्य योनिरस्यै वा इमाः प्रजाः प्रजाताः ॥ तं वा एतग्ं रेतो भूतग्ं सोममृत्विजो बिभ्रति यद्वा अयोन् रेतः सिच्यते प्र वै तन्नीयतेऽथ यद्योन् सादयत्यस्यामेव तत्सादयति (*tadyadupayāmena grahā gṛhyaṃte anayyeva tadgṛhyaṃte 'tha yadyon sādayatīyaṃ vā asya sarvasya yonirasyai vā imāḥ prajāḥ prajātāḥ ‖ taṃ vā etagṃ reto bhūtagṃ somamṛtvijo bibhrati yadvā ayon retaḥ sicyate pra vai tannīyate 'tha yadyon sādayatyasyāmeva tatsādayati*)
(Śa. Brā. 4-1-2-9 to 10)
The upayāma cup is taken with the help of this Earth. And since this Earth is the womb for the birth of all creatures and is the mother, he places the upayāma cup in the womb itself. Whatever is placed in the womb is as good as placed in the Earth—thus the point that Earth is the mother of all beings is described. If Earth is the mother, then heaven is the father—thus the conjugal relation of heaven and earth is shown. But since in the present Ṛk the relation between Āditya and Earth is stated, it need not be understood that there is a difference between the relation of heaven and earth and the relation of Āditya and earth.

उद्वयं तमसस्परीति पाप्मा वै तमः पाप्मानमेव तमोऽपहते स्वः पश्यंत उत्तरमित्ययं वै लोकोऽद्ध्य उत्तरोऽस्मिन्नेव लोके प्रतितिष्ठति देवं देवत्रा सूरमगन्मज्योतिरुत्तममिति स्वर्गो वै लोकः सूरो ज्योतिरुत्तमग्ग् स्वर्ग एव लोकेऽंततः प्रतितिष्ठति (*udvayaṃ tamasasparīti pāpmā vai tamaḥ pāpmānameva tamo 'pahate svaḥ paśyaṃta uttaramityayaṃ vai loko 'ddhya uttaro 'sminneva loke pratitiṣṭhati devaṃ devatrā sūramaganmajyotiruttamamiti svargo vai lokaḥ sūro jyotiruttamagg svarga eva loke 'ṃtataḥ pratitiṣṭhati*)
(Śa. Brā. 14-3-1-28)
Sūra, the most brilliant of all the shining gods, is himself the world of the atmosphere (antarikṣa). Since he is eternally established in the atmosphere, there is complete unity between him and that world. Since identity is stated thus, whatever sense there is in stating a conjugal relation between Āditya and Earth, the same sense there is in stating a conjugal relation between Earth and the atmosphere. Therefore,

अथ यत्राहोपहूते द्यावापृथिवी इति । तदग्नीध आदधाति तदग्नीत्पाश्नात्युपहूता पृथिवी मातोप मां पृथिवी माता ह्वयतामग्नि राग्नीध्राहोपहूतो द्यौष्टितोप मां द्यौष्टिता ह्वयतामग्नि राग्नीध्रात्स्वाहेति द्यावा पृथिव्यो वाएष यदाग्नीध्रः (*atha yatrāhopahūte dyāvāpṛthivī iti | tadagnīdha ādadhāti tadagnītpāśnātyupahūtā pṛthivī mātopa māṃ pṛthivī mātā hvayatāmagni rāgnīdhrāhopahūto dyauṣṭitopa māṃ dyauṣṭitā hvayatāmagni rāgnīdhrātsvāheti dyāvā pṛthivyo vāeṣa yadāgnīdhraḥ*)
(Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-41)

### Printed p. 340
*Running head: 340 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

When the Hotṛ recites “Heaven and Earth have been invoked here” and hands over to the Āgnīdhra, the Āgnīdhra says: “Earth, the mother, has been invoked here; may she likewise invite me too; since I have taken the Āgnīdhra seat, I am Agni himself. Likewise the father, the deity of the heaven-world and so on, has been invoked.” In this way, Heaven and Earth are indicated as father and mother in many places. In such contexts “father” may mean the heaven-world, or Āditya who abides in the heaven-world. For example—

पिता नोऽसि पिता नो बोधीति । एष वै पिता य ! एष तपत्येष उ प्रवर्ग्यः (*pitā no 'si pitā no bodhīti | eṣa vai pitā ya ! eṣa tapatyeṣa u pravargyaḥ*) *[as supplied: the text has य ! (*ya !*) before एष तपत्येष (*eṣa tapatyeṣa*)]*
(Śa. Brā. 14-1-4-15)
“You are our father. Be our father. Lo, the Āditya who shines in the atmosphere is our father, and the Pravargya is Āditya”—thus Āditya, who abides in the atmosphere, is indicated as the father, and so on.

In this way the conjugal love, prior in time, of the two who are the mother and father of the creatures of the world is described in the present Ṛk. In many contexts even worldly couples are accustomed to compare themselves to Heaven and Earth and to describe their ultimate relationship. For example—

द्यौरहं पृथिवी त्वं तावेहि संरंभावहै (*dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ tāvehi saṃraṃbhāvahai*)
(Bṛ. U. 6-4-20)
द्यौरहं पृथिवी त्वग्ं रेतोऽहग्ं रेतोभृत्त्वं (*dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvagṃ reto 'hagṃ retobhṛttvaṃ*) .... .... .... ।
(Tai. Ekāgni-kāṇḍa 1-3)
“We two are Heaven and Earth; let us two come together and strive for the begetting of offspring”—thus the husband says, addressing his wife. In this way in many places the conjugal relation of the Āditya-world and Earth is described. These two, the primal couple, are the father and mother of the world. Of them it is said that the mother served the father with धीति (*dhīti*).

धीत्या (*dhītyā*)—यागादिरूपेण कर्मणा (*yāgādirūpeṇa karmaṇā*); that is, by rites in the form of sacrifice etc. The word धीति (*dhīti*) has two meanings, कर्म (*karma*) (rite) and प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*) (insight). [In the Nirukta (Ni. 3-8) this word is also read among the names of the fingers.] The author of the Nirukta has cited two Ṛks in which the two meanings, rite and insight, occur.

सारावतघ्नीमवसे सुवृक्तिभिः सरस्वतीमा विवसेम धीतिभिः (*sārāvataghnīmavase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīmā vivasema dhītibhiḥ*) ।
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-61-2)
In this Ṛk धीतिभिः (*dhītibhiḥ*) is explained as कर्मभिः (*karmabhiḥ*), and in

ऋतस्य हि शुरुधः संति पूर्वीर्यतस्य धीतिर्वृजिनानि हंति (*ṛtasya hi śurudhaḥ saṃti pūrvīryatasya dhītirvṛjināni haṃti*) ॥
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-23-8) *(the sentence continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 341
*Running head: [ಆ. ೨. ಆ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫ ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 341 (as supplied; "ಆ" stands for "ಅ." here).*

...here it is explained as प्रज्ञा (*prajñā*). In some places this word is also used in the sense of praise. In the present Ṛk it means a rite in the form of sacrifice.

गर्भरसा (*garbharasā*)—गर्भोत्पत्ति निमित्तेन रसेन निविधा नितरां विद्या असीत् (*garbhotpatti nimittena rasena nividhā nitarāṃ vidyā asīt*) *[as supplied: निविधा (*nividhā*); the bhāṣya has निविद्धा (*nividdhā*)]*. Explaining that she became completely united with the sap that is the means of the origin of the embryo, Sāyaṇa has said:
गर्भे रसः ओषध्याद्युत्पादनसमर्थमुदकं यस्याः सा तादृशी उदकेन अत्यंतं क्लिन्ना निविद्धा कृषीवलैर्हलमुखेन नितरां विदारिता भवति (*garbhe rasaḥ oṣadhyādyutpādanasamarthamudakaṃ yasyāḥ sā tādṛśī udakena atyaṃtaṃ klinnā nividdhā kṛṣīvalairhalamukhena nitarāṃ vidāritā bhavati*) ।
that is, having held in her womb the water that is the means of the origin of plants, herbs and so on—that is, after the whole earth has been drenched with that water—she is ploughed by the farmers and made ready for procreation in the form of crop-wealth.

उपवाकं (*upavākaṃ*)—this word has been explained in two ways. First, उपेत्य वचनं परस्परं सम्यगभिवृद्धानि सस्यानीति वचनं (*upetya vacanaṃ parasparaṃ samyagabhivṛddhāni sasyānīti vacanaṃ*) ("coming near and saying to one another: 'the crops have grown well'"). When kinsmen or friends meet one another, all the people also express their joy over the growth of crops and the increase of fruit-wealth, and in addition speak words of congratulation. This is generally a worldly expression of joy in the form of an upavacana (a "saying-to").

उदू अयां उपवक्तेव बाहू हिरण्यया सविता सुप्रतीका । दिवो रोहांस्यरुहत्पथिव्या अरीरमत्पतयत्कच्चिदभ्वं (*udū ayāṃ upavakteva bāhū hiraṇyayā savitā supratīkā | divo rohāṃsyaruhatpathivyā arīramatpatayatkaccidabhvaṃ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-21-5) *[as supplied: पथिव्या (*pathivyā*)]*
Here the attractive spreading of the rays of Savitṛ is compared to a worldly expression of joy: as a friend, to show his satisfaction at his friend's prosperity, raises his hands and congratulates him, so may he too rise with the spreading of his rays—so it is described. This amounts to stating the nature of the worldly upavāka.

Besides this, there is also the recitation of a mantra, the so-called upavacana, which is part of a rite. That this meaning too is possible here, Sāyaṇa has said:
हनिर्लक्षणान्नवंतः उपेत्य वचनं प्रैषादिरूपमीयुः । वृष्टौ सत्यां सस्यादिद्वारा यागमनुतिष्ठेयुरित्यर्थः (*hanirlakṣaṇānnavaṃtaḥ upetya vacanaṃ praiṣādirūpamīyuḥ | vṛṣṭau satyāṃ sasyādidvārā yāgamanutiṣṭheyurityarthaḥ*) ॥
that is, after the fall of the rain the plants and so on grow, and when they approach the time of fruit, obtaining food in the form of oblation and performing the sacrifice, they recited mantras such as the praiṣa. This praiṣa mantra has to be recited by one of the ṛtviks. Which of them it is cannot be stated precisely. Because,

वेषि ह्यध्वरीयतामुपवक्ता जनानां । हव्या च मानुषाणां (*veṣi hyadhvarīyatāmupavaktā janānāṃ | havyā ca mānuṣāṇāṃ*) ।
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-9-5) *(the discussion continues in the next window)*

### Printed p. 342
*Running head: 342 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪]] (as supplied; with a doubled closing bracket).*

[Continuing from the previous page:] In the Ṛk (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-9-5), in explaining the word उपवक्ता (*upavaktā*), Sāyaṇa has said:
उपवक्ता, अध्वर्युप्रभृतीनां सर्वेषां कर्मणामनुज्ञार्थं “ मां प्रणय ” इत्यादि रूपस्य वाक्यस्य वक्ता सन् ब्रह्मा चासि (*upavaktā, adhvaryuprabhṛtīnāṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāmanujñārthaṃ “ māṃ praṇaya ” ityādi rūpasya vākyasya vaktā san brahmā cāsi*) ॥
that is, uttering sentences such as “मां प्रणय (*māṃ praṇaya*)” (“lead me forth”), he is Brahmā, who gives permission to the rites of all the ṛtviks beginning with the Adhvaryu. Hence it is understood from this that the one who speaks the upavacana is Brahmā. Or,
उपवक्ता सर्वेषां कर्मणामनैकल्यार्थमुपद्रष्टा वा सदस्योऽसि । “ स हि सप्तदशः कर्मणामुपद्रष्टा भवति ” ॥ इत्यापस्तंबेनोक्तत्वात् (*upavaktā sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāmanaikalyārthamupadraṣṭā vā sadasyo 'si | “ sa hi saptadaśaḥ karmaṇāmupadraṣṭā bhavati ” ‖ ityāpastaṃbenoktatvāt*) ॥
that is, the seventeenth member of the assembly, who sees that all the rites are carried out without deficiency and without obstacle, is the upadraṣṭṛ (overseer). Āpastamba has stated his characteristic with “सप्तदशः कर्मणामुपद्रष्टा भवति (*saptadaśaḥ karmaṇāmupadraṣṭā bhavati*)”. Explaining the nature of this upadraṣṭṛ, the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa says thus:
ब्राह्मणो दक्षिणत उपास्ते । ब्राह्मणो वै प्रजानामुपद्रष्टा । उपद्रष्टुमत्येव प्रजायते (*brāhmaṇo dakṣiṇata upāste | brāhmaṇo vai prajānāmupadraṣṭā | upadraṣṭumatyeva prajāyate*) ॥
(Tai. Brā. 2-2-1-3)
In explaining the word उपद्रष्टृ (*upadraṣṭṛ*) in this sentence, Sāyaṇa has said उपद्रष्टृ हिताहितस्य प्रजानामुपदेष्टृ (*upadraṣṭṛ hitāhitasya prajānāmupadeṣṭṛ*): the member of the assembly who, seeing that there is no deficiency in the rites, tells everyone what is beneficial and what is harmful. In the explanation of the Ṛk cited here (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-9-5), identity of the upavaktṛ and the upadraṣṭṛ is stated. Again, in what is said in the Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa,
प्रजापतिरकामयत प्रजाः सृजेयेति । स एतं दशहोतारमपश्यत् (*prajāpatirakāmayata prajāḥ sṛjeyeti | sa etaṃ daśahotāramapaśyat*) ॥
(Tai. Brā. 2-2-1-1)
Sāyaṇa, in naming the ten hotṛs *[as supplied: दशमोतृगळन्नु (*daśamotṛgaḷannu*)]*, cites this mantra of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka:
चित्तिः स्रुक्, चित्तमाज्यं, वाग्वेदिः, आधीतं बर्हिः, केतो अग्निः, विज्ञातमग्निः वाक्प्रतिर्होता, मन उपवक्ता (*cittiḥ sruk, cittamājyaṃ, vāgvediḥ, ādhītaṃ barhiḥ, keto agniḥ, vijñātamagniḥ vākpratirhotā, mana upavaktā*) .... .... .... .... ॥
and explains: उपवक्तृशब्देनानुवचनकर्तुर्होतुः पुरा प्रैषवक्ता मैत्रावरुणो विवक्षितः (*upavaktṛśabdenānuvacanakarturhotuḥ purā praiṣavaktā maitrāvaruṇo vivakṣitaḥ*)—that is, by the word upavaktṛ is meant the Maitrāvaruṇa, who in front of the Hotṛ, his assistant, recites the praiṣa (the Hotṛ being the one who recites the anuvacana). He has explained that in front of the Hotṛ his assistant the Maitrāvaruṇa recites the upavacana. Thus, if in the present Ṛk it is the recitation of a mantra forming part of a rite, then it is the upavacana-mantra recited by Brahmā, by the upadraṣṭṛ or by the Maitrāvaruṇa; or else it is a word of congratulation.

### Printed p. 343
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 343 (as supplied).*

*Grammatical process (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)*

बभाज (*babhāja*)—the root भज सेवायां (*bhaja sevāyāṃ*). By छंदसि लुज् लज् लिटः (*chaṃdasi luj laj liṭaḥ*) [as supplied] liṭ in the sense of the present. A form ending in the third person singular. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.

धीती (*dhītī*)—when the instrumental singular follows, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-139) [as supplied] the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding vowel comes (the sentence is printed with a stray full stop: "ಬರುತ್ತದೆ.").

संजग्मे (*saṃjagme*)—the root गम्‌ल्य गतौ (*gamlya gatau*) [as supplied]. By समो गम्यृच्छिभ्याम् (*samo gamyṛcchibhyām*) (Pā. Sū. 1-3-29) it takes ātmanepada. Vedic liṭ, a form ending in the third person singular. By हिच (*hica*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-34) the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes, so that by the suffix accent it becomes final-udātta.

बीभत्सुः (*bībhatsuḥ*)—when san comes in the sense of desire, after the san-ending stem, by सनाशंसभिक्ष उः (*sanāśaṃsabhikṣa uḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-164) the suffix u. By अतो लोपः (*ato lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-48) the vowel a of the san (सनिन (*sanina*) [as supplied]) is dropped. By the suffix accent it becomes final-udātta.

गर्भरसा (*garbharasā*)—गर्भस्य रसः तेन (*garbhasya rasaḥ tena*). By सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*)—(Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) when the instrumental case ending follows, the substitute ā for it. Or गर्भे रसः यस्याः सा (*garbhe rasaḥ yasyāḥ sā*), गर्भरसा (*garbharasā*). By बहुव्रीहौप्रकृत्यापूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhauprakṛtyāpūrvapadam*) the first member keeps its natural accent.

निविद्धा (*nividdhā*)—the root व्यध ताडने (*vyadha tāḍane*). In the passive, by निष्ठा (*niṣṭhā*) the suffix kta. By ग्रहिज्यावयिव्यधि- (*grahijyāvayivyadhi-*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-16) saṃprasāraṇa. By the sūtra न संप्रसारणे संप्रसारणम् (*na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam*) the letter y is replaced by i. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the gati (ni) takes the udātta accent.

नमस्वंतः (*namasvaṃtaḥ*)—नमः अन्नादि येषामस्ति इति (*namaḥ annādi yeṣāmasti iti*). By the sūtra तदस्यास्ति (*tadasyāsti*) the suffix matup. By मादुपधायाश्च (*mādupadhāyāśca*) the m is replaced by v. Because the suffix is pit, it becomes anudātta.

उपवाकम् (*upavākam*)—the root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*), the suffix ghañ. By अतउपधायाः (*ataupadhāyāḥ*) vṛddhi of the penultimate. By चजोः कुघिण्यतोः (*cajoḥ kughiṇyatoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-52) the guttural substitution (kutva). By कर्षात्वतः— (*karṣātvataḥ—*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-159) the final-udātta accent comes. When it is a prādi compound, the accent of the kṛdut­tarapada (the final member keeps its natural accent) comes.

ईयुः (*īyuḥ*)—the root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) [as supplied]. Vedic liṭ in the present sense. A form ending in the third person plural. Because it does not stand after a finite verb *[as supplied: अतिजंतव (*atijaṃtava*) for "ತಿಜಂತ"]*, the nighāta accent comes. ॥ 8 ॥

> *yuktā | mātā | āsīt | dhuri | dakṣiṇāyāḥ | atiṣṭhat | garbhaḥ | vṛjanīṣu | aṃtariti |*
> *amīmet | vatsaḥ | anu | gāṃ | a pa śya t | viśvarūpyaṃ | triṣu | yojaneṣu ‖ 9 ‖*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> माता । निर्मियंतेऽस्मिन्भूतानीति माता द्यौः । दक्षिणाया अभिमतपूरणसमर्थायाः पृथिव्या धुरि निर्वहणे युक्तासीत् । वर्षणाय समर्थाभूदित्यर्थः ।
> कथमिति तदुच्यते । गर्भो गर्भस्थानीय उदकसंघो वृजनीषूदकवत्तु मेघपंक्तिष्टंतर्मध्यॆऽतिष्ठत् । तिष्ठति । अनंतरं वत्सः पुत्रस्थानीय उदकसंघस्तिषु
> योजनेषु मेघरश्मिवायुषु संयुक्तेषु सत्स्वमीमेत् । वर्षणसमये
> शब्दयति । अनंतरं विश्वरूप्यं विश्वरूपवतीं गामन्वपश्यत् । अनुक्रमेण पश्यति ।
> वर्षतीत्यर्थः । यद्वा । त्रिषु योजनेषु सत्तु वत्सो मेघो वर्षणाय गां
> भूमिं प्रत्यमीमेत् । अनंतरं सर्वो जनोऽनुक्रमेण विश्वरूप्यं सस्यादिभिर्नानारूपवतीं भूमिमपश्यत् । पश्यति ॥

*Gist:* Heaven the mother is yoked to earth's burden; the water-embryo rests in the clouds; the calf thunders and beholds multiform earth: rain falls.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
माता (*mātā*)—the heaven-world, maker of all; दक्षिणायाः (*dakṣiṇāyāḥ*)—of the earth, which is capable (of fulfilling desired ends); धुरि (*dhuri*)—in the carrying out of the duty in the form of protection; युक्ता आसीत् (*yuktā āsīt*)—was appointed. गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—the mass of water that is in the place of the embryo; वृजनीषु (*vṛjanīṣu*)—in the rows of clouds filled with waters; अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—in the middle; अतिष्ठत् (*atiṣṭhat*)—has settled. वत्सः (*vatsaḥ*)—the mass of water that is in the place of the son; त्रिषु योजनेषु (*triṣu yojaneṣu*)—when cloud, wind and ray are joined together; अमीमेत् (*amīmet*)—makes the sound of thunder (and then); विश्वरूप्यं (*viśvarūpyaṃ*)—possessed of many kinds of forms; गां (*gāṃ*)—to the earth; अनु अपश्यत् (*anu apaśyat*)—in order pours down rain.

### Printed p. 345
*Running head: [ಆ.೨.ಅ. ೩ ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 345 (as supplied).*

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Heaven, the mother of all, is appointed to the duty of protecting the earth, which is capable of fulfilling desired ends. The mass of water that is in the place of the embryo has settled in the middle of the rows of clouds filled with waters. When the mass of water that is in the place of the son, the cloud, the wind and the ray are joined together, it makes the sound of thunder. After that it pours rain on the earth of many forms.

**Printed English**
The mother, (sky), was associated in (sustaining) the burthen of the fulfiller of desires, (the earth): the embryo (water) rested within the (womb of the) clouds : thereupon the calf bellowed, and beheld the omniform cow in the three combinations.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
In the previous Ṛk the Earth was indicated as mother and Āditya, who abides in the atmosphere, as father. Here the atmosphere is called mother. By this it is shown that both the Earth and the atmosphere have a power of a special kind in the work of creating beings. To show that the Earth undertakes not only the work of creation but also the works of sustaining and protecting, the word दक्षिणायाः (*dakṣiṇāyāḥ*), a synonym of Earth, has been used. Sāyaṇa has explained this word as अभिमतपूरणसमर्थायाः पृथिव्याः (*abhimatapūraṇasamarthāyāḥ pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the Earth, which has the capacity to fulfil what is desired. The Earth has obtained all kinds of wealth and, besides, the power of sustaining. For providing what is desired, both these powers are absolutely necessary.

खं वायुज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी (*khaṃ vāyujyotirāpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī*) ।
(Mu. U. 2-1-3)
In sentences such as this the Earth is described as the sustainer of the world. Moreover,
एषां भूतानां पृथिवी रसः (*eṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ pṛthivī rasaḥ*) ; (Chā. U. 1-1-2)
पृथिवी ना अन्नं (*pṛthivī nā annaṃ*) । (Tai. U. 3-9-1) *[as supplied: ना (*nā*)]*
In sentences such as these, as it is said that all the power that is essential for the existence and nourishment of beings is to be obtained from the Earth alone, the Earth, since it has all kinds of power, has the epithet dhāriṇī (sustainer). The author of the Nirukta too, when stating the etymology of the word दक्षिणा (*dakṣiṇā*), shows this very meaning,

### Printed p. 346
*Running head: 346 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೮೪] (as supplied; the Sūkta number is printed ೮೪, whereas the other pages have ೧೬೪).*

दक्षिणा दक्षतेः समर्धयति कर्मणो व्यृद्धं समर्धयतीति (*dakṣiṇā dakṣateḥ samardhayati karmaṇo vyṛddhaṃ samardhayatīti*) ।
(Ni. 1-2)
[saying that] it is derived from the root दक्स् (*daks*) [as supplied], which gives the meaning of causing complete growth, and he has explained that the meaning “it makes complete what is deficient” is also possible. Since the Earth has all these powers, this epithet shows its power.

वृजनीषु (*vṛjanīṣu*)—उदकवत्तु मेघपंक्तिषु (*udakavattu meghapaṃktiṣu*). Sāyaṇa has explained it as: in the rows of clouds that possess water in abundance. For the ī-ending word वृजनी (*vṛjanī*) the scholar Monier Williams, in his Sanskrit–English Dictionary, first gives the meaning “an enclosure; fold” (āvaraṇa) and then shows that in Sāyaṇa's view the meaning “cloud” (printed ವೇಘ, as supplied) also occurs. Besides, he states that in the Atharvaveda 7-30-7 this word gives the meaning deceit, intrigue.

त्रिषु योजनेषु (*triṣu yojaneṣu*)—मेघरश्मिनायुषु संयुक्तेषु सत्सु (*megharaśmināyuṣu saṃyukteṣu satsu*) *[as supplied: रश्मिनायुषु (*raśmināyuṣu*); the bhāṣya has वायुषु (*vāyuṣu*)]*. To show that, when the cloud, the sun's ray and the wind were joined together, there was the sound of thunder, it is described: अमीमेत् वर्षणसमये शब्दयति (*amīmet varṣaṇasamaye śabdayati*)—it sounded at the time of the fall of rain.

विश्वरूप्यं अपश्यत् (*viśvarūpyaṃ apaśyat*)—two kinds of meaning are given for this. First, विश्वरूपवतीं गां अनुक्रमेण पश्यति (*viśvarūpavatīṃ gāṃ anukrameṇa paśyati*): the water in the form of the calf looks in order at the Earth of many forms; that is, the rain falls in order and reaches the Earth. And second,
त्रिषु योजनेषु सत्तु वत्सो मेघो वर्षणाय गां भूमिं प्रति अमीमेत् । जनः क्रमेण विश्वरूप्यं सस्यादिभिर्नानारूपवतीं भूमिमपश्यत् पश्यति (*triṣu yojaneṣu sattu vatso megho varṣaṇāya gāṃ bhūmiṃ prati amīmet | janaḥ krameṇa viśvarūpyaṃ sasyādibhirnānārūpavatīṃ bhūmimapaśyat paśyati*) ।
that is, after the cloud, the wind and the sun's ray had been joined together, the cloud in the form of the calf made the sound of thunder that precedes the fall of rain. Immediately rain falls, and all the people, seeing the earth shining with plants of many kinds and with the varied colours of those plants, rejoice—so it is described in another way too.

On the whole, having stated earlier the original nature of Heaven-and-Earth as the mother and father of all beings, this Ṛk explains the point that they nourish the world that has come into being by providing it with wealth in the form of food. The matter that the union of Heaven and Earth is in one way or another present for the origin, the sustaining and the nourishment of the universe and of everything is stated clearly.

### Printed p. 347
*Running head: [ಅ ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 347 (as supplied).*

*Grammatical process (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)*

युक्ता (*yuktā*)—the root युजिर् योगे (*yujir yoge*). The suffix kta. By चोःकुः (*coḥkuḥ*) kutva for the j of the root. By the suffix accent it becomes final-udātta. In the feminine, because it ends in a, ṭāp.

दक्षिणाया (*dakṣiṇāyā*)—the root दक्ष वृद्धौ (*dakṣa vṛddhau*). By द्रुदक्षिभ्यामिनन् (*drudakṣibhyāminan*) (U. Sū. 2-208) the suffix inan. By the sūtra अट् कुप्वाज्— (*aṭ kupvāj—*) ṇatva for the n of the suffix. By इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-169) the initial-udātta accent comes.

अतिष्ठत् (*atiṣṭhat*)—the root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*). Vedic laṅ in the present sense, a form ending in the third person singular. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. Because the augment aṭ is udātta, it becomes initial-udātta.

वृजनीषु (*vṛjanīṣu*)—the root वृजी वर्जने (*vṛjī varjane*). By कृष्णवृजि (*kṛṣṇavṛji*) (U. Sū. 2-239) the suffix kyu. By युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) the substitute ana for it. Because it is kit, the guṇa of a light penultimate does not come. In the feminine, jīp. A form ending in the locative.

अमीमेत् (*amīmet*)—the root मी गतौ (*mī gatau*), of the curādi class. ṇic comes optionally. Vedic laṅ. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) the substitute śLu for śap. Because of śLu, doubling etc. of the root. The augment aṭ to the stem. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. It becomes initial-udātta.

विश्वरूपम् (*viśvarūpam*)—when the accusative singular follows, Vedic yaṇ substitution. By उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः— (*udāttasvaritayoryaṇaḥ—*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) the svarita accent comes on the anudātta case ending. ॥ 9 ॥

### Printed p. 348
*Running head: 348 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied; "ಆ." stands for "ಅ." here).*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> तिस्रः । मात्याः । त्रीन् । पित्र्यन् । बिभ्रत् । एकः । ऊर्ध्वः । तस्थौ । न । ईं । अव ।
> ग्लपयंति ।
> मंत्रयंते । दिवः । अमुष्य । पृष्ठे । विश्वविदं । वाचं । अविश्वमिन्वां ॥ १० ॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> एकः प्रधानभूतोऽसहायो वा पुत्रस्थानीय आदित्यः संवत्सराख्यः कालो
> ना तिस्रो मात्यः सस्यवृष्टाद्युत्पादयित्रिः । क्षित्यादिलोकत्रयमित्यर्थः । तथा
> श्रीन्पित्यज्जगतां पालयित्कल्लोकत्रयाभिमानिनोऽग्निवायुसूर्याख्यान्बिभ्रत्
> सन्नूर्ध्वस्तस्थौ । उन्नतोऽत्यंतदीर्घस्तिष्ठति भूतभविष्यदाद्यात्मना । सूर्यपक्षे
> सर्वेभ्यः उन्नतः । ईमेनं नाव ग्लपयंति । ग्लानिं नैव कुर्वंति । न हि काल
> आदित्यो नान्येन पराभूयते । दिवः पृष्टे द्युलोकस्योपर्यंतरिक्षे मंत्रयंते । गुप्तं परस्परं भाषंते देवाः । किं । विश्वविदं विश्ववेदनसमर्थां विश्वैर्वेदनीयां नाविश्वमिन्वामसर्वव्यापिनीं वाचं गर्जितलक्षणां । अमुष्यादित्यस्य
> संबंधिनीं मंत्रयंत इत्यर्थः ॥

*Gist:* Āditya, as time, stands alone aloft, bearing three worlds and their deities; none can weary him; gods speak his thundering word above heaven.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
एकः (*ekaḥ*)—Āditya, who is the chief of (everything), or (time, called the year); तिस्रः मात्र्याः (*tisraḥ mātryāḥ*)—the three worlds beginning with the earth, which are the producers of crops, rain and so on, त्रीन् पित्र्यन् (*trīn pitryan*)—and also Agni, Vāyu and Sūra (printed ಸೂರ), who are the protectors of the world and the presiding deities of the three worlds; बिभ्रत् (*bibhrat*)—bearing; ऊर्ध्वः (*ūrdhvaḥ*)—high (above everything) or long; तस्थौ (*tasthau*)—stands. (Or: exists.) ईं (*īṃ*)—this Āditya (or time); न अव ग्लपयंति (*na ava glapayaṃti*)—no one can make wane; दिवः पृष्ठे (*divaḥ pṛṣṭhe*)—on the upper part of the heaven-world; अमुष्य (*amuṣya*)—concerning this Āditya (or concerning time); विश्वमिदं (*viśvamidaṃ*) *[as supplied; the Pada-pāṭha has विश्वविदं (*viśvavidaṃ*)]*—which is understood by all; अविश्वमिन्वां (*aviśvaminvāṃ*)—(but) not applicable to all; वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—a proclamation in the form of praise; (देवाः (*devāḥ*)—the gods); मंत्रयंते (*maṃtrayaṃte*)—recite.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Āditya, the chief of everything, bearing the three worlds beginning with the earth, which are the producers *[as supplied: उक्षादकरागिरतक्क (*ukṣādakarāgiratakka*)]* of crops, rain and so on, and also Agni, Vāyu and Sūra, who are the protectors of the world and the presiding deities of the three worlds, is in the highest region of all. No one can make this Āditya wane. On the upper part of the heaven-world, the gods recite a proclamation in the form of praise, directed to this Āditya, understood by all but

### Printed p. 349
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫. ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 349 (as supplied).*

not applicable to all. [This is also how the purport with reference to time is to be stated.]

**Printed English**
The one sole (sun), having three mothers and three fathers, stood on high : none ever over-weary him : The (gods) on the summit of the sky take counsel respecting him in language all-comprehending, (but) not extending to all

*[as supplied: a garbled label विशेषविवरगळु (*viśeṣavivaragaḷu*) stands here, before the label Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu (Special Topics).]*
**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
This Ṛk can be explained as referring either to Āditya or to time in the form of the year; or, in such contexts, one may show the identity of Āditya and time in the form of the year, and may also show that the place, the nature and the power of the two are one. In many contexts unity of Āditya and time in the form of the year is shown. In some places it is said that Āditya is the cause of time, and in other places, since the movement of Āditya takes place by the law of time, that time itself is the cause of Āditya. In the Maitrāyaṇa-brāhmaṇa-upaniṣad the relation between Āditya and time in the form of the year *[as supplied: वत्सराज्यवाद (*vatsarājyavāda*)]* is stated in this way:
अन्नं सर्वस्य योनिः कालश्चान्नस्य सूरो योनिः कालस्य .... .... .... कालात्स्रवंति भूतानि कालाद्वृद्धिं प्रयांति च । द्वेवाव ब्रह्मणो रूपे कालश्चाकालश्च । य आदित्याद्यः स कालः .... .... .... तस्मात्संवत्सरो वै कालः । पचति भूतानि .... .... .... महात्मनि (*annaṃ sarvasya yoniḥ kālaścānnasya sūro yoniḥ kālasya .... .... .... kālātsravaṃti bhūtāni kālādvṛddhiṃ prayāṃti ca | dvevāva brahmaṇo rūpe kālaścākālaśca | ya ādityādyaḥ sa kālaḥ .... .... .... tasmātsaṃvatsaro vai kālaḥ | pacati bhūtāni .... .... .... mahātmani*) ॥
(Maitrāyaṇī U. 6-14 to 16)
Food is the cause of the state and course of all beings. For food the cause is time, and for time, the sun. The year, which is an object of perception, is the form of time. Through the parts of time the movement of the sun takes place. From this time all beings come into being, and by it all grow. The visible Āditya and the invisible moments and so on are forms of time. For Brahman there are two parts, time and non-time; the time that is prior to Āditya is unbounded and partless. The year itself is the form of this part. From the year all beings are born, grow and dissolve. Therefore the year is Prajāpati, the year is food, Brahman and the Supreme Self.

### Printed p. 350
*Running head: 350 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧, ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪.] (as supplied).*

To show that Āditya, whose self is time, shines as the lord of all the worlds, it is said एकः तस्थौ (*ekaḥ tasthau*). Describing this in the Chāndogya and other works,
आदित्यो ब्रह्मेत्यादेशः (*ādityo brahmetyādeśaḥ*) (Chā. U. 3-19-1) असावादित्यो ब्रह्मेति (*asāvādityo brahmeti*) (Tai. Ā. 2-1)
it is taught that Āditya is the Supreme Brahman. Showing the unity of this Āditya with the year, and describing the power of Āditya, who pervades the three worlds beginning with the earth, the Aitareya Āraṇyaka says thus. According to its description Āditya is at the same time the pervader of the world and the one who has occupied the most excellent heaven-world.
महापुरुष इति यमवोचाम संवत्सर एव प्रध्वंसयन्नन्यानि भूतान्कैक्या भावयन्नन्यानि तस्यैतस्यासावादित्यो रसः ॥ स यश्चायमशरीरः प्रज्ञात्मा यश्चासावादित्य एकमेतदिति विद्यात् । तस्मात्पुरुषं पुरुषं प्रत्यादित्यो भवति । तदप्येतदृषिणोक्तं । चित्रं देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः । आ प्रा द्यावापृथिवी अंतरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थु षश्चेति (*mahāpuruṣa iti yamavocāma saṃvatsara eva pradhvaṃsayannanyāni bhūtānkaikyā bhāvayannanyāni tasyaitasyāsāvādityo rasaḥ ‖ sa yaścāyamaśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaścāsāvāditya ekametaditi vidyāt | tasmātpuruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyādityo bhavati | tadapyetadṛṣiṇoktaṃ | citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | ā prā dyāvāpṛthivī aṃtarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthu ṣaśceti*) ॥
(Ai. Āraṇyaka 3-2-3)
The principle which we indicated as the Great Person, that Great Person is the year. The essence of that year is Āditya. The incorporeal Prajñātman and Āditya are to be understood as one principle. This very thing the sage Kutsa has described in the Ṛk Saṃhitā (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-115-1): “The brilliance, which is the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the face of the gods, has risen and has pervaded the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven-world. This is the self of all the worlds, moving and unmoving.” This same Āditya, “bearing three mothers” तिस्रो मात्मः बिभ्रत् (*tisro mātmaḥ bibhrat*) *[as supplied]*, is described in the Ṛk Saṃhitā in this way:
दिपो धर्ता भुवनस्य प्रजापतिः पिशंगं द्रापिं प्रति मुंचते कविः । निचक्षणः प्रथयन्नापृणन्नुर्वजीजनत्सविता सुम्ममुक्थम् (*dipo dhartā bhuvanasya prajāpatiḥ piśaṃgaṃ drāpiṃ prati muṃcate kaviḥ | nicakṣaṇaḥ prathayannāpṛṇannurvajījanatsavitā summamuktham*) ॥ *[as supplied: दिपो (*dipo*)]*
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-53-2)
न प्रिमिये सवितुर्दैव्यस्य तद्यथा विश्वं भुवनं धारयिष्यति । यत्पृथिव्या वरिमन्ना स्वंगुरिर्वष्मन्पिवः सुवति सत्यमस्य तत् (*na primiye saviturdaivyasya tadyathā viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ dhārayiṣyati | yatpṛthivyā varimannā svaṃgurirvaṣmanpivaḥ suvati satyamasya tat*) ॥
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-54-4)
Āditya in the form of Savitṛ is the supporter of the heaven-world and the earth-world. He pours rain on the earth and the atmosphere and gives all kinds of comforts. No one can hinder the work of this Āditya, who is the supporter of “the whole world”—thus his greatness is praised. In the same way, where it is said त्रीन् पित्थन् (अपि) बिभ्रत् (*trīn pitthan (api) bibhrat*) *[as supplied]*, for the word पित्थन् (*pitthan*) *[as supplied]* the explanation is जगतां पालयित्थन् लोकत्रया (*jagatāṃ pālayitthan lokatrayā*) *[as supplied; the quotation continues on the next page]*

### Printed p. 351
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫.] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 351 (as supplied).*

भिमानिनः अग्निवायुसूर्याख्यान् (*bhimāninaḥ agnivāyusūryākhyān*)—that is, (he bears) Agni, the presiding deity of the earth, Vāyu, the presiding deity of the atmosphere, and Sūrya, the presiding deity of the heaven-world.
त्रिस्र एव देवता इति नैरुक्ताः । अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानो वायुर्वेंद्रो वांतरिक्षस्थानः सूरोद्युस्थानः (*trisra eva devatā iti nairuktāḥ | agniḥ pṛthivīsthāno vāyurveṃdro vāṃtarikṣasthānaḥ sūrodyusthānaḥ*) ॥
(Ni. 7-5)
ब्रह्म वा इदमग्र आसीत् । तद्देवानसृजत । तद्देवान् सृष्टैषु लोकेषु व्यारोहयदस्मिन्नेव लोकेग्निं वायुमंतरिक्षे दिव्येव सूर्यं (*brahma vā idamagra āsīt | taddevānasṛjata | taddevān sṛṣṭaiṣu lokeṣu vyārohayadasminneva lokegniṃ vāyumaṃtarikṣe divyeva sūryaṃ*) ॥
(Śa. Brā. 11-2-3-1)
As is stated in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa that in the beginning Brahman was alone, and afterwards created the gods and established Agni on the earth, Vāyu in the atmosphere and Sūrya in the heaven-world, and as in the statement of the Nirukta, त्रीन् पित्थन् (*trīn pitthan*) is to be explained. The meaning is: bearing all of them, Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya, the protectors of the three worlds, he shines as the sole lord.

नेमव ग्लापयंति (*nemava glāpayaṃti*)—न हि कालः आदित्यो वा अन्येन पराभूयते (*na hi kālaḥ ādityo vā anyena parābhūyate*)—neither time nor Āditya comes under the authority of others. This point,
न यस्येंद्रो वरुणो न मित्रो व्रतमर्यमा न मिनंति रुद्रः । नारातॆयस्तमिदं स्वस्ति हुवे देवं सवितारं नमोभिः (*na yasyeṃdro varuṇo na mitro vratamaryamā na minaṃti rudraḥ | nārātèyastamidaṃ svasti huve devaṃ savitāraṃ namobhiḥ*) ॥
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-38-9)
Neither Indra, nor Varuṇa, nor Mitra, nor Aryaman *[as supplied: ಅರಮ್ಯ]* can resist this work of Āditya in the form of Savitṛ, which consists of universal regulation. And
अस्य हि स्वयशस्तरं सवितुः कच्चन प्रियं । न मिनंति स्वराज्यं (*asya hi svayaśastaraṃ savituḥ kaccana priyaṃ | na minaṃti svarājyaṃ*) ॥
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-82-2)
The fame of this Āditya is extraordinary. The sovereignty of this Āditya, who is dear to all, can be harmed by neither asuras nor gods—thus in many places the greatness of this Āditya, the controller of the universe, is described and praised. Or, applying this very thing to time, it can be explained with reference to it too.

### Printed p. 352
*Running head: 352 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧ ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೦] (as supplied; the Sūkta number is printed ೧೬೦, whereas the other pages have ೧೬೪).*

अमुष्य मंत्रयंते (*amuṣya maṃtrayaṃte*)—आदित्यसंबंधिनीं गर्जितलक्षणां वाचं मंत्रयंते इत्यर्थः (*ādityasaṃbaṃdhinīṃ garjitalakṣaṇāṃ vācaṃ maṃtrayaṃte ityarthaḥ*). That is, they perform a recitation of praise, in the form of a proclamation, that glorifies Āditya. This recitation of mantras in the form of a proclamation is described in the Chāndogya in this way:
अथ यत्तदजायत सोऽसावादित्यस्तं जायमानं घोषा उलूलवोऽनूदतिष्ठन्त्सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामास्तस्मात्तस्योदयं प्रति प्रत्यायनं प्रति घोषा उलूलवोऽनूत्तिष्ठंति सर्वाणि च भूतानि सर्वे च कामाः । स य एतमेवं विद्वानादित्यं ब्रह्मेत्युपास्तेऽभ्याशो ह यदेनं साधवो घोषा आ च गच्छेयुरुप च निम्रेडेरन्निम्रेडेरन् (*atha yattadajāyata so 'sāvādityastaṃ jāyamānaṃ ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūdatiṣṭhantsarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāstasmāttasyodayaṃ prati pratyāyanaṃ prati ghoṣā ulūlavo 'nūttiṣṭhaṃti sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sarve ca kāmāḥ | sa ya etamevaṃ vidvānādityaṃ brahmetyupāste 'bhyāśo ha yadenaṃ sādhavo ghoṣā ā ca gaccheyurupa ca nimreḍerannimreḍeran*) । ಇತಿ ॥
(Bhā. U. 3-19-3, 4) *[as supplied: "ಭಾ. ಉ."]*
Immediately after the manifestation of this Āditya, all beings proclaimed their joy, and all creatures awoke and obtained what they desired. For that reason, at every time of sunrise, a proclamation of this kind invites Āditya. If one, knowing this, worships Āditya as the Supreme Brahman, then for him too this proclamation and its joy will be a continuous cause of joy.
आदित्य इति होवाच सर्वाणि ह वा इमानि भूतान्यादित्यमुच्चैः संतं गायंति सैषा देवतोद्गीथमन्वायत्ता (*āditya iti hovāca sarvāṇi ha vā imāni bhūtānyādityamuccaiḥ saṃtaṃ gāyaṃti saiṣā devatodgīthamanvāyattā*) ॥
(Chā. U. 3.-11-2) *[as supplied]*
When Āditya shines in the most elevated region, all beings gather together and praise Āditya in a loud voice. Āditya is the deity connected with the udgītha *[as supplied: उद्दीथ (*uddītha*)]*, and so on; since there results from Āditya लोपकार (*lopakāra*) *[as supplied]*, at the very sight of him all beings recite words of praise that indicate their joy and gratitude. This matter is stated in the present Ṛk by अमुष्य मंत्रयंते (*amuṣya maṃtrayaṃte*).

विश्वविदं (*viśvavidaṃ*)—this is an adjective of वाचं (*vācaṃ*). It can be taken in two ways: “what is known to all”, or “what is to be known by all”.

अविश्वमिन्वां (*aviśvaminvāṃ*)—the verb इन्वति (*invati*) is read among the names of the act of pervading (Ni. 3.- 10) *[as supplied]*. विश्वमिन्वां (*viśvaminvāṃ*) would mean “what pervades everywhere”. But this praise-recitation in the form of a proclamation applies to Āditya alone. To indicate that this praise cannot apply to any other deities or to others, the adjective अविश्वमिन्वां (*aviśvaminvāṃ*) has been used; if one explains thus,

### Printed p. 353
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೫ ] Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 353 (as supplied).*

it cannot be wrong. Sāyaṇa too has explained it as असर्वव्यापिनीं (*asarvavyāpinīṃ*) and has shown that it is an adjective of वाचं (*vācaṃ*).

Since Sāyaṇa has commented on the word वाचं (*vācaṃ*) as गर्जितलक्षणां (*garjitalakṣaṇāṃ*), the sound of thunder may also be understood here. Then विश्वविदं (*viśvavidaṃ*) means “to be known by all”, because this sound is heard by the whole world; but अविश्वमिन्वां (*aviśvaminvāṃ*) means “not pervading everywhere”, because this sound spreads over only a small part; in this way, it can be said, the nature of this thunder is described.

*Grammatical process (Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā)*

तिस्रः (*tisraḥ*)—the word त्रि (*tri*) (tri). When śas follows, the final-udātta substitute tisṛ. By अचिर ऋतः (*acira ṛtaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-100) yaṇ substitution. By उदात्तस्वरितयोः (*udāttasvaritayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-4) the case ending takes the udātta accent.

बिभ्रत् (*bibhrat*)—the root डुबृञ् भरणे (*ḍubṛñ bharaṇe*) [as supplied]. The substitute śatṛ for laṭ. The śLu vikaraṇa. Taking it as the cause, doubling; by बृञामित् (*bṛñāmit*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-76) i for the abhyāsa. By अभ्यस्तानामादिः (*abhyastānāmādiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-189) the initial-udātta accent comes.

तस्थौ (*tasthau*)—the root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत् (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛt*) [as supplied]. Liṭ, a form ending in the third person singular. Because it stands after a finite verb *[as supplied: अतिजंतद (*atijaṃtada*)]*, the nighāta accent comes.

ग्लपयंति (*glapayaṃti*)—the root ग्लै हर्षक्षये (*glai harṣakṣaye*). By हेतुमति च (*hetumati ca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-26) ṇic. By आदेच उपदेशेशिति (*ādeca upadeśeśiti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-45) ātva for the root. By अर्तिह्रीप्ली- (*artihrīplī-*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-36) the augment puk. In the third person plural of laṭ, the substitute anta for jhi. Because of śap, guṇa and the substitute ay for ṇic. The nighāta accent of a finite verb comes.

मंत्रयंते (*maṃtrayaṃte*)—the root मत्रि गुप्तपरिभाषणे (*matri guptaparibhāṣaṇe*). By इदितो नुम् धातोः (*idito num dhātoḥ*) (Pā. Sū 7-1 58) [as supplied] the augment num. By the sūtra सत्यापपाश- (*satyāpapāśa-*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-25) ṇic in the own sense. A form ending in the third person plural of laṭ. Because it stands at the beginning of a pāda, the nighāta accent does not come. The accent of ṇic remains.

विश्वविदम् (*viśvavidam*)—the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*). विश्वं वेत्ति इति विश्ववित् (*viśvaṃ vetti iti viśvavit*). ताम् (*tām*). By सत्सुद्विषद्रुह- (*satsudviṣadruha-*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-61) the suffix kvip. By गतिकारकोपपदात्‌कृत् (*gatikārakopapadātkṛt*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-139) the accent of the kṛdut­tarapada comes. A form ending in the accusative singular.

अविश्वमिन्वाम् (*aviśvaminvām*)—विश्वमिन्वति व्याप्न्नोति इति विश्वमिन्वा (*viśvaminvati vyāpnnoti iti viśvaminvā*). The root इवि व्याप्तौ (*ivi vyāptau*). By नंदिग्रहपचादिभ्यः- (*naṃdigrahapacādibhyaḥ-*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-134) the suffix ac. इदितो नुम् धातोः (*idito num dhātoḥ*) and by ऎंबु (*èṃbu*) *(the sentence is cut off at the end of the page and continues in the next window; the foot of the page carries the signature mark "[23] [Vol. 12" as supplied)*

### Printed p. 354
*Running head: 354 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

[Continuing the grammatical note on Ṛk 10, word *aviśvaminvām*, from the previous page:] … by the rule quoted above, the augment num is added to the root; in the compound, Vedically, the luk (elision) of the case ending does not occur. Or, the suffix khac comes to this root also *[as supplied: the Kannada reads "ಅಥವಾ ಬಹುವಚನದಿಂದ ಖಚ್ ಪ್ರತ್ಯಯ" — "or from the plural, the suffix khac"; the text is kept as it stands]*. Then the augment mum is added to the preceding member. It is a nañ-tatpuruṣa compound. By तत्पुरुषेतुल्यार्थ (*tatpuruṣetulyārtha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the first member, an indeclinable, comes. A form ending in the accusative singular. || 10 ||

#### Ṛk 11
*[ಸಂಹಿತಾಕಾರರು]* *(garbled label as supplied; repaired by the script to Saṃhitā-pāṭha)*

**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**
> द्वाद॑शारं न॒हि तज्जरा॑य॒ वर्व॑र्ति च॒क्रं परि॒ द्यामृ॒तस्य॑ ।
> आ पु॒त्रा अ॑ग्ने मिथु॒नासो॒ अत्र॑ स॒प्त श॒तानि॑ विंश॒तिश्च॑ तस्थुः ॥
> ॥ ११ ॥

*[ಪವನಾಕ್ಷಿ]* *(garbled label as supplied; repaired by the script to Pada-pāṭha)*

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> द्वादश अरं । नहि । तत् । जराय । वर्वर्ति । चक्रं । परि । द्यां । ऋतस्य ।
> आ । पुत्राः । अग्ने । मिथुनासः । अत्र । सप्त । शतानि । विंशतिः । च । तस्थुः ॥ ११ ॥

*[ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯ C]* *(garbled label as supplied; repaired by the script to Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)*

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> ऋतस्योदकस्य सत्यात्मकस्य वादित्यस्य चक्रं पुनः पुनः क्रमणशीलं मंडलाख्यं रथचक्रं ना वर्वर्ति । पुनःपुनर्वर्तते । संचरति । कुत्र । द्यां परि म्यलोकस्यांतरिक्षस्य परितः । कीदृशं तत् । द्वादशारं द्वादशसंख्याकमेषादिराश्यात्मकैर्मासात्मकैर्नारै रथांगावयवैर्युक्तं । किंच तच्चक्रं नहि जराय नैव खलु जराय्कॆ
> भवति । हे अग्ने सर्वदागमनयुक्तादित्य । यद्वा । अग्नेरेव स्थानत्रये तत्तदात्मना
> वर्तमानत्पादसावप्यग्निरित्युच्यते। आत्रास्मिंस्त्वदीये चक्रे मिथुनासः स्त्रीपुंसरूपेण
> परस्परं मिथुनभूताः सप्त शतानि विंशतिश्च विंशत्युत्तरसप्तशतसंख्याकाः पुत्राः पुत्रवदुत्पद्यमानाः प्राणिनां दुःखात्रातारो वाहोरात्ररूपास्तस्थुः । तिष्यंति । निष्पद्यंते । षष्ठ्यधिकशतत्रयसंख्याकान्यहानि तावत्य एव रात्रय इत्येवं तद्विभागः । सप्त
> च वै शतानि विंशतिश्च संवत्सरस्याहोरात्राः स एषोऽहःसंमानः । ऐ. आ. ३.२-१ ।
> इत्यारण्यकं ॥

*Gist:* The Sun's twelve-spoked wheel of months revolves round the sky without decay; in it stand 720 day-and-night "sons", as the Aitareya Āraṇyaka explains.

*[ಪ್ರತಿಪಾರ್ಥ]* *(garbled label as supplied; repaired by the script to Pratipadārtha)*

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
यतस्य (*yatasya*)—of the Āditya who is of the nature of truth *[as supplied: यतस्य (*yatasya*); the Saṃhitā word is ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)]*; द्वादशारं (*dvādaśāraṃ*)—furnished with spokes in the form of the twelve zodiacal signs, or of the twelve months; चक्रं (*cakraṃ*)—the wheel, which is circular in form; द्यां परि (*dyāṃ pari*) (continued on the next page)

### Printed p. 355
*Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 355 [ಅ. ೨. ಆ. ೩. ವ. ೧೬ ] (as supplied).*

—round the atmosphere (antarikṣa); वर्वर्ति (*varvarti*)—revolves again and again *[as supplied: "ಸುತ್ತುತ್ತಿದೆ"]*; तत् (*tat*)—that wheel; जराय न (*jarāya na*)—is not liable to decay; अग्ने (*agne*)—O Āditya, who art of the nature of Agni; अत्र (*atra*)—in this wheel; मिथुनासः (*mithunāsaḥ*)—joined together with one another; सप्तशतानि विंशतिश्च (*saptaśatāni viṃśatiśca*)—numbering seven hundred and twenty; पुत्राः (*putrāḥ*)—the days and nights, who are of the nature of sons; आ तस्थुः (*ā tasthuḥ*)—stand surrounding (it).

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
The wheel of the Āditya, which is furnished with spokes in the form of the twelve zodiacal signs or the twelve months, and is circular in form, revolves again and again round the atmosphere. That wheel is not liable to decay. O Āditya, who art of the nature of Agni, in this wheel the days and nights, which are joined together with one another, which number seven hundred and twenty, and which are of the nature of sons, stand surrounding it. *[as supplied: the Kannada begins "ದನ್ನೆರಡು" for "ಹನ್ನೆರಡು" (twelve), and ends without a full stop]*

**Printed English**
The twelve-spoked wheel of the true (sun) revolves round the heavens, and never (tends) to decay : seven hundred and twenty children in pairs, Agni. abide in it.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
The description of the Āditya, who, although he possesses an eternal revolving motion in the atmosphere in the form of recurrence, does not decay but keeps perpetual youth, is given in this Ṛk and in the next two Ṛks. The pair of days and nights, which are in the form of couples, which number seven hundred and twenty, and which are as sons to the Āditya, is contained within this wheel of time. This wheel of time, made up of parts such as the ayanas (solstitial courses), continues its revolution without a break. This is the principle of the universe. That this principle is contained in Prajāpati, the creator, is explained in some places; that it is contained in Agni and reflects his external principles, in others. In the present Ṛk the Āditya, the soul of the universe, is addressed as Agni. The identity of this principle of time with the principle of sacrifice is shown, and it is described in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā that Prajāpati, who is of the form of Āditya or of Agni, is the support of both these principles. Since the points mentioned in this Ṛk and in the next two Ṛks are also contained in that description, it will be explained in the Special Topics of the next Ṛk.

*[as supplied: the next paragraph begins "ದಾದಶಾರಂ", a misprint for द्वादशारं (*dvādaśāraṃ*)]* दादशारं (*dādaśāraṃ*)—द्वादशसंख्याकमेषादिराश्यात्मकैः मासात्मकैर्न अरैः रथांगावयवैर्युक्तं (*dvādaśasaṃkhyākameṣādirāśyātmakaiḥ māsātmakairna araiḥ rathāṃgāvayavairyuktaṃ*) (the sentence of the bhāṣya, here taken with the words "ಮಾಸಾತ್ಮಕೈರ್ನ ಅರೈಃ" as printed). The word द्वादशारं (*dvādaśāraṃ*) is an epithet of the word "wheel". Here the orb of the Āditya is compared to the wheel of a chariot, and the twelve months to the spokes of the wheel. The twelve

### Printed p. 356
*Running head: 356 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

signs, Meṣa, Vṛṣabha and the rest, are meant, so that it is understood either as the solar orb having twelve signs or as the revolution of the solar orb having twelve months. Since the days and nights are taken into account here, it fits better if the sense of months is taken. The word "twelve" is also used merely as a synonym of the year, which has twelve months. For example:

देवहितिं जुगुपुद्र्वादशस्य ऋतुं नरो न प्र मिनंत्येते । संवत्सरे प्रावृष्यागतायां तप्ता घर्मा अश्नुवते विसर्ग० (*devahitiṃ jugupudrvādaśasya ṛtuṃ naro na pra minaṃtyete | saṃvatsare prāvṛṣyāgatāyāṃ taptā gharmā aśnuvate visarga0*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-103-9)

In such Ṛks the meaning is, indeed, द्वादशमासात्मकस्य संवत्सरस्य (*dvādaśamāsātmakasya saṃvatsarasya*) "of the year consisting of twelve months". In the present Ṛk also it must be understood in the same way. The author of the Nirukta, too, quotes the pāda द्वादशारं नहि तज्ञराय (*dvādaśāraṃ nahi tajñarāya*) *[as supplied: तज्ञराय (*tajñarāya*); the Saṃhitā block above reads तज्जराय (*tajjarāya*)]* of this Ṛk and the pāda द्वादश प्रधयश्चक्रमेकं (*dvādaśa pradhayaścakramekaṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-48) and explains with इति मासानां (*iti māsānāṃ*) "of the months" that these words for "twelve" are synonyms of months. (Ni. 4-27) Thus the wheel, with its twelve spokes consisting of months, द्यां परि (*dyāṃ pari*)—round the atmosphere, वर्वर्ती (*varvartī*) *[as supplied: ವರ್ವರ್ತೀ]*—undergoes revolution again and again in the form of recurrence; thus it is described, and the Āditya, who is of the nature of such a wheel, is addressed with the epithet अग्ने (*agne*).

अग्ने (*agne*)—Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning to this word. First, in one way, सर्वदा गमनयुक्त आदित्य (*sarvadā gamanayukta āditya*), that is, "O Āditya, whose nature is to move always". Secondly, in another way: अग्नीरेव स्थानत्रये तत्तदात्मना वर्तमानत्वात् असावप्यग्निरित्युच्यते (*agnīreva sthānatraye tattadātmanā vartamānatvāt asāvapyagnirityucyate*) — whether it be the Āditya or the deities such as Vāyu, since it is Agni himself who exists in the several forms in the three places beginning with the earth, the Āditya is here addressed as Agni. It may be said that the first meaning is contained in the second, because Sāyaṇa explains the Āditya as that very Agni who pervades the three places, and the form of Agni pervading the three places is described also in the Bṛhaddevatā and other works. That this threefold existence of Agni, and the threefold manifestation corresponding to it, reflect the fundamental principle of the world, is known from the description of the Bṛhaddevatā:

भवद्भूतस्य भव्यस्य जंगमस्थावरस्य च । अस्यैके सूर्यमेवैकं प्रभवं प्रलयं विदुः ॥ एतद्भूतेषु लोकेषु अग्निभूतं स्थितं त्रिधा । ऋषयो गीर्भिरर्चंति व्यंजितं नामभिस्त्रिभिः (*bhavadbhūtasya bhavyasya jaṃgamasthāvarasya ca | asyaike sūryamevaikaṃ prabhavaṃ pralayaṃ viduḥ ‖ etadbhūteṣu lokeṣu agnibhūtaṃ sthitaṃ tridhā | ṛṣayo gīrbhirarcaṃti vyaṃjitaṃ nāmabhistribhiḥ*)
(Bṛ. Me. 1-61; 1-63) *[as supplied: "ಬೃ. ಮೇ." — elsewhere on the next page "ಬೃ. ದೇ."]*

### Printed p. 357
*Running head: Ṛgveda-saṃhitā 357 [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. .೩ ವ. ೧೬.] (as supplied).*

Prajāpati, the source of all beings, is the origin of creation and dissolution for all moving and unmoving beings existing in the past, the future and the present, and holds his existence in three places, in the form of Agni, in three ways. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā, describing the greatness of Agni and praising him, have thus described how the sages, too, speak of this threefold manifestation of Agni by three names, as seen below:

त्रिस्थानं चैनमर्चंति होत्रायां व्यक्तबर्हिषः । इहैव पवमानोग्निर्मध्यमोग्निर्वनस्पतिः ॥ अमुष्मिन्नेव विप्रैस्तु लोकेग्निशुचिरुच्यते । इहाग्निभूतस्त्वृषिभिर्लोके स्तुतिभिरीळितः ॥ जातवेदाःस्तुतो मध्यॆ स्तुतो वैश्वानरो दिवि (*tristhānaṃ cainamarcaṃti hotrāyāṃ vyaktabarhiṣaḥ | ihaiva pavamānognirmadhyamognirvanaspatiḥ ‖ amuṣminneva vipraistu lokegniśucirucyate | ihāgnibhūtastvṛṣibhirloke stutibhirīḷitaḥ ‖ jātavedāḥstuto madhyè stuto vaiśvānaro divi*)
(Bṛ. De. 1-65 to 67)

Of these three kinds, the Agni who manifests on the earth is known as Pavamāna-agni, पवमानाग्नि (*pavamānāgni*); the Agni in the middle world is known as Vanaspati; and the Agni abiding in the heaven-world as Śuci. These three varieties are recited in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (2-2-4) under the names पवमान शुचि, पावक (*pavamāna śuci, pāvaka*). The author of the Nirukta, quoting the Ṛk of the Ṛk-saṃhitā—

स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनञ्क्तिभी रोदसिप्रां । तमू अकृण्वन् त्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः (*stomena hi divi devāso agnimajījanañktibhī rodasiprāṃ | tamū akṛṇvan tredhā bhuve kaṃ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-10)

—and then तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः (*tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ*), following the explanation of Śākapūṇi, has explained these three forms with examples from Saṃhitā sentences: that in the three places, the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven-world, Agni has manifested in the three forms अग्निः (*agniḥ*), जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*) and वैश्वानर (*vaiśvānara*). (Ni. 7-14 to 7-25.)

Similarly, in some other Ṛks also the manifestation of Agni is explained by the names समुद्रे (*samudre*), दिवि (*divi*) and अप्पु (*appu*), and it is stated that he is seen in the sea as the submarine fire, in the heaven-world as the Āditya, and in the अप्पु (*appu*), that is, in the atmosphere, as lightning. This threefold manifestation of Agni, and his shining in the heaven-world in the form of the Āditya, is described thus in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka and other works:

आपो ना अर्कस्तद्यदपां शर आसीत्तत्समहन्यत । सा पृथिव्यभवत्तस्यामश्राम्यत्तस्य श्रांतस्य तप्तस्य तेजोरसो निरवर्तताग्निः (*āpo nā arkastadyadapāṃ śara āsīttatsamahanyata | sā pṛthivyabhavattasyāmaśrāmyattasya śrāṃtasya taptasya tejoraso niravartatāgniḥ*)

### Printed p. 358
*Running head: 358 Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya-sahitā [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪.] (as supplied: "ಆ." for "ಅ." in the Maṇḍala-Anuvāka position).*

स त्रेधात्मानं व्यकुरतादित्यं तृतीयं वायुं तृतीयं स एष प्राणस्त्रेधा विहितः (*sa tredhātmānaṃ vyakuratādityaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vāyuṃ tṛtīyaṃ sa eṣa prāṇastredhā vihitaḥ*)
(Bṛ. U. 1-2-2-3)

From the water in the form of arka the earth came into being, and from the solidified earth Agni, endowed with great brilliance, was produced. That Agni divided himself into the terrestrial fire, Vāyu and Āditya, and occupied the three places. And again:

सोऽकामयत द्वितीयो म आत्मा जायेतेति स मनसा वाचं मिथुनं समभवदशनाया मृत्युस्तद्यद्रेत आसीत्स संवत्सरोऽभवत् । न ह पुरा ततः संवत्सर आस तमेतावंतं कालमबिभः (*so 'kāmayata dvitīyo ma ātmā jāyeteti sa manasā vācaṃ mithunaṃ samabhavadaśanāyā mṛtyustadyadreta āsītsa saṃvatsaro 'bhavat | na ha purā tataḥ saṃvatsara āsa tametāvaṃtaṃ kālamabibhaḥ*)
(Bṛ. U. 1-2-4)

Thereupon Prajāpati, who is of the form of Agni, desired to have a second, and became united in mind with Vāk. Then that seed became the year. Before that there was no year at all. Thus the relation between Prajāpati in the form of Agni and the year described in the present Ṛk is shown. The parts of this year are explained in the Aitareya Āraṇyaka just as in this Ṛk:

तानि सप्तविंशतिशतानि भवंति सप्त च वै शतानि विंशतिश्च संवत्सरस्याहोरात्राः । स विषोऽहस्समानः (*tāni saptaviṃśatiśatāni bhavaṃti sapta ca vai śatāni viṃśatiśca saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāḥ | sa viṣo 'hassamānaḥ*)
(Ai. Ā. 3-2-1) *[as supplied: "ಇ ಆ. ೩-೨-೧"]*

The total of these is seven hundred and twenty. The reckoning of seven hundred and twenty is stated to be the total number of days and nights in the year. These days and nights are designated in the present Ṛk as sons. Here, for the word "sons", Sāyaṇa has said पुत्रवदुत्पद्यमानाः प्राणिनां दुःखात्त्रातारो वा अहोरात्ररूपाः (*putravadutpadyamānāḥ prāṇināṃ duḥkhāttrātāro vā ahorātrarūpāḥ*), that is, it is understood either as those born like sons, or as days and nights having the power to protect living beings from sorrow.

*Grammar (transcribed, not explained):*
द्वादशारम् (*dvādaśāram*)—a bahuvrīhi: "that which has twelve spokes". By बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्या पूर्वपदम् (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-1) the accent of the first member comes. वर्वर्ति (*varvarti*)—the root वृतु वर्तने (*vṛtu vartane*); by the sūtra धातोरेकाचः (*dhātorekācaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-22) yaṅ; by यजूचि च (*yajūci ca*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-74) its non-causal luk; by सन्यजूः (*sanyajūḥ*) reduplication of the root; by रुग्रिकौच लुकि (*rugrikauca luki*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-91) the augment ruk to the reduplicative syllable (the entry continues on the next page).
