**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> साकंजानामेकस्मादादित्यात्सहोत्पन्नानां सप्तानामृतूनां मध्यॆ सप्तथं
> सप्तममृतुं ॥ थट् च छंदसि । पा- ५-२-५० । इति थट् ॥ एकजमेकेनोत्पन्नमाहुः
> कालतत्त्वविदः । चैत्रादीनां द्वादशानां मासानां द्वयमेलनेन वसंताद्याः षडृतवो भवंति । अधिकमासेनैक उत्पद्यते सप्तमर्तुः । न च तादृशो मास एव नास्तीति
> मंतव्यं । अस्ति त्रयोदशो मास इत्याहुः । तै. सं. ६-५-३-४ । इति श्रुतेः । तदेवोच्यते । षडिद्यमाः । इच्छब्द एवकारार्थः । षडेवर्तवो मासद्वयरूपा ऋषयो
> गंतारः । ते च देवजा देवादादित्याज्ञाता इत्येवमाहुः । सप्तमाधारस्य त्रयोदशस्य मासस्य देवाभावः । निःसूर्योऽधिकमासो मंडलं तपते रवेरित्यादिस्मृतेः
> तस्मात् षडेव देवजाः अदेवज एकः । तेषामृतूनां स्वरूपाणीष्टानि सर्वलोकाभिमतानि धामशस्त्रत्तत्स्थाने विहितानि पृथक् पृथक् स्थापितानि रूपशो रूपभेदेन
> विकृतानि विविधाकृतियुक्तानि । स च रूपभेदस्मैत्तिरीयैराम्नातः । स रसमह
> वसंताय प्रायच्छद्यवं ग्रीष्मायेत्यादि । तै. सं. ७-२-१०.१ । स्थात्रेऽधिष्ठात्रे
> तदर्थाय रेजंते । चलंति । जगद्व्यवहाराय पुनःपुनरावर्तंत इत्यर्थः ॥
*Gist:* Of the seven seasons born together from the sun, the seventh (the intercalary month) is single-born; the six, of two months each, are divine-born, move, and revolve for the world.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
साकंजानां (*sākaṃjānāṃ*)—among the seven seasons produced together (from Āditya); सप्तथं (*saptathaṃ*)—the seventh; एकजं (*ekajaṃ*)—as born single; आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—(the knowers of the truth) have said; षडित् (*ṣaḍit*)—the six seasons only; यमाः (*yamāḥ*)—as composed of two months each; गंतारः (*gaṃtāraḥ*)—as moving; देवजा इति (*devajā iti*)—and as produced from the shining Āditya they have called them; तेषां (*teṣāṃ*)—of those seasons; इष्टानि (*iṣṭāni*)—(approved by all the worlds); धामशः (*dhāmaśaḥ*)—in their respective fixed places; विहितानि (*vihitāni*)—separately established; रूपशः (*rūpaśaḥ*)—endowed with changes of form; विकृतानि (*vikṛtāni*)—the different manifestations; स्थात्रे (*sthātre*)—for the performance of the duty of their lord; रेजंते (*rejaṃte*)—are revolving.

**Bhāvārtha** *[as supplied: the label here is printed ಭಾಷೆ]*
Among the seven seasons produced together from Āditya, the knowers of the truth have said that the seventh is born single. Only the six seasons they have called moving, as composed of two months each, and as produced from the gods. The different manifestations of those seasons, approved by all the worlds, each established separately in its fixed place and endowed with changes of form, are revolving for the welfare of the stable world.

### Printed p. 385
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೬. ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 385 (as supplied).*

**Printed English**
Of those that are born together, sages have called the seventh the single-born ; for six are twins, and are moveable, and born of the gods : their desirable (properties), placed severallay [sic] in ltheir [sic] proper abode, are various (also) in form, and revolve for (the benefit of) that which is stationery [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Describing the nature of the seven seasons, which are produced from Āditya and dependent on Āditya, this Ṛk explains their manifestation and disappearance, in the form of recurrence, which go on for the activity of the world. It also states the difference between the season that is single-born and the seasons that are twin in nature. Sāyaṇa has given a somewhat different meaning to this same mantra in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka. Since one can first understand the explanation given here and then examine the difference in the Āraṇyaka, the purport of this Ṛk is explained according to Sāyaṇa's commentary.

साकंजानां सप्तधं एकजं आहुः—एकस्मादादित्यात् सहोत्पन्नानां सप्तानामृतूनां मध्यॆ सप्तमं ऋतुं एकेन उत्पन्नं आहुः । (*sākaṃjānāṃ saptadhaṃ ekajaṃ āhuḥ—ekasmādādityāt sahotpannānāṃ saptānāmṛtūnāṃ madhyè saptamaṃ ṛtuṃ ekena utpannaṃ āhuḥ |*) *[as supplied: सप्तधं (*saptadhaṃ*) here against सप्तथं (*saptathaṃ*) in the verse]* From Āditya seven seasons in all arise; among them the six seasons are twin in nature (composed of two months each) and born of the gods, while the seventh season only is single-born. How is that? —

चैत्रादीनां द्वादशानां मासानां द्वयमेलनेन वसंताद्याः षडृतवः भवंति । अधिकमासेन एकः उत्पन्नते सप्तमर्तुः । (*caitrādīnāṃ dvādaśānāṃ māsānāṃ dvayamelanena vasaṃtādyāḥ ṣaḍṛtavaḥ bhavaṃti | adhikamāsena ekaḥ utpannate saptamartuḥ |*) In the twelve months beginning with Caitra, taking two and two together, the six seasons beginning with spring come about. The intercalary month is a single one, and this is a season consisting of one month. Having explained thus, he then says न च तादृशो मास एव नास्तीति मंतव्यं (*na ca tādṛśo māsa eva nāstīti maṃtavyaṃ*) : if there is any objection that there is no such month producing a season, it is not right; for:

तस्मादादित्यः षण्मासो दक्षिणेनैति षडुत्तरेणोपयामगृहीतोऽसि सग्ंसर्पोर्स्यग्ंहस्पत्यायत्वेत्याहास्ति त्रयोदशो मास इत्याहुस्तमेव तत्प्रीणाति ॥ (*tasmādādityaḥ ṣaṇmāso dakṣiṇenaiti ṣaḍuttareṇopayāmagṛhīto 'si sagṃsarporsyagṃhaspatyāyatvetyāhāsti trayodaśo māsa ityāhustameva tatprīṇāti ‖*)

(Tai. Saṃ. 6-5-3-4)

Āditya moves for six months to the south and for another six months to the north. "You are Saṃsarpa (this is the name of the intercalary month). You are with a support. Those who know time say that there is a thirteenth month." Therefore in it he indicates his satisfaction; and since there are Śruti sentences of this kind *(the sentence is cut by the page end and continues on p. 386)*

*[stray line as supplied: [25] [ Vol. 12]*

### Printed p. 386
*Running head: 386 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ.೧೬೪.] (as supplied).*

(continuing) ...there is no room for such objections: thus he has resolved the doubt. But, explaining what is the significance of the qualification देवजाः (*devajāḥ*) (born of the gods) for the remaining six seasons, he says सप्तमाधारस्य त्रयोदशस्य मासस्य देवाभावः (*saptamādhārasya trayodaśasya māsasya devābhāvaḥ*) : "निस्सूर्योऽधिकमासो मंडलं तपते रवेः (*nissūryo 'dhikamāso maṃḍalaṃ tapate raveḥ*)" *[as supplied: the bhāṣya above reads निःसूर्यो (*niḥsūryo*) in the corresponding place]*. Since it is stated that the intercalary month is without the sun, the idea is that it is not born of the gods. For ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*) he gives गंतारः (*gaṃtāraḥ*): the meaning is that they are of the nature of going, with the nature of always moving. Commenting on this same mantra in the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka, Sāyaṇa says:

साकंजानानां सहोत्पन्नानामादित्यरश्मीनां मध्ये सप्तथं यः स सप्तमो रश्मिः “ सूरो मरीचिमादत्ते ” इति पूर्वत्रोक्तस्तं सप्तमं रश्मिं एकजमाहुरितररश्मीभ्यः पूर्वमेक एवोत्पन्न इत्यभिज्ञाः कथयंति । (*sākaṃjānānāṃ sahotpannānāmādityaraśmīnāṃ madhye saptathaṃ yaḥ sa saptamo raśmiḥ “ sūro marīcimādatte ” iti pūrvatroktastaṃ saptamaṃ raśmiṃ ekajamāhuritararaśmībhyaḥ pūrvameka evotpanna ityabhijñāḥ kathayaṃti |*)

(Tai. Ā. Sā. Bhā. 1-3)

The knowers say that among the rays produced together from Āditya, the seventh was produced before all the others. Bhaṭṭabhāskara also has stated this same view when commenting on this mantra; explaining the word एकजं (*ekajaṃ*), he says एकत्वेन प्रधानत्वेन जातं सर्वसारभूतं आहुः मंत्रदृशः (*ekatvena pradhānatvena jātaṃ sarvasārabhūtaṃ āhuḥ maṃtradṛśaḥ*) ; he has explained that this ray, the essence of all the other rays, was produced first of all. Both commentators, in order to show proper support for these views of theirs, quote what stands in the Anuvāka preceding this mantra:

एतैरादित्यमंडलं । सर्वैरेव विधास्यते । सूर्यो मरीचिमादत्ते । सर्वस्माद्भुवनावधि । तस्याः पाकविशेषेण । स्मृतं कालविशेषणं । नदीव प्रभवात्काचित् । अक्षय्यात्स्यंदते यथा । (*etairādityamaṃḍalaṃ | sarvaireva vidhāsyate | sūryo marīcimādatte | sarvasmādbhuvanāvadhi | tasyāḥ pākaviśeṣeṇa | smṛtaṃ kālaviśeṣaṇaṃ | nadīva prabhavātkācit | akṣayyātsyaṃdate yathā |*)

(Tai. Ā. 1-2-1 *[as supplied: printed "ತ್ರೈ. ಆ."]*)

Having quoted the sentence that Āditya takes up this Marīci, the essence of all, and through it bestows vigour and the like on all beings, they say that in the present mantra (of the Āraṇyaka) एकजं (*ekajaṃ*) denotes the ray (Marīci). Then, for the sentence षडुद्यमा ऋषयो देवजा इति (*ṣaḍudyamā ṛṣayo devajā iti*) (in the Ṛk-saṃhitā the reading is षडिद्यमा (*ṣaḍidyamā*)), the purport is stated: षड्रश्मयः सप्तमरश्मेरुपसर्जनभूताः (*ṣaḍraśmayaḥ saptamaraśmerupasarjanabhūtāḥ*), that the other six rays *[as supplied: printed "ರತ್ನಿ", for raśmi]* are subordinate to the seventh ray, which is the principal one, and help its work; and ते तु षण्णां ऋतूनां प्रवर्तका (*te tu ṣaṇṇāṃ ṛtūnāṃ pravartakā*) : these six rays are the causes of the six seasons. In the present Ṛk, Sāyaṇa, giving the meaning of षडिद्यमा देवजाः (*ṣaḍidyamā devajāḥ*), says:

इच्छब्दः एवकारार्थः । षडेव ऋतवः मासद्वयरूपाः । देवादादित्याज्ञाताः । (*icchabdaḥ evakārārthaḥ | ṣaḍeva ṛtavaḥ māsadvayarūpāḥ | devādādityājñātāḥ |*)

Only these six seasons, produced from Āditya, are of two months each; the seventh *(the sentence is cut by the end of the window as supplied and continues in the next window)*

### Printed p. 387
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಆ. ೩. ವ. ೧೬.] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 387 (as supplied).*

(Continuing) ...the seventh is not a season (ṛtu): thus the purport is stated. For the latter half the same kind of meaning is given in both places. The purport is that the six seasons produced from these six rays, manifesting themselves also in their fixed places, become helpers in the activities of the world according to the command of Āditya, their presiding lord.

रूपशः विकृतानि (*rūpaśaḥ vikṛtāni*)—रूपभेदेन विविधाकृतियुक्तानि (*rūpabhedena vividhākṛtiyuktāni*) : the meaning is "having different forms". Because there are these differences of form, Sāyaṇa quotes the sentence in which it is stated in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā that gifts and the like suited to the respective seasons are to be made:

सरसमहवसंताय प्रायच्छद्यवं ग्रीष्माय (*sarasamahavasaṃtāya prāyacchadyavaṃ grīṣmāya*) *[as supplied: the first words are printed glued together; the bhāṣya above has them as separate words]*

(Tai. Saṃ. 7-2-10-1, 2)

Here, by prescribing the gift of grain and the like suited to the respective seasons, the variety of forms of the seasons is shown. That even these six seasons, of such manifold forms, stand in aid of their presiding lord and give, each according to its own nature, help in his duties, he who controls the world, is conveyed by the description स्थात्रे रेजंते (*sthātre rejaṃte*).

रेजंते (*rejaṃte*)—चलंति । जगद्व्यवहाराय पुनःपुनरावर्तंते इत्यर्थः (*calaṃti | jagadvyavahārāya punaḥpunarāvartaṃte ityarthaḥ*).

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammatical derivation)*

साकंजानाम् (*sākaṃjānām*)—the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*). By अन्येष्टपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣṭapi dṛśyate*) *[as supplied: so spelt]* (Vā. Sū. 3-2-101) the suffix ḍa. By the force of the ḍit-ness the ṭi is elided; the accent of the prakṛti of the latter member (kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svara) comes. A form ending in the genitive plural, in the sense of determination (nirdhāraṇa).

एकजं (*ekajaṃ*) । देवजाः (*devajāḥ*)—for the root stated before, by पंचम्यामजात् (*paṃcamyāmajāt*) (Pā Sū. 3-2-98) *[as supplied: no full stop after "Pā"]* the suffix ḍa; as before, elision of ṭi, and the kṛd-uttarapada-prakṛti-svara comes.

सप्तथम् (*saptatham*)—सप्तानां पूरणः (*saptānāṃ pūraṇaḥ*); by थट् च छंदसि (*thaṭ ca chaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 5-2-50) the suffix thaṭ in the sense of completion; since the preceding has the name pada, elision of the letter n comes.

ऋषयः (*ṛṣayaḥ*)—the root ऋषी गतौ (*ṛṣī gatau*). By इगुपधात् कित् (*igupadhāt kit*) (Uṇ. Sū. 4-559) the suffix in. By the prescription of kit the guṇa of the laghūpadha does not come. By इत्यादिर्नित्यम् (*ityādirnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-169) the ādyudātta accent comes. A form ending in the nominative plural.

स्थात्रे (*sthātre*)—the root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*). In the active, the suffix tṛc; since it is cit, it becomes antodātta. A form ending in the dative singular.

*Running head: 388 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

रेजंते (*rejaṃte*)—the root रेजृ कंपने (*rejṛ kaṃpane*). A form ending in the third person plural of लट् (*laṭ*). Because it stands after a non-finite word *[as supplied: printed ಅತಿಜಂತ]*, the nighāta accent comes.

विहितानि (*vihitāni*)—the root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*). When the niṣṭhā suffix follows, by दधातेर्हिः (*dadhāterhiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-42) the substitution hi. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent comes on the gati (vi).

रूपशः (*rūpaśaḥ*)—by संख्यैकवचनाच्च वीप्सायां (*saṃkhyaikavacanācca vīpsāyāṃ*) (Pā. Sū, *[as supplied: comma]* 5-4-43) the suffix śas in the sense of repetition. By तद्धितश्चासर्वविभक्तिः (*taddhitaścāsarvavibhaktiḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 1-1-38) it obtains the name avyaya. (End of Ṛk 15; printed ‖ 15 ‖.)

> मंत्रकृदिति । तां. १३-२-२४ । मंत्रद्रष्टुदेव किल पितृत्वं तत्त्ववित् पितुः पितासदिति
> किमाश्चर्यमित्यभिप्रायः ॥
*Gist:* The rays, called women, are called men by the knowers; the seer perceives it, the blind man not; the wise son who knows these becomes the father of the father.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
मे (*me*)—these rays belonging to me; स्त्रियः सतीः (*striyaḥ satīḥ*)—although they are in the female form through bearing the embryo in the form of water; तान् उ (*tān u*)—those very ones; पुंसः (*puṃsaḥ*)—(because they pour out the water in the form of rain) by the designation "males"; आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—they call (this hidden secret); अक्षण्वान् (*akṣaṇvān*)—the great one endowed with the eye of knowledge; पश्यति (*paśyati*)—understands; अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*)—he who, lacking that eye of knowledge, is like a blind man; न वि चेतत् (*na vi cetat*)—cannot understand; यः (*yaḥ*)—who; कविः पुत्रः (*kaviḥ putraḥ*)—is a sage son; सः (*saḥ*)—he alone; ईं (*īṃ*)—this secret; आ चिकेत (*ā ciketa*)—understands; यः (*yaḥ*)—who; ता (*tā*)—all those; विजानात् (*vijānāt*)—understands with the special knowledge (of each thing) *(the entry continues on the next page)*

### Printed p. 390
*Running head: 390 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ಮಂ. ೧ ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

*(continuing)* सः (*saḥ*)—he; पितुः (*pituḥ*)—of the rays that protect the world; पिता (*pitā*)—the father, Āditya himself; असत् (*asat*)—becomes.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Although these rays belonging to me are in the female form through bearing the embryo in the form of water, they are called by the designation "males" because they pour out the water in the form of rain. This hidden secret is understood only by the great one endowed with the eye of knowledge. He who, lacking that eye of knowledge, is like a blind man, cannot understand it. He who is a sage son understands this secret. He who understands all those, with the special knowledge of each thing, becomes the father of the rays that protect the world, namely Āditya himself.

**Printed English**
They have called these, my virtuous females, males : he who hss [sic] eyes beholds ; the blind man sees not : he who is a sage son understands this, and he who discriminates is the father of the father.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**

Since both kinds of meaning, the one relating to the deities (adhidaivata) and the one relating to the Self (adhyātma), are contained in this mantra, Sāyaṇa has given it two kinds of meaning. First, explaining the worldly meaning, he has explained the physical nature of the rays.

शीर्ष्णः क्षीरं दुह्रते गावो अस्य वन्रिं वसाना उदकं पदापुः । (*śīrṣṇaḥ kṣīraṃ duhrate gāvo asya vanriṃ vasānā udakaṃ padāpuḥ |*)

(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-164-7)

In this and similar passages it has been described before that the rays of Āditya rain down water, and that the same rays of Āditya, sucking up water from the earth, hold it again within themselves. Therefore in these rays the female nature and the male nature are mingled. When they bear the embryo in the form of water the female form, and when they pour out the rain the male form, becomes manifest. When it displays the female form it is extremely attractive, and when it displays the male form it is extremely powerful. Its nature cannot be grasped by the merely physical eye. For this the power of obtaining a supernatural vision is absolutely necessary. Therefore the power of seeing is stated by अक्षण्वान् पश्यत् (*akṣaṇvān paśyat*). If the nature of these rays is to be described, they are the cause of all kinds of creation and preservation, and pervade everything by their own nature.

### Printed p. 391
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. .೩ ವ. ೧೭.] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 391 (as supplied).*

अथादित्य उदयन्यत्पाचीं दिशं प्रविशति तेन प्राच्यान्प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते । यद्दक्षिणां यत्पतीचीं यदुदीचीं यदधो यदूर्ध्वं यदंतरा दिशो यत्सर्वं प्रकाशयति तेन सर्वान् प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते । (*athāditya udayanyatpācīṃ diśaṃ praviśati tena prācyānprāṇānraśmiṣu saṃnidhatte | yaddakṣiṇāṃ yatpatīcīṃ yadudīcīṃ yadadho yadūrdhvaṃ yadaṃtarā diśo yatsarvaṃ prakāśayati tena sarvān prāṇānraśmiṣu saṃnidhatte |*)

(Praśna U. 1-6)

These rays of Āditya spread to the various directions and the intermediate directions of the universe, illumine everything, and gather all the things of the universe within themselves. Having hidden everything in his own womb, Āditya himself is the one who has all forms.

विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपंतं । सहस्ररश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानामुदयत्येष सूर्यः ॥ (*viśvarūpaṃ hariṇaṃ jātavedasaṃ parāyaṇaṃ jyotirekaṃ tapaṃtaṃ | sahasraraśmiḥ śatadhā vartamānaḥ prāṇaḥ prajānāmudayatyeṣa sūryaḥ ‖*)

(Praśna 1-8)

In descriptions such as: "Āditya, who has all forms, who is all-knowing, the final refuge, the one single light for the whole world, who has a thousand rays, rises as the one single life-breath of all creatures", he is for the world both father and mother, he who bears the world in the form of an embryo and creates the world that is in the womb. Explaining this very thing from the spiritual point of view, Sāyaṇa says:

याः इदानीं स्त्रियः सतीः स्त्रीत्वं प्राप्ता आहुर्लौकिकाः तान् उ तानेव मे मह्यं पुंसः पुरुषा नाहुः प्रतिपादयंति तत्त्वज्ञाः ॥ (*yāḥ idānīṃ striyaḥ satīḥ strītvaṃ prāptā āhurlaukikāḥ tān u tāneva me mahyaṃ puṃsaḥ puruṣā nāhuḥ pratipādayaṃti tattvajñāḥ ‖*) *[as supplied: पुरुषा नाहुः (*puruṣā nāhuḥ*) stands split in two words here; the bhāṣya on p. 389 has पुरुषानाहुः (*puruṣānāhuḥ*) as one word]*

He has explained the meaning thus: what the worldly people call the female-formed principle of the ray, that very thing the knowers of the truth call male-formed.

कथमन्यस्य अन्यभावः उच्यते । एकस्यॆव निरस्तसमस्तोपाधिकस्य आत्मनस्तद्देहावस्थानमात्रेण तत्तद्व्यपदेशोपसत्तेः । (*kathamanyasya anyabhāvaḥ ucyate | ekasyèva nirastasamastopādhikasya ātmanastaddehāvasthānamātreṇa tattadvyapadeśopasatteḥ |*) *[as supplied: the last word reads upasatteḥ here, against upapatteḥ in the bhāṣya on p. 389]* Then, if the objection arises: how can the principle that has the female form be called of male form? He has given the solution that there is no room for such objections about the greatness of this primal principle, which is free of all limiting adjuncts and has the power of assuming every form by mere resolve. The description of how, being non-dual, and afterwards, having desired creation, it assumed the female form by the mere power of its will, and itself, taking both the female and the male forms, brought about the creation of the world, is given in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad in this manner:

आत्मैवेदमग्र आसीत्पुरुषविधः सोऽनुवीक्ष्य नान्यदात्मनः। स वै नैवे रेमे तस्मादेकाकी न रमते स द्वितीयमैच्छत् । स हैतावानास यथा स्त्रीपु- (*ātmaivedamagra āsītpuruṣavidhaḥ so 'nuvīkṣya nānyadātmanaḥ| sa vai naive reme tasmādekākī na ramate sa dvitīyamaicchat | sa haitāvānāsa yathā strīpu-*) *(the quotation is cut by the page end, at a hyphenated word, and continues on p. 392)*

### Printed p. 392
*Running head: 392 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧ ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

मांसौ संपरिष्वक्तौ स इममेवात्मानं द्वेधापातयत्ततः पतिश्च पत्नि चाभवतां तस्मादिदमर्धबृगलमिव स्व इति ह स्माह याज्ञवल्क्यस्तस्मादयमाकाशः स्त्रिया पूरैत एव तां समभवत्ततो मनुष्या अजायंत ॥ (*māṃsau saṃpariṣvaktau sa imamevātmānaṃ dvedhāpātayattataḥ patiśca patni cābhavatāṃ tasmādidamardhabṛgalamiva sva iti ha smāha yājñavalkyastasmādayamākāśaḥ striyā pūraita eva tāṃ samabhavattato manuṣyā ajāyaṃta ‖*)

(Bṛ U. 1-4-1 to 3) *[as supplied: "ಬೃ ಉ." without the full stop]*

In the beginning this universal Self was non-dual, and saw no second thing other than himself. Because of that he had no delight, and desired to create a second thing that would give him delight. Afterwards he grew as extended as a woman and a man become when they are embraced together; at once, taking a dual form, he became husband and wife. "Therefore this whole space is pervaded by the female form. When the universal Self united with this female form, the creation of human beings and the rest took place," Yājñavalkya has described. In the same way, describing the creation of other creatures also, he has given the details of how, taking the forms of cow, bull and the like, he created cattle and the rest. In the same way in the Praśna Upaniṣad also the details of how the universal Self, assuming both the female and the male forms, carried on the creation of the world are stated thus:

प्रजाकामो वै प्रजापतिः स तपोऽतप्यत स तपस्तप्त्वा स मिथुनमुत्पादयते रयिं च प्राणं चेत्येत् मे बहुधा प्रजाः करिष्यत इति । (*prajākāmo vai prajāpatiḥ sa tapo 'tapyata sa tapastaptvā sa mithunamutpādayate rayiṃ ca prāṇaṃ cetyet me bahudhā prajāḥ kariṣyata iti |*) *[as supplied: चेत्येत् मे (*cetyet me*) as printed]*

(Praśna 1-4)

Prajāpati, desiring offspring, by the greatness of his austerity created Nature in the female form (रयिं (*rayiṃ*)) and the life-breath in the male form (प्राणं (*prāṇaṃ*)), and from that pair brought about the increase of creatures. Having begun thus, it is then explained that by the expansion of those original principles the whole universe was transformed into the very forms of rayi and prāṇa. Describing that very nature, in the Praśna Upaniṣad:

मासो वै प्रजापतिः .... .... .... अन्नं वै प्रजापतिस्ततो ह वै तद्रेतस्तस्मादिमाः प्रजाः प्रजायंत इति । तद्ये ह वै तत्प्रजापतिव्रतं चरंति ते मिथुनमुत्पादयंते । तेषामेवैष ब्रह्म लोको येषां तपो बह्मचर्यं येषु त्यं प्रतिष्ठितं । (*māso vai prajāpatiḥ .... .... .... annaṃ vai prajāpatistato ha vai tadretastasmādimāḥ prajāḥ prajāyaṃta iti | tadye ha vai tatprajāpativrataṃ caraṃti te mithunamutpādayaṃte | teṣāmevaiṣa brahma loko yeṣāṃ tapo bahmacaryaṃ yeṣu tyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ |*) *[as supplied: the dots are in the print; त्यं (*tyaṃ*) as printed]*

(Praśna 1-12 to 15)

By sentences of this kind it is described that the primal principle, manifesting itself both in the female form and in the male form, as described in the present Ṛk, became the cause of the creation and other activities of the world. It must be understood that Prajāpati, Āditya and the year are all different names of one and the same principle. Therefore: संवत्सरो वै प्रजापतिः (*saṃvatsaro vai prajāpatiḥ*) ; मासो वै प्रजापतिः । (*māso vai prajāpatiḥ |*) ; अहोरात्रो वै प्रजापति (*ahorātro vai prajāpati*) ; *(the list is cut by the end of the window as supplied and continues in the next window)*

### Printed p. 393
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ನ. ೧೭. ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 393 (as supplied; the printed "ನ." and "ವ." of the Varga are not made uniform).*

[Continuing the Special Topics of the previous Ṛk.]

Beginning with अन्नं वै प्रजापतिः (*annaṃ vai prajāpatiḥ*) (Praśna 1), Prajāpati, who pervades the world, is described. Describing this principle in the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad:

त्वं स्त्री त्वं पुमानसि त्वं कुमार उत ना कुमारी । त्वं जीर्णो दंडेन वंचसि त्वं जातो भवसि विश्वतोमुखः (*tvaṃ strī tvaṃ pumānasi tvaṃ kumāra uta nā kumārī | tvaṃ jīrṇo daṃḍena vaṃcasi tvaṃ jāto bhavasi viśvatomukhaḥ*)
(Śve. U. 4-3)

"You, whose face is turned to every side, are praised as being of female form and of male form, and likewise as having the form of a boy and a girl."

अक्षण्वान् पश्यत्—ज्ञानदृष्टुपेतः कश्चिन्महान् पश्यति (*akṣaṇvān paśyat—jñānadṛṣṭupetaḥ kaścinmahān paśyati*): only a great soul endowed with the sight of knowledge can see; others cannot. After giving an example for this, the occasion on which Indra and the others who knew this principle, female and male in form, are praised is told in the Kena Upaniṣad in this manner, and this beautiful secret is made known:

अथेंद्रमब्रुवन्मघवन्नेतद्विजानीहि किमेतद्यक्षमिति तथेति तदभ्यद्रवत्तस्मात्तिरोदधे । सतस्मिन्नेवाकाशेस्त्रियमाजगाम बहुशोभमानामुमाग्ं हैमवतीं तागां होवाच किमेतद्यक्षमिति (*atheṃdramabruvanmaghavannetadvijānīhi kimetadyakṣamiti tatheti tadabhyadravattasmāttirodadhe | satasminnevākāśestriyamājagāma bahuśobhamānāmumāgṃ haimavatīṃ tāgāṃ hovāca kimetadyakṣamiti*)
(केस. ३-१८, १२ (*kesa. 3-18, 12*)) *[as supplied: the reference abbreviation "ಕೇಸ." and the numbers are kept as printed.]*

The gods all told Indra to find out the nature of this Yakṣa, and Indra went near it. [This occasion, at which Agni and the others did not fully understand its nature, and even the gods were unable to make its secret known, was described earlier among the Special Topics of the 5th Ṛk of the Sūkta now in hand.] Then Indra saw in the atmosphere a female figure, exceedingly charming and radiant. When he asked who this was,

सा ब्रह्मेति होवाच ब्रह्मणो वा एतद्विजये महीयध्वमिति (*sā brahmeti hovāca brahmaṇo vā etadvijaye mahīyadhvamiti*)
(Kena. 4-1)

it was told that this female figure is Brahman, and that the victory of the gods and the rest is through her greatness; and afterwards, praising the greatness of Indra and the others who knew that beautiful Brahman-principle, and telling that it is not possible for other ordinary persons,

तस्माद्वा एते देवा अतितरामिवान्वान्यादग्निर्वायुरिंद्रस्ते ह्येनन्ने दिष्ठं पस्पृशुस्ते ह्येनत्प्रथमो विदांचकार ब्रह्मेति (*tasmādvā ete devā atitarāmivānvānyādagnirvāyuriṃdraste hyenanne diṣṭhaṃ paspṛśuste hyenatprathamo vidāṃcakāra brahmeti*)
(Praśna. 4-2) *[as supplied: the reference is printed so; it is not changed.]*

### Printed p. 394
*Running head: 394 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied; "ಆ." as printed).*

Because these gods, approaching this primal principle to learn its nature, knew its greatness before the others, Agni, Indra and Vāyu are superior to the other gods. Even among Agni, Vāyu and Indra, Indra is the greatest because he knew this Brahman-principle. Thus, praising greatly the power of knowing its secret, it is told that this is possible only for those who have supernatural sight of knowledge. One without this knowledge of the Self is merely blind.

अंधं तमः प्रविशंति येऽविद्यामुपासते । ततो भूय इव ते तमो य उ विद्यायां रताः (*aṃdhaṃ tamaḥ praviśaṃti ye 'vidyāmupāsate | tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u vidyāyāṃ ratāḥ*)
(Bṛ. U. 4-4-10)

Those who cannot know the nature of this Supreme Self and rely only on ignorance enter the cave of darkness;

आनंदा नाम ते लोका अंधेन तमसा वृताः । तांस्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छंत्यविद्वांसोऽबुधो जनाः (*ānaṃdā nāma te lokā aṃdhena tamasā vṛtāḥ | tāṃste pretyābhigacchaṃtyavidvāṃso 'budho janāḥ*)
[Bṛ. U. 4-4-11]

For those who have entered this cave of the form of darkness there is no kind of joy whatever. Even after death the same fate is obtained by them. Thus the place that falls to the ignorant who do not know the secret of this universal principle is described. Such persons are described as "blind" in the Ṛk now in hand also. This description is there to show the necessity of the eye of knowledge for knowing this principle, which is of female and male form.

To show that one who knows such a great principle becomes greater than all: यस्ता विजानात्स पितुष्टितासत् (*yastā vijānātsa pituṣṭitāsat*) — it is told that such a knower becomes worthy of greater reverence than the father. The same point, praising it, in the Praśna Upaniṣad:

ते तमर्चयंतस्त्वं हि नः पिता योऽस्माकमविद्यायाः परं पारं तारयसीति । नमः परम ऋषिभ्यो नमः परमयषिभ्यः (*te tamarcayaṃtastvaṃ hi naḥ pitā yo 'smākamavidyāyāḥ paraṃ pāraṃ tārayasīti | namaḥ parama ṛṣibhyo namaḥ paramayaṣibhyaḥ*)
(Praśna. U. 6-8) *[as supplied: परमयषिभ्यः (*paramayaṣibhyaḥ*) as printed.]*

Then all those who had received instruction from Pippalāda, worshipping him, offer their devotion thus: "You are our father. You have taught us knowledge, taken us across the ocean of ignorance and brought us to the shore of knowledge; therefore you are worthy of worship like a father." Having told this, reverence is paid to the supreme sages who are knowers. The meaning is: only one who is a Ṛṣi is a knower; all knowers are Ṛṣis. The same is told in the Ṛk now in hand by the sentence कविर्यः पुत्रः स इमा चिकेत (*kaviryaḥ putraḥ sa imā ciketa*).

### Printed p. 395
*Running head: [ಅ ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೭. ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 395 (as supplied).*

To show that such a knower is the father even of fathers, that is, is worthy of reverence, Sāyaṇa has given an example from the Tāṇḍaka-brāhmaṇa.

शिशुर्वा अंगिरसो मंत्रकृतां मंत्रकृदासीत् स पित्थन् पुत्रका इत्यामंत्रयत (*śiśurvā aṃgiraso maṃtrakṛtāṃ maṃtrakṛdāsīt sa pitthan putrakā ityāmaṃtrayata*)
(शां. ब्रा, १३-३-२४ (*śāṃ. brā, 13-3-24*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation शां. ब्रा (*śāṃ. brā*) and the numbers are kept as printed.]*

The very young Āṅgirasa was a mantra-maker greater than the other mantra-makers. He used to address even the fathers as "sons". Then,

ते देवानपृच्छंत ते देवा अब्रुवन्नेष वाव पिता यो मंत्रकृत् (*te devānapṛcchaṃta te devā abruvanneṣa vāva pitā yo maṃtrakṛt*)

those fathers approached the gods and asked whether this was right; then the gods gave the answer that, since he is a true mantra-maker, he alone is worthy of reverence like a father. This occasion is cited. Explaining this same mantra in the Pariśiṣṭa of the Nirukta:

स्त्रिय एवैताः शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगंधहारिण्यस्ता अमुं पुंशब्देन निराहारः प्राण इति पश्यन् कष्टान्नविजानात्यंधः कविर्यः पुत्रः स इमा जानाति , यः स इमा जानाति स पितुष्पितासदित्यात्मगतिमाचष्टे (*striya evaitāḥ śabdasparśarūparasagaṃdhahāriṇyastā amuṃ puṃśabdena nirāhāraḥ prāṇa iti paśyan kaṣṭānnavijānātyaṃdhaḥ kaviryaḥ putraḥ sa imā jānāti , yaḥ sa imā jānāti sa pituṣpitāsadityātmagatimācaṣṭe*)
(Ni. 14-20)

— thus it is explained. Its meaning too is the same as said above.

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammatical procedure)*

Grammar (transcribed, not explained):

सतीः (*satīḥ*) — by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) [the sūtra is quoted in the print with a following hyphen], when jas follows, the lengthening by the preceding similar letter comes.

पश्यत् (*paśyat*) — the root दृशिर् प्रेक्षणे (*dṛśir prekṣaṇe*); the suffix tip in the third person singular of leṭ; by इतश्चलोपः (*itaścalopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97) the letter i is dropped; by पाघ्राध्मा (*pāghrādhmā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-28) the substitute paśya. Because it stands at the beginning of the pāda, the nighāta accent does not come; the root accent remains.

अक्षण्वान् (*akṣaṇvān*) — by अक्षि अस्य अस्ति इति छंदस्यपि दृश्यते (*akṣi asya asti iti chaṃdasyapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-76) the substitute ava, even though no suffix beginning with a vowel follows. When matup follows it, it has the pada-designation, hence loss of n. By अनोनुट् (*anonuṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-2-16) the augment nuṭ to matup. By the sūtra अट् कुप्पाज् (*aṭ kuppāj*) the retroflexion of it. By हस्वनुड्भ्यां मतुप् (*hasvanuḍbhyāṃ matup*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-176) matup becomes udātta.

### Printed p. 396
*Running head: 396 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೭೬೦] (as supplied: the Sūkta number is printed "೭೬೦" here, although the neighbouring heads have 164; kept as printed).*

Grammar (continued, transcribed, not explained):

चेतत् (*cetat*) — the root चिती संज्ञाने (*citī saṃjñāne*); when tip of the third person singular of leṭ comes, by इतश्च लोपः (*itaśca lopaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-97) the loss of its letter i. By the sūtra लेटोऽडाट् (*leṭo 'ḍāṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-94) the augment aḍ. By बहुलं छंदसि (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasi*) the loss of the vikaraṇa. Guṇa of the short penultimate vowel of the root, caused by the suffix. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*) — the root अद भक्षणे (*ada bhakṣaṇe*). By अदेर्नुम् धौच (*adernum dhauca*) (U. Sū. 4-645) asun, the augment num, and the substitute of dha. The form becomes अंधः (*aṃdhaḥ*).

चिकेत (*ciketa*) — the root कित ज्ञाने (*kita jñāne*). In the Vedic manner liṭ in the present sense. A form ending as the third person singular. Because it stands after an atiṅanta, the nighāta accent comes.

विजानात् (*vijānāt*) — the root ज्ञा अवबोधने (*jñā avabodhane*). Leṭ, third person singular, tip, loss of i. The augment aḍ to it. The vikaraṇa śnā. By ज्ञाजनोर्जा (*jñājanorjā*) (Pā. Sū. 7-3-79) the substitute jā for the root. By यद्वृत्तान्वित्यम् (*yadvṛttānvityam*) the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes, so the accent of the vikaraṇa remains. By तिजिचोदात्तवति (*tijicodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the anudātta accent comes to the gati (vi).

असत् (*asat*) — the root अस भुवि (*asa bhuvi*). As before, a form ending as leṭ third person singular. ॥ : ६ ॥ (*‖ : 6 ‖*) *[as supplied: the closing mark is printed "॥ : ೬ ॥"; no number is given here.]*

*[Label as supplied: garbled "ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯದಲಿ" before the heading, repaired by the script to Saṃhitā-pāṭha.]*

> सा क॒द्रीची॒ कं स्वि॒दर्धं॒ परा॑गा॒त्त्व॑ स्वित्तूते न॒हि यू॒थे॒

**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> अत्राग्नौ हूयमानाहुतिर्गॊरूपेण स्तूयते । गौर्गोरूपा गमनशीलैषाहुतिसंघेन पोष्यं वत्सं वत्सस्थानीयमग्निमवोऽवस्तादधोदेशे परेण पदा
> पादद्वयेन स्वावयवेनाकृष्य बिभ्रती धारयंती तथा परः परस्तादुपरिदेश एनानेनावरेण च पदा पादद्वयेनाकृष्य तमेव वत्सं भिभ्रत्युदस्थात् । सूर्यं प्रत्युतिष्ठति । अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिः सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते । मनु. ३-७६ । इति स्मृतेः ।
> अथैवं कृतवती साहुतिः कद्रीची क्व गतेत्यनिश्चयगमना । आदित्यं प्राप्तवतीत्यर्थः ।
> किं स्वित् कं फलभाजं पुरुषं प्रत्यर्धमर्धमार्गमागत्य । यद्वा । अर्धमृद्धं ।
> परागात् । परागच्छति । आगत्य च क्व स्वित्तूते । कुत्र प्रदेशे फलमुत्पादयति । नहीतरगोवदियं यूथेऽंतः सजातीयगोमध्यॆ सूते । साधारण्येन यत्रक्वचिन्न
> सूते अपि तु कस्मिंश्चिदनुष्टातरि । आतः स महान् को नु खल्विति । यद्वा । आदित्यरश्मीसमूह एव गोरूपेण स्तूयते । गौरुक्तलक्षणा रश्मिरूपा गौर्वत्वं वत्सवद्रक्षणेयं यजमानमुक्तक्रमेण बिभ्रत्युदस्थात् । अथ तथा कृत्वा सा कद्रीच्यदृश्यगमना सती कं स्विदर्धमृद्धमर्धस्थानभाजं ना कं स्वित्पुरुषमादित्यं परागात् ।
> अप्रतिनिवृत्ता गता । तं नयंत्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः । मुं उ. १-२-५ । इति श्रुतेः । तथा कृत्वा च क्व स्वित्तूते। कस्मिन्निंद्रादिलोके
> जनयति । न सर्वत्र । शिष्टं समानं ॥
*Gist:* The offering made in the fire is praised in the form of a cow, which carries Agni as her calf upward to the Sun; where it ends is uncertain, as the Ṛk asks.

*[Label as supplied: garbled "ಪ್ರಸಿಪದಾರ್ಥ", repaired by the script to Pratipadārtha.]*
**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
गौ: (*gau:*)—this moving offering; वत्सं (*vatsaṃ*)—Agni who is in the form of the calf; अवः (*avaḥ*)—in her lower region; परेण पदा (*pareṇa padā*)—with her forefeet; बिभ्रती (*bibhratī*)—holding (and likewise); परः (*paraḥ*)—in the upper part; एना अवरेण (*enā avareṇa*)—with these hind feet (holding the same Agni, the calf); उदस्थात् (*udasthāt*)—rises (climbs) towards the Sun; सा (*sā*)—that cow of the form of the offering; कद्रीची (*kadrīcī*)—where did she go?; कं स्वित् (*kaṃ svit*)—towards which man; अर्धं (*ardhaṃ*)—half-way, or for producing prosperity (wealth) for him; परागात् (*parāgāt*)—turned back?; क्व स्वित् (*kva svit*)—in which place; सूते (*sūte*)—does she bring forth fruit? (pour it out); यूथे अंतः (*yūthe aṃtaḥ*)—amidst the herd of her own cattle; न हि (*na hi*)—certainly she does not pour it out.

*[Label as supplied: "॥ ಭವಾರ್ಥ ॥", repaired by the script to Bhāvārtha.]*
**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
This offering in the form of a cow holds Agni, who is in the form of the calf, in her lower region with her forefeet and in the upper part with her hind feet, and rises towards the Sun. Where did that cow of the form of the offering go? Towards which man, for him (the sentence continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 398
*Running head: 398 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

… did she turn back from half the way, to produce wealth and offspring? In which place does she bring forth fruit? This cannot be told exactly. But certainly she does not pour it out amidst the herd of her own cattle.

**Printed English**
The cow, holding her calf underneath with her fore-feet, and then above with her hind-feet, has risen up: whither is she gone? to whom has she turned back when half-way? where does she bear young? it is not amidst the herd.

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
The offering made in the fire is praised here in the form of a cow. Or आदित्यरश्मिसमूह एव गोरूपेण स्तूयते (*ādityaraśmisamūha eva gorūpeṇa stūyate*) — the mass of the Sun's rays itself is praised in the form of a cow: thus Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of purport.

गौ: (*gau:*) — that this word has the meanings earth, cattle and so on, and the derivation of the word in those meanings, was told before. In the present context it is natural that this word means the sacrificial offering or the Sun's ray. The commentator quotes the Smṛti saying अग्नौ प्रास्ताहुतिस्सम्यगादित्यमुपतिष्ठते (*agnau prāstāhutissamyagādityamupatiṣṭhate*) and says that the offering made in the fire too reaches the Sun alone; so the purport is that it is transformed into the form of rays.

आदित्योऽपि गौरुच्यते । सर्वॆऽपि रश्मयो गाव उच्यंते (*ādityo 'pi gaurucyate | sarvè 'pi raśmayo gāva ucyaṃte*)
(Ni. 2-6)

To explain the meaning of this word, the author of the Nirukta, having quoted the Ṛk

ता वां वास्तून्युश्चसि गमध्यै यत्र गावो भूरिशृंगा अयासः । अत्राह तदुरुगायस्य वृष्णः परमं पदमव भाति भूरि (*tā vāṃ vāstūnyuścasi gamadhyai yatra gāvo bhūriśṛṃgā ayāsaḥ | atrāha tadurugāyasya vṛṣṇaḥ paramaṃ padamava bhāti bhūri*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-154-6)

and shown that rays that have many horns and are tireless (आयास (*āyāsa*) as printed: "ಆಯಾಸವೂ") are described, has told that the word is a synonym for the Sun's rays. *[as supplied: the print has "ಬಹುಶೃಂಗಗಳುಳ್ಳವೂ, ಆಯಾಸವೂ ಆದ"; rendered as printed.]*

The relation between such a ray of the Sun, or the sacrificial offering that becomes identical with a ray of the Sun, and the sacrificer, the performer of the sacrifice, is told here. The ray of the Sun is compared to the cow, and the sacrificer to the calf. On the whole, the relation between the Sun and the sacrificer is also told.

### Printed p. 399
*Running head: [ಆ. ೨. ಆ. ೩. ಪ. ೧೭] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 399 (as supplied; "ಆ.", "ಪ." as printed).*

[Continuing the Special Topics of Ṛk 17.]

Here, if the word "go" is explained as referring to the sacrificial offering, then by the descriptions beginning with क्व स्मित् सूते (*kva smit sūte*) *[as supplied: so printed, "ಸ್ಮಿತ್"]* the wealth of food and the like that may accrue to the sacrificer become the aims. Or, if explained as referring to the Sun's rays, then the excellent station of the heavenly world that accrues to the sacrificer becomes the aim. It may be said that both these meanings are specified in the following sentence quoted from the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa.

स उदीक्षते । स्वयंभूरसि श्रेष्ठो रश्मिरित्येष वै श्रेष्ठो रश्मिर्यत्सूर्यस्तस्मादाह स्वयंभूरसि श्रेष्ठो रश्मिरिति वर्चोदा असि वर्चो मे देहीति त्वेवाहं ब्रवीमीति ह स्माह याज्ञवल्क्यस्तद्भैव ब्राह्मणेनेष्टव्यं यद्ब्रह्मवर्चसी स्यादित्युतो ह स्माहौपोदितेय एष नाव मह्यं गा दास्यति गोदा गा मे देहीत्येवं यं कामं कामयते सोऽस्मै कामः समृध्यते (*sa udīkṣate | svayaṃbhūrasi śreṣṭho raśmirityeṣa vai śreṣṭho raśmiryatsūryastasmādāha svayaṃbhūrasi śreṣṭho raśmiriti varcodā asi varco me dehīti tvevāhaṃ bravīmīti ha smāha yājñavalkyastadbhaiva brāhmaṇeneṣṭavyaṃ yadbrahmavarcasī syādityuto ha smāhaupoditeya eṣa nāva mahyaṃ gā dāsyati godā gā me dehītyevaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate*)
(श. बा. १-९-३-१६ (*śa. bā. 1-9-3-16*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation श. बा. (*śa. bā.*) as printed.]*

The Āditya is the most excellent ray, self-existent, the giver of lustre. Therefore he is prayed to, "Give me too lustre." Here there are two kinds of prayer. Yājñavalkya prayed, वर्चोदा असि वर्चोमे देहि (*varcodā asi varcome dehi*), "You are possessed of lustre; give me too lustre." Aupoditeya prayed, एष वाव मह्यं गा दास्यति गोदा गामे देहीत्येवं (*eṣa vāva mahyaṃ gā dāsyati godā gāme dehītyevaṃ*): "This Āditya is a giver of cows; therefore, O Āditya, give me a cow." Therefore, to say that whatever prayer anyone makes, Āditya fulfils that prayer, it is said यं यं कामं कामयते सोऽस्मै कामः समृध्यते (*yaṃ yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate so 'smai kāmaḥ samṛdhyate*). It appears that the sentence explaining the second meaning stated here is quoted in the Śatapatha from the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.

सग्गश्रवा ह सौवर्चनसस्तुमिंजमौपोदितिमुवाच यत्सत्रिणाग्ं होता भूः कामिडामुपाह्वथा इति तामुपाश्व इति होवाच या प्राणेन देवान्साधार व्यानेन मनुष्यानपानेन पितृनिति छिनत्ति सा न छिनत्ती३ इति छिनत्तीति होवाच शरीरं वा अस्यै तदुपाह्वथा इति होवाच गौर्वै (*saggaśravā ha sauvarcanasastumiṃjamaupoditimuvāca yatsatriṇāgṃ hotā bhūḥ kāmiḍāmupāhvathā iti tāmupāśva iti hovāca yā prāṇena devānsādhāra vyānena manuṣyānapānena pitṛniti chinatti sā na chinattī3 iti chinattīti hovāca śarīraṃ vā asyai tadupāhvathā iti hovāca gaurvai*)
(तै. सं. १-७-२-१ (*tai. saṃ. 1-7-2-1*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation तै. सं. (*tai. saṃ.*) as printed.]*

In this Saṃhitā sentence there is a conversation between Saṃśravas and Aupoditi. *[as supplied: the Sanskrit text has सग्गश्रवा (*saggaśravā*), the Kannada "ಸಂಶ್ರವಸ್ಸು"; both kept.]* The Śatapatha says that in it Aupoditi reveals only the earthly wish, as explained above. What is wanted in the present context is that from the cow of the form of the Sun's rays one may obtain worldly wealth also; or

### Printed p. 400
*Running head: 400 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

as Yājñavalkya desired, one may obtain spiritual wealth also; this is clear. Explaining this very point in the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad:

एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् । तं नयंत्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः (*eteṣu yaścarate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ cāhutayo hyādadāyan | taṃ nayaṃtyetāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra devānāṃ patireko 'dhivāsaḥ*)
(पु. उ. १-२-५ (*pu. u. 1-2-5*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation as printed.]*

While these rays are shining, if the offerings suited to each time are made, these rays of the Sun carry that sacrificer to the region where the Supreme Person, the lord of all the gods, dwells. Not only that,

एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूरस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहंति । प्रियां वाचमभिवदंत्योर्चयंत्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः (*ehyehīti tamāhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūrasya raśmibhiryajamānaṃ vahaṃti | priyāṃ vācamabhivadaṃtyorcayaṃtya eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ*)
(मुं. उं. १-२-६ (*muṃ. uṃ. 1-2-6*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation as printed.]*

These excellent offerings, calling the sacrificer lovingly "Come, come", and carrying him with the rays of the Sun to the world of Brahmā, speaking pleasant words, "This is the world of Brahmā, won by your good deeds", and praising him, take him away. Thus the help that the Sun's ray does to the best sacrificer is described. Sāyaṇa, having quoted this sentence of the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad, has shown that the same idea is stated in the Ṛk now in hand.

वत्सं बिभ्रती—वत्सस्थानीयमग्निं धारयंती (*vatsaṃ bibhratī—vatsasthānīyamagniṃ dhārayaṃtī*): holding Agni, who stands in the place of the calf; that is, "holding the Agni who is in the form of the calf".

अज्ज गोजा इत्यब्बाश्च ह्येष गोजाश्च (*ajja gojā ityabbāśca hyeṣa gojāśca*)
(श. ब्रा. ६-७-३-११ (*śa. brā. 6-7-3-11*)) *[as supplied: so printed.]*

Describing thus, it is told that Agni is "go-jā", that is, born of the cow. Here it is described that the mother cow, holding Agni, who is the calf, climbs upward. The epithet and the vocative "calf" has been used in many places, showing the natural quality of Agni.

गर्भो यो अपां गर्भो ननानां गर्भश्च स्थातां गर्भश्वरथां (*garbho yo apāṃ garbho nanānāṃ garbhaśca sthātāṃ garbhaśvarathāṃ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-20-2)

### Printed p. 401
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಆ. ೩. ವ. ೧೭ ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 401 (as supplied).*

क इमं वो निण्यमा चिकेत वत्सो मात्यर्जनयत स्वधाभिः । बह्वीनां गर्भो अपसामुपस्थान्महान्यविनिर्निश्चरति स्वधावान् (*ka imaṃ vo niṇyamā ciketa vatso mātyarjanayata svadhābhiḥ | bahvīnāṃ garbho apasāmupasthānmahānyavinirniścarati svadhāvān*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-95-4)

In such descriptions it is told that Agni in the form of lightning, being as it were an embryo in the waters, which are forms of the Sun's rays, changes into the Sun through the form of the herbs and साग्नि (*sāgni*) *[as supplied: "ಔಷಧಸಾಗ್ನಿರೂಪದಿಂದ" as printed]* and comes out from the atmosphere; and that this same Agni, in the form of the calf, is possessed of svadhā.

अस्मे वत्सं परि षंतं न विंदन्निच्छंतो विश्वे अमृता अमूराः (*asme vatsaṃ pari ṣaṃtaṃ na viṃdannicchaṃto viśve amṛtā amūrāḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-72-2)

In Ṛks of this kind also the relation of Agni, in the form of the calf, to the gods, men and all the others is told. The purport is that the mother cow held such an Agni, in the form of the calf. Thus the meaning that refers to Agni is one kind. Secondly,

गौः उक्तलक्षणा रश्मिरूपा गौः वत्सं वत्सवद्रक्षणीयं यजमानं उक्तक्रमेण बिभ्रती उदस्थात् (*gauḥ uktalakṣaṇā raśmirūpā gauḥ vatsaṃ vatsavadrakṣaṇīyaṃ yajamānaṃ uktakrameṇa bibhratī udasthāt*)

He has said that it may be explained thus: the cow of the form of the ray, taking up the sacrificer who is as it were her calf, flying and becoming invisible, went to the Sun. The explanation of this idea in the sentence beginning कं नयंत्येताः (*kaṃ nayaṃtyetāḥ*) ".... .... .... " *[as supplied: the dots are in the print; कं (*kaṃ*) as printed]* and so on has been given above.

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammatical procedure)*

Grammar (transcribed, not explained):

अवः (*avaḥ*) — the word अवर (*avara*); when the suffix astāti comes after it, by पूर्वाधरावराणाम (*pūrvādharāvarāṇāma*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-39) the substitute av; the substitute ās for the suffix; by the suffix accent it becomes final-acute.

एना (*enā*) — when the instrumental ending follows, by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the lengthening by the preceding similar letter comes.

पदा (*padā*) — by ऊडिदं पदादि (*ūḍidaṃ padādi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-171) the acute accent comes to the instrumental ending.

अस्मात् (*asmāt*) — the root ष्या गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣyā gatinivṛttau*) *[as supplied: "ಷ್ಯಾ" as printed]*; luṅ in the Vedic manner; a form ending as third person singular. Because it stands after an atiṅanta, the nighāta accent comes.

अगात् (*agāt*) — the root इण् गतौ (*iṇ gatau*); as before luṅ, a form ending as third person singular. By इणोगालुजि (*iṇogāluji*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-45) the substitute gā for the root. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

Grammar (continued, transcribed, not explained):

सूते (*sūte*) — the root षूज् प्राणिगर्भविमोचने (*ṣūj prāṇigarbhavimocane*). By धात्वादेः षःसः (*dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥsaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-64) the substitution of s for the initial *[as supplied: the print has "ಅದಾದಿ" before the sūtra]*. A form ending as third person singular of laṭ. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

यूथे (*yūthe*) — the root यु मिश्रणामिश्रणयोः (*yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ*). By तिथपृष्ठगूथयूथप्रोथाः (*tithapṛṣṭhagūthayūthaprothāḥ*) (U. Sū. 2-166) it is irregularly formed ending in the suffix thak. By the suffix accent it becomes final-acute. A form ending in the locative singular. || 17 ||

#### Ṛk 18
*[Label as supplied: garbled "ಸಮಿತಾ", read by hand as Saṃhitā-pāṭha.]*

> क॒वी॒यमा॑नः॒ क इ॒ह प्र वो॑चद्दे॒वं मनः॒ कुतो॒ अधि॒॑

**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> अवः । परेण । पितरं । यः । अस्य । अन्वेव । परः । एना । अवरेण ।
> कवीऽयमानः । कः । इह ! प्र । वोचत् । देवं । मनः । कुतः । अधि । प्रजातं ॥१८॥
*[Label as supplied: garbled "ಸಯಾಭ್ಯಾಂ", read by hand as Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya; the sentence lines were not marked as a block by the script and were wrapped by hand.]*
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> अवोऽवस्तात्स्थितमस्य पितरमेतल्लोकपालकमग्निं परेणादित्येन सह योऽनुवेद अनुक्रमेण जानाति तथा परः परस्तात्स्थितमादित्यमस्य पितरं पालकं । सोऽपीममेव लोकं वृष्टादिना पालयति । तादृशमादित्यमेनानेनावरेणाग्नि ना सह
> योऽनुवेद अग्न्यादित्यौ व्यतिहारेणोपास्त्रे । यद्वा । अभिभूतरजस्तमस्कावुद्बुद्धसत्त्वौ अत एव स्वाधीन मायावेतावेकत्वेन वाधिगच्छति । स तादृशः पुरुषः कवीयमानः कविवदाचरन् क्रांतदर्शित्वमात्मनः ख्यापयन् क इहास्मिल्लिको प्र वोचत् ।
> प्रब्रवीति । किंच देवं द्योतमानं देवविषयमलौकिकं वा मनः कुतः कस्माददृष्टविशेषादध्याधिक्येन प्रजातं । उत्पन्नं । उभयमपि दुर्लभमित्यर्थः ॥
*Gist:* He who knows Agni below with the Sun above, and the Sun with Agni, is a seer; yet who can expound this, and whence did the divine mind arise?

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
अवः (*avaḥ*)—the one who is in the lower part; अस्य पितरं (*asya pitaraṃ*)—Agni, the protector of this earth; परेण (*pareṇa*)—as joined with the Āditya who is in the upper part; (and) परः (*paraḥ*)—in the upper part (the sentence is cut by the page end and continues on the next page)

### Printed p. 403
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೭ ] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 403 (as supplied).*

… the Āditya; अवरेण एन (*avareṇa ena*)—as mixed with this Agni who is in the lower part; यः (*yaḥ*)—who; अनुवेद (*anuveda*)—knows, (such a one); कवीयमानः (*kavīyamānaḥ*)—a seer; कः (*kaḥ*)—who indeed; इह (*iha*)—on this earth; प्र वोचत् (*pra vocat*)—will tell in a special manner? देवं (*devaṃ*)—having supernatural intelligence; मनः (*manaḥ*)—mind; कुतः (*kutaḥ*)—by what special destiny; अधि (*adhi*)—exceedingly; प्रजातं (*prajātaṃ*)—has it been produced?

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Who, being like a seer, can on this earth explain clearly the relation of the Āditya and the others for one who knows Agni, who is in the lower part and is the protector of this earth, as joined with the Āditya who is in the upper part, and also the Āditya who is in the upper part as mixed with this Agni who is below? By what special destiny, and in an exceedingly wonderful manner, has the mind, having intelligence that is supernatural and concerned with the gods, been produced?

**Printed English**
He who knows the protector of this (world) as the the [sic] inferior associ-ated with the superior, and the superior associated with the inferior, he is, as it were, a sage; but who in this world can expound (it)? whence is the divine mind in its supremacy engendered ?

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
The relation between Agni and the Āditya is explained in this Ṛk. This relation can be shown in two ways. Firstly, in the order of the protection of the world, which consists of an exchange between Āditya and Agni, the two are two parts of one principle; secondly, even though both appear in different forms by outward manifestation, it is understood that there is unity of the two. Their positions are told by the words अव (*ava*) and पर (*para*). Here अव (*ava*) may be taken to mean the lower part, and पर (*para*) the atmosphere in the upper part. To take the meaning "superiority and inferiority" is not quite proper. The scholar Wilson, with

He who knows the protector of this world as the inferior associated with the Superior, and the superior associated with the inferior .... .... .... .... ".

has explained the word अव (*ava*) as inferior and the word पर (*para*) as superior. Since Āditya and Agni are two parts of one principle, to say this meaning may be improper. In the Nirukta, while describing the greatness of Agni, no support for this meaning is found.

### Printed p. 404
*Running head: 404 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

मूर्धा भुवो भवति नक्तमग्निस्ततः सूरो जायते प्रातरुद्यन् । मायामू तु यज्ञियानामेतामपो यत्तूर्णिश्चरति प्रजानन् (*mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktamagnistataḥ sūro jāyate prātarudyan | māyāmū tu yajñiyānāmetāmapo yattūrṇiścarati prajānan*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-88-6)

This Vaiśvānara Agni, by his supernatural power the chief of all beings, shining at night in the form of Agni and in the morning in the form of the Sun, carries out his task of protecting the world. Explaining this same point, again in the Nirukta:

स्तोमेन हि दिवि देवासो अग्निमजीजनञ्क्तिभी रोदसिप्रां । तमू अकृण्वन्त्रेधा भुवे कं स ओषधीः पचति विश्वरूपाः (*stomena hi divi devāso agnimajījanañktibhī rodasiprāṃ | tamū akṛṇvantredhā bhuve kaṃ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-28-10)

".... .... .... द्यावापृथिव्यो: पूरणं तमकुर्वंस्त्रेधाभावाय पृथिव्यामंतरिक्षे दिवीति शाकपूणिः (*dyāvāpṛthivyo: pūraṇaṃ tamakurvaṃstredhābhāvāya pṛthivyāmaṃtarikṣe divīti śākapūṇiḥ*)" *[as supplied: the dots are in the print]* The gods caused Agni to blaze, pervading the earth, the atmosphere and the heaven, in order to carry out his duties of protection. By his changes of form he pervades the three worlds. Thus the author of the Nirukta has explained, by quoting Śruti sentences, the idea that the universal principle which shines in forms like the Āditya is one and not different. (Ni. 7-27) The same idea is stated in the Ṛk in hand also. But this kind of unity of Āditya and Agni is not a matter visible to the physical eye. To know it, the quality of being a seer is quite indispensable. Therefore the question is asked, कवीयमानः क इह प्र वोचत् (*kavīyamānaḥ ka iha pra vocat*). This seer knows the two kinds of relation of Āditya and Agni. Firstly, as said above, they are doers of different tasks by exchange in day and night. Sāyaṇa has told this as अग्न्यादित्यौ व्यतिहारेण उपास्ते (*agnyādityau vyatihāreṇa upāste*). Secondly, "or": अभिभूतरजस्तमस्कौ उद्बुद्धसत्त्वा आत एव स्वाधीनमायौ एत् एकत्वेन वा अधिगच्छति (*abhibhūtarajastamaskau udbuddhasattvā āta eva svādhīnamāyau et ekatvena vā adhigacchati*) *[as supplied: the stray word एत् (*et*) at the end of the printed line is kept in the copied passage]*. Overcoming the quality of rajas and the quality of tamas, and manifesting the pure quality of sattva, Āditya and Agni exercise their lordship. It is said that the seer understands that they are different only by their activities, but the original principle of both is one. Explaining the same in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka,

स त्रेधात्मानं व्यकुरुतादित्यं तृतीयं वायुं तृतीयं स एष प्राणस्त्रेधा विहितः (*sa tredhātmānaṃ vyakurutādityaṃ tṛtīyaṃ vāyuṃ tṛtīyaṃ sa eṣa prāṇastredhā vihitaḥ*)
(बृ. ५. १-२-३ (*bṛ. 5. 1-2-3*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation and the "೫." as printed.]*

the original Prajāpati expanded into three parts and manifested himself in the form of cause and effect, and so on; and in the Chāndogya, (the sentence ends here as supplied and continues in the next window).

[Continuing the sentence of the previous window: "… and in the Chāndogya,"]

नागेव ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्थः पादः सोग्निना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च भाति च तपति च कीर्त्या यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद (*nāgeva brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ sogninā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca bhāti ca tapati ca kīrtyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda*)

प्राण एव ब्रह्मणश्चतुर्थः पादः स वायुना ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च........... ब्रह्मवर्चसेन य एवं वेद (*prāṇa eva brahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ sa vāyunā jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca........... brahmavarcasena ya evaṃ veda*)

चक्षुरेव ब्रह्मणश्च तुर्थः पादः स आदित्येन ज्योतिषा भाति च तपति च (*cakṣureva brahmaṇaśca turthaḥ pādaḥ sa ādityena jyotiṣā bhāti ca tapati ca*)
(छा. उ. ३-१८-३ रिंद ६ (*chā. u. 3-18-3 riṃda 6*)) *[as supplied: the dots and the printed "ನಾಗೇವ", "ಚ ತುರ್ಥಃ" are kept in the copied passages.]*

By passages of this kind it is described that the presiding deities of the three worlds, Agni, Vāyu and Āditya, are manifestations of Brahman, and that the speech and the other faculties of a person shine with the help of the deities Agni and the rest, who are parts of this Brahman. And in the Śatapatha-brāhmaṇa:

संवसथाग् स्वर्विदा । समीची उरसा त्मनेति संवसथामेनग् स्वर्विदा समीची उरसा चात्मना चेत्येतदग्निमंतर्भरिष्यंती ज्योतिष्मंत मजस्रमिदित्यसौ वा आदित्य एषोऽग्निः स एष ज्योतिष्मानजस्रस्तमेतेअंतराबिभृतस्तस्मादाह ज्योतिष्मंतमजस्रमिदिति (*saṃvasathāg svarvidā | samīcī urasā tmaneti saṃvasathāmenag svarvidā samīcī urasā cātmanā cetyetadagnimaṃtarbhariṣyaṃtī jyotiṣmaṃta majasramidityasau vā āditya eṣo 'gniḥ sa eṣa jyotiṣmānajasrastameteaṃtarābibhṛtastasmādāha jyotiṣmaṃtamajasramiditi*)
(श. ब्रा. ६-४-१-११ (*śa. brā. 6-4-1-11*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation as printed.]*

"O luminous ones, this shining and immortal Agni is the very Āditya who shines in the world of heaven. Therefore, joining him with the breast and the heart, worship this brilliance" — thus; and likewise:

अग्ने यत्ते दिवि वर्च इति । आदित्यो ना अस्य दिवि वर्चः पृथिव्यामित्ययमग्निः पृथिव्यां यदोषधीष्वप्स्वा यजत्रेति य एवौषधीषु चाप्सु चाग्निस्तमेतदाह येनांतरिक्षमुर्वा ततंथेति वायुः स त्वेषः स भानुरर्णवो नृचक्षा इति महान्स भानुरर्णवो नृचक्षा इत्येतत् (*agne yatte divi varca iti | ādityo nā asya divi varcaḥ pṛthivyāmityayamagniḥ pṛthivyāṃ yadoṣadhīṣvapsvā yajatreti ya evauṣadhīṣu cāpsu cāgnistametadāha yenāṃtarikṣamurvā tataṃtheti vāyuḥ sa tveṣaḥ sa bhānurarṇavo nṛcakṣā iti mahānsa bhānurarṇavo nṛcakṣā ityetat*)
(श. ब्रा. ७-१-१-२३ (*śa. brā. 7-1-1-23*))

"O Agni, your lustre which is in the world of heaven is great; this same lustre shines in the form of Āditya. On the earth it is in the form of the earthly fire; and it shines also in the herbs and in other forms. This same lustre pervades the wind and the rest, and, beholding everything, men and the others, it exists in the form of a great brilliance" — thus it is described. Similarly, describing the nature of this Agni, who is the Self of the universe, in the Kaṭhopaniṣad,

### Printed p. 406
*Running head: 406 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಆ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪.] (as supplied; "ಆ." as printed).*

प्र ते ब्रवीमि तदु मे निबोध स्वर्ग्यमग्निं नचिकेतः प्रजानन् । अनंतलोकाप्तिमथो प्रतिष्ठां विद्वि त्वमेतं निहितं गुहायां (*pra te bravīmi tadu me nibodha svargyamagniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan | anaṃtalokāptimatho pratiṣṭhāṃ vidvi tvametaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ*)
(कठ. १-१-१४ (*kaṭha. 1-1-14*))

"O Naciketas, this heavenly Agni provides the endless world, and is also in the form of the foundation, that is, in the form of the Virāṭ he is the support of the world; and he is pervading the hearts of the worshippers" — thus. Describing the nature of this same Virāṭ Puruṣa, in the Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad,

अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चंद्रसूर्य्य दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च वेदाः । वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतांतरात्मा (*agnirmūrdhā cakṣuṣī caṃdrasūryya diśaḥ śrotre vāgvivṛtāśca vedāḥ | vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvamasya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hyeṣa sarvabhūtāṃtarātmā*)
(मु. उ. २-१-४ (*mu. u. 2-1-4*))

He for whom Agni is the head, the moon and the sun the eyes, the quarters the ears, the wind the life-breath, the universe the heart, is the Virāṭ Puruṣa, famed as the universe.

तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्यां । पुमान् रेतः सिंचति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात् संप्रसूताः (*tasmādagniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ somātparjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyāṃ | pumān retaḥ siṃcati yoṣitāyāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt saṃprasūtāḥ*)
(म: उ. २-१-५ (*ma: u. 2-1-5*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation as printed.]*

For that Supreme Person whose fuel is the Sun, from him that Agni is born; and by that same Sun the world of heaven shines. From Soma produced from the Agni that is the world of heaven, the second Agni, called Parjanya, arises. It is described thus. The same in the Praśna Upaniṣad:

एषोग्निस्तपत्येष सूर‍्य एष पर्जन्यो मघवानेष वायुरेष पृथिवी रयिर्देवः सदसच्चामृतं च यत् (*eṣognistapatyeṣa sūrya eṣa parjanyo maghavāneṣa vāyureṣa pṛthivī rayirdevaḥ sadasaccāmṛtaṃ ca yat*)
(Praśna. 2-5)

This Supreme Self, of the form of the life-breath, burns as Agni; likewise he shines as the Sun; and as Parjanya he pours down rain; as Indra he protects the creatures; and he alone is the formed and the formless, the cause of the origin of the gods and the rest. The identity of Āditya and Agni, told in many Śruti sentences of this kind, is described in the Ṛk now in hand also, in अवः परेण पितरं यो अस्यानुवेद पर एनावरेण (*avaḥ pareṇa pitaraṃ yo asyānuveda para enāvareṇa*) and so on. To know the nature of such a Supreme Self one must be a seer; and his mind too must be far from earthly and perishable things and must have a pure thought. Therefore its characteristic is stated as देवं मनः (*devaṃ manaḥ*). Without such purity the form of this Supreme Self cannot be known. Why? (the answer continues after the next page-head)

### Printed p. 407
*Running head: ೫. ೨. ಆ .೩ ಪ. ೧೭.] ಮುಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 407 (as supplied: the head was not marked by the script and was inserted by hand; "ಮುಗ್ವೇದ" and "೫." as printed).*

न चक्षुषा गृह्यते नापि वाचा नान्यैर्देवैस्तपसा कर्मणा वा । ज्ञानप्रसादेन विशुद्धसत्त्वस्ततस्तु तं पश्यते निष्कलं ध्यायमानः (*na cakṣuṣā gṛhyate nāpi vācā nānyairdevaistapasā karmaṇā vā | jñānaprasādena viśuddhasattvastatastu taṃ paśyate niṣkalaṃ dhyāyamānaḥ*)
(मु:. उ. ३-१-८ (*mu:. u. 3-1-8*)) *[as supplied: the abbreviation as printed.]*

This principle, the original cause, has no form; therefore it cannot be grasped by the eye. It is not to be spoken; therefore it cannot be grasped by speech, nor by the other senses. It becomes possible only through a mind that is far from the contact of the stains, such as passion, arising from the relation between the senses and their objects, and is clear and calm. How the characteristic of a seer who has such a pure mind should be:

संप्राप्य नमृषयो ज्ञानतृप्ताः कृतात्मानो वीतरागाः प्रशांताः । ते सर्वगं सर्वतः प्राप्य धीरा युक्तात्मानः सर्वमेवाविशंति (*saṃprāpya namṛṣayo jñānatṛptāḥ kṛtātmāno vītarāgāḥ praśāṃtāḥ | te sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ prāpya dhīrā yuktātmānaḥ sarvamevāviśaṃti*)
(मुं. उ. ३-२-५ (*muṃ. u. 3-2-5*)) *[as supplied: नमृषयो (*namṛṣayo*) as printed.]*

These sages, who have obtained such a seer's mind, are satisfied with knowledge, have perfected selves, are free from passion, and are very tranquil. Such wise ones, having obtained the all-pervading Self everywhere, with their selves united, become all-pervading. But since such united selves are very rare, it is told that a mind of this kind, concerned with the gods, देवं मनः कुतः अधिजातं (*devaṃ manaḥ kutaḥ adhijātaṃ*) *[as supplied: so printed, "ಅಧಿಜಾತಂ"]*, is possible only through a special destiny.

*[Stray word as supplied: "ವ್ಯಕ್ತಿತ್ವ" in place of the heading of the grammar, kept as a note; the heading was then read as Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.]*

*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammatical procedure)*

Grammar (transcribed, not explained):

अनुवेद (*anuveda*) — the root विद ज्ञाने (*vida jñāne*); in the third person singular of laṭ, for tip by विदोलटोवा (*vidolaṭovā*) (Pā. Sū. 3-4-83) the substitute ṇal; luk for the vikaraṇa; guṇa of the short penultimate vowel of the root. Because of the connection with ya, the nighāta accent does not come. Since ṇal has the mark l, by लिति (*liti*) the acute accent comes before the suffix. By तिजीचोदात्तवति (*tijīcodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the gati (anu) gets the all-grave accent.

एना (*enā*) — by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-39) *[as supplied: the number as printed]*, when the instrumental follows, the lengthening by the preceding similar letter.

कवीयमानः (*kavīyamānaḥ*) — कविरिव आचरन् कवीयमानः (*kaviriva ācaran kavīyamānaḥ*); by कर्तु: क्यज् सलोपश्च (*kartu: kyaj salopaśca*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-11) the suffix kyaj. By अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-137) lengthening of the preceding. After the kyajanta the substitute śānac for laṭ. By आने मुक् (*āne muk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-83) the augment muk to the stem ending in a. By तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the laṭ-sārvadhātuka becomes anudātta, so the kyaj accent remains.

Grammar (continued, transcribed, not explained):

वोचत् (*vocat*) — the root वच परिभाषणे (*vaca paribhāṣaṇe*); luṅ in the Vedic manner in the present sense. When tip follows, by अस्यतिवक्ति (*asyativakti*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-53) the substitute aj for च्चि (*cci*) *[as supplied: so printed]*. By वचउम् (*vacaum*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-20) the augment um to the root. Guṇa. By बहुलं छंदस्यमाज् (*bahulaṃ chaṃdasyamāj*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-75) the augment aḍ does not come. The tiṅanta nighāta accent comes.

प्रजातम् (*prajātam*) — the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); the suffix kta. By गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the gati (pra) keeps its own accent. || 18 ||

#### Ṛk 19
**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**
> ये अ॒र्वांच॒स्ता उ॒ परा॑च आहु॒र्ये परां॑च॒स्ता उ॒॑॑
> अ॒र्वाच॑ आहुः ।
> इंद्र॑श्च॒ या च॒क्रथुः॑ सोम॒ तानि॑ धु॒रा न यु॒क्ता रज॑सो
> वहंति ॥ १९ ॥
**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> ये । अर्वांचः । तान् । ऊं इति । पराचः । आहुः । ये । परांचः । तान् । ऊं
> इति । अर्वाचः । आहुः ।
> इंद्रः । च । या । चक्रथुः । सोम । तानि । धुरा । न । युक्ताः । रजसः । वहंति ॥१९॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> ये सूर्यसोमयोश्चक्रे वर्तमाना रश्मयो ग्रहादयश्च तत्परिभ्रमणवशेनार्वांचोर्वागंचना अधोमुखाः संति ता उ तानेव पराच आहुः । पराङ्मुखांचनानूर्ध्वानाहुः कालविदः । तथा प्रथमं ये परांचः परागंचनाः ता उ
> तानेवार्वाच आहुः । हे सोम त्वमिंद्रः परमेश्वर इरां भूमिं वृष्टा धारक
> आदित्यः । यद्वा । द्वादशादित्यानां मध्य इंद्रोऽप्येकः । निवस्वदिंद्रयुता इत्युक्तत्वादयमपींद्रः । स च युवां या यानि मंडलपरिभ्रमणानि चक्रथुः कृतवंतौ

> *ye sūryasomayoścakre vartamānā raśmayo grahādayaśca tatparibhramaṇavaśenārvāṃcorvāgaṃcanā adhomukhāḥ saṃti tā u tāneva parāca āhuḥ | parāṅmukhāṃcanānūrdhvānāhuḥ kālavidaḥ | tathā prathamaṃ ye parāṃcaḥ parāgaṃcanāḥ tā u*
> *tānevārvāca āhuḥ | he soma tvamiṃdraḥ parameśvara irāṃ bhūmiṃ vṛṣṭā dhāraka*
> *ādityaḥ | yadvā | dvādaśādityānāṃ madhya iṃdro 'pyekaḥ | nivasvadiṃdrayutā ityuktatvādayamapīṃdraḥ | sa ca yuvāṃ yā yāni maṃḍalaparibhramaṇāni cakrathuḥ kṛtavaṃtau*

### Printed p. 409
*Running head: [ಅ. ೨. ಅ. ೩. ವ. ೧೭.] ಋಗ್ವೇದಸಂಹಿತಾ 409 (as supplied).*

[Continuing the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya of Ṛk 19.]
> तानि रजसो रंजनात्मकस्य लोकस्य ॥ कर्मणि षष्ठी ॥ लोकं वहंति । निर्वहंति ।
> तत्र दृष्टांतः । धुरा शकटादौ धुरि युक्ताः संबद्धा अश्वादयो यथा धुरं
> वहंति तद्वत् । यद्वा । एतत्पूर्वार्धे दृष्टांतितं । धुरा युक्ताः । धुरि स्थितं
> चक्रमपि धुर् शब्देनोच्यते । तत्र युक्ताः समर्पिताः पुरुषास्तत्परिभ्रमणवशेनार्वांचोऽपि परांचः परांचोऽत्यर्वांचो भवति तद्वत् ॥
*Gist:* The rays that turn downward are called upward, and the upward ones downward, by the revolution of the wheel; Soma and Indra made orbits that carry the worlds like yoked horses.

**प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)**
अर्वांचः (*arvāṃcaḥ*)—having a downward-turned movement; ये (*ye*)—whichever rays of the Sun's wheel there are; तान् उ (*tān u*)—those same; पराचः (*parācaḥ*)—as having upward-turned positions; आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—(the knowers of time) say; ये (*ye*)—which rays; परांचः (*parāṃcaḥ*) have upward-turned spreadings; तान् उ (*tān u*)—those same; अर्वाचः (*arvācaḥ*)—as downward-going; आहुः (*āhuḥ*)—they say; सोम (*soma*)—O Soma; (you); इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*)—and Indra, together; या (*yā*)—whichever planets and the rest, of the nature of revolution; चक्रथुः (*cakrathuḥ*)—you created; ता (*tā*)—all those; धुरा (*dhurā*)—in the yokes of carts and the like; युक्ताः न (*yuktāḥ na*)—like horses and the rest, harnessed; रजसः (*rajasaḥ*)—the delightful worlds; वहंति (*vahaṃti*)—bear.

**भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)**
Those rays of the Sun's wheel which have a downward-turned movement, those same the knowers of time call as having upward-turned positions. Those rays which have upward-turned spreadings, those same they call downward-going. O Soma, whichever revolving planets and the rest you and Indra together have created, all those too, like horses and the rest harnessed in the yokes of carts and the like, bear the delightful worlds.

**Printed English**
Those which (the sages) have termed descending, they have also termed ascending; and those they have termed ascending, they have also called descending: and those (orbits) which you, Soma and Indra, have made, bear along the worlds like (oxen) yoked to a wan [sic].

**विशेषविषयगळु (Viśeṣaviṣayagaḷu)**
In the Ṛk now in hand also, the very matter described in the previous mantra is stated by other sentences. When this primal principle, by its outward manifestation, revolves in a wheel-like manner, the rays and the planets and the rest that are in the upper part turn to the lower part, and those in the lower part to the upper

### Printed p. 410
*Running head: 410 ಸಾಯಣಭಾಷ್ಯಸಹಿತಾ [ ಮಂ. ೧. ಅ. ೨೨. ಸೂ. ೧೬೪] (as supplied).*

part, by way of exchange, in a cycle. Therefore one and the same object is called in two ways, as having a downward face and as having an upward face.

इंद्रश्च या चक्रथुः सोम (*iṃdraśca yā cakrathuḥ soma*) — it is a well-known matter that these orbs of brilliance, the Āditya and the rest, were created by Indra and by Soma.

इंद्रासोमा वासयथ उषासमुत्सूर्यं नयथो ज्योतिषा सह । उप द्यां स्कंभथुः स्कंभनेनाप्रथतं पृथिवीं मातरं वि (*iṃdrāsomā vāsayatha uṣāsamutsūryaṃ nayatho jyotiṣā saha | upa dyāṃ skaṃbhathuḥ skaṃbhanenāprathataṃ pṛthivīṃ mātaraṃ vi*)
(ऋ. सं. ६-७-२ (*ṛ. saṃ. 6-7-2*)) *[as supplied: the reference as printed.]*

"O Indra and Soma, you created the Dawn by uniting her with splendour and the Sun with brilliance; you set up heaven and earth with a support" — thus they are praised. And further, praising the greatness of Indra,

यदा सूर्यममुं दिवि शुक्रं ज्योतिरधारयः । आदित्ते विश्वा भुवनानि येमिरे (*yadā sūryamamuṃ divi śukraṃ jyotiradhārayaḥ | āditte viśvā bhuvanāni yemire*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-12-30)

इंद्रेण रोचना दिव्ये दृळ्हानि दृढितानि च । सिराणि न पराणुदे (*iṃdreṇa rocanā divye dṛḷhāni dṛḍhitāni ca | sirāṇi na parāṇude*)
(Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-14-9)

When Indra established the orb of brilliance in the atmosphere, all the worlds bowed to Indra in gratitude. Among the masses of brilliance of the atmosphere established by him, none falls from its place, and they carry out their duties continuously. The point described in passages of this kind is told here.

*[Label as supplied: "ಸ್ಮರಣಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾ", repaired by the script to Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā.]*
*Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā (grammatical procedure)*

Grammar (transcribed, not explained):

चक्रथुः (*cakrathuḥ*) — डुकृञ् करणे (*ḍukṛñ karaṇe*); the root; liṭ, a form ending as second person dual. By यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् (*yadvṛttānnityam*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66) the prohibition of the nighāta accent comes, so the initial-acute accent of the suffix comes.

धुरा (*dhurā*) — by सुपां सुलुक् (*supāṃ suluk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-39) the substitute ā for the locative singular.

रजसः (*rajasaḥ*) — the root रंज रागे (*raṃja rāge*); by भूरंजिभ्यां कित् (*bhūraṃjibhyāṃ kit*) (U. Sū. 4-656) the suffix asun. Because it has the mark k, by अनिदितां हललु (*aniditāṃ halalu*) *[as supplied: so printed]* the loss of the nasal of the penultimate. The genitive stands in the sense of the object.

#### Ṛk 20
**॥ संहितापाठः ॥**
> द्वा सु॑प॒र्णा स॒युजा॒ सखा॑या समा॒नं वृ॒क्षं परि॑षस्वजाते ।
> तयो॑र॒न्यः पिप्प॑लं स्वा॒द्वत्त्यन॑श्नन्न॒न्नो अ॒भि चा॑कशीति ॥ २० ॥
**॥ पदपाठः ॥**
> द्वा । सुपर्णा । सयुजा । सखाया । समानं । वृक्षं । परि । सस्वजाते इति ।
> तयोः । अन्यः । पिप्पलं । स्वादु । अत्ति । अनश्नन् । अन्यः । अभि । चाकशीति ॥ २० ॥
**॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥**
> अत्र लौकिकपक्षिद्वयद्रष्टांतेन जीवपरमात्मानौ स्तूयेते । यथा लोके
> दौ सुपर्णौ सुपतन् शोभनगमनौ सयुजा समानयोगौ सखाया समानख्यान्
> समानं वृक्षं परि षस्वजाते एकमेव वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते आश्रयतः तयोरन्य एकः
> पिप्पलं पक्वं स्वादुतरमत्ति अपरोऽनश्वन्नभि चाकशीति अभिपश्यति तद्वत् दौ सुपर्णस्थानीयौ क्षेत्रज्ञ परमात्मानौ सयुजा समानयोगौ । योगो नाम संबंधः स च
> तादात्मलक्षणः स एवात्मा जीवात्मनः स्वरूपं यस्य परमात्मन स तदात्मा । एवमन्यस्यापि स एवात्मा परमात्मनः स्वरूपं यस्य जीवात्मनः । एवमेकस्वरूपावित्यर्थः ।
> अनेन भास्कर मतानुसारिणोऽतिरेकिनान्नो जीवात्मा परमात्मनो नान्यः सच
> परमात्मा जीवादन्यो नानाजीवाश्रयणादिति मतं निरस्तं भवति । ननु संबंधो
> द्विष्यः स च दक्षिणॊरेव भेदमपेक्षते अतः कथमैकात्ममिति न औपाधिकभेदं वास्तवा
> भेदं चापेक्ष प्रवृत्तः। आत एव सखायौ समानख्यान् नान्यख्यान्। नन्नेकस्य यादृशं
> ख्यानं तादृशमेवान्यस्यॆति व्युत्पत्ता भेदः स्पुटं प्रतिभाति कथं तादात्ममुच्यत
> इति न वक्तव्यं ! नात्र परस्परं दृष्टांतदार्ष्टांतिकभावः । अपि तु यस्य यादृशं
> ख्यानं स्पुरणं परमात्मनः तदेव ज्ञानमितरस्यापि जीवात्मन इति सखायावित्युच्यते ।
> एकरूपप्रकाशावित्यर्थः । आत उपपन्नमैकात्मं । अनेन वास्तवभेदोऽपि निरस्तः ।
> समानं वृक्षं परि षस्वजाते इत्यत्र यथाश्रयांताराभावादुभयोरेकाश्रयत्व-
*Gist:* By the example of two birds on one tree, the individual self and the Supreme Self are praised; the commentary continues and is cut at the end of the window.
